DCR module realisations stable: Surya Ghar about 24-24.5 cents/W, KUSUM about 22 cents/W, C&I slightly lower; no change expected over 12-15 months as orders are booked.
Cell pricing (mono-PERC) stable; long-term cell contracts have variable wafer, silver and FX pass-through. Most orders are USD-linked.

US minimum import price proposal on cells and modules cited as making US manufacturing attractive; Europe tenders in Italy and France and expected in Germany.

qa_highlights.question: How much DC overloading should be assumed for PM KUSUM, and what is the demand outlook for the next nine months?
qa_highlights.answer: Blended overloading of 1.2-1.25x (KUSUM B at 1.0x, KUSUM C at 1.3-1.5x). Management expects about 1.2-1.3 GW per quarter of rooftop and 6-8 GW AC (possibly more than 8 GW) of KUSUM over nine months; total about 23-24 GW DC over nine months.

qa_highlights.question: Why sell cells rather than convert them into DCR modules and capture the margin?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said legacy cell contracts signed earlier must be honoured; as the 7 GW cell line starts, DCR module output will rise and cell sales will fall. Q1 module orders were mostly for modules.

qa_highlights.question: Will C&I demand be deferred by the ALMM extension, and is DCR capacity blocked?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said C&I clients are already blocking capacity for FY28 and are not deferring; DCR is sold out with FY28 sales underway.

qa_highlights.question: Is 29-30% EBITDA margin sustainable over the next two to three years?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it targets maintaining 29-30% (plus or minus 100-150 bps), citing 7 GW cell line, transformer scale-up and backward integration into ingot-wafer.

qa_highlights.question: What is the transformer revenue ramp for FY27 and FY28?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects the initial ramp to be slightly below the analyst's INR600-700 crore FY27 estimate; business to treble over three years versus last year's INR400 crores; margins targeted slightly above the historical 15% EBITDA / 8-10% PAT cycle average.

qa_highlights.question: Why did other expenses and employee costs jump sharply?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed this to advance hiring for Seetharampur and Naidupeta, power costs of Seetharampur built up before July ramp-up, and corporate hiring tied to acquisitions. Per-GW manpower at Seetharampur is expected about 40% lower.

risks_watch: Execution timing on the 7 GW TOPCon cell line: trial runs slated for later in August, first revenue targeted for September, and 50-60% utilisation by November; at least 70% targeted by the March quarter.

Non-DCR module pricing and profitability: management said non-DCR business is not profitable currently against over 200 GW of module capacity versus about 30 GW of non-DCR demand, with slight price improvement expected for the coming quarter.

Transformer ramp risk: management said FY27 revenue will be slightly below the analyst's INR600-700 crore estimate due to certification and type-testing lead times; watch transformer revenue against the 16.25 GVA FY28 capacity target.

Depreciation step-up to about INR240-250 crores per quarter in Q3 and Q4 FY27, and other expenses and employee costs rising sharply ahead of capacity ramp; watch whether the 29-30% EBITDA margin guidance (plus or minus 100-150 bps) holds.

BESS technology partner expected in 2-3 months, with management going slow pending government guidelines on non-tariff barrier rules; US cell JV output expected in 24-30 months; Europe export office being opened.

DCR is, we are sold out. So, you know, we are selling now only for FY28 now.
As we speak, I can confirm that there is no concrete plan to raise any primary capital in the near future.
So, in general, we have said in the past that we want to maintain a business split of 50-50 for our cell production: 50% to be sold externally and 50% to be consumed internally.

544238|2026-09.headline: Premier Energies Q2 FY27 revenue rose 38.2% YoY to INR2,656 crore, with PAT up 30.8% to INR462 crore and a INR16,260 crore order book.
544238|2026-09.overview: Consolidated revenue grew 38.2% YoY to INR2,656 crore, EBITDA rose 17.8% to INR760 crore and PAT rose 30.8% to INR462 crore. Solar manufacturing EBITDA margin was 29.3% and PAT margin 17.9%, with PAT margin moderating on higher depreciation and lower other income. Management flagged a 7 GW TOPCon cell line at Naidupeta as commissioned with commercial production expected later in November, and a fresh INR4,001 crore cell and module order intake. Working capital rose on raw material inventory, which management called temporary.

financial_highlights.change: moderated slightly on higher depreciation and lower other income
new cell and module order wins of INR4,001 crore in quarter

segments.name: Solar cells and modules
segments.commentary: Order book split is about 48% cells and 48% modules, with about 20% of the module book being DCR; 68-70% of the total book is domestic DCR manufacturing. Non-DCR is 25-30% of the book at single-digit EBITDA margins and realisations above INR12.75/W.

segments.name: Transformers (new capacity)
segments.commentary: 4 GVA of new capacity is being commissioned and type testing is complete for all power transformer ranges except EHV. Management says normalised margin is about 15%, after 12% in Q2 versus about 22% in the prior quarter.

segments.name: Transcon (subsidiary)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR122 crore, PAT INR18 crore, EBITDA margin 15% and PAT margin 8% in the quarter.

segments.name: Battery energy storage (BESS)
segments.commentary: Operationalisation expected in Q2 2027 through cell-to-pack and pack-to-container lines, in partnership with German firm RCT. LFP cell supply is not yet tied up; sourcing is from Chinese tier-1 makers.

guidance_outlook: Naidupeta 7 GW cell line: CUF ramp to 25-30% in December and about 70% by end-March 2027.
Capex for the next two quarters moderates to about INR700 crore, implying about INR2,400 crore for FY27.
Management expects a significant step-up in financial performance as Naidupeta and Seetharampur volumes ramp up over the next few quarters.
Annual industry capacity addition expected to reach about 50 GW AC this year, above last year.
Ingot-wafer Phase 1 targeted for December 2027 and Phase 2 (additional 5 GW, total about 10 GW) for June 2028, subject to government timing.
Transformer revenue expected to more than treble over three years, with capacity ramping to 80-90% over three years.
Order book of about 10 GW to execute over 12-14 months.
US cell factory with JV partner: site finalisation targeted in 12-18 months.
Depreciation for FY27 about INR600 crore, per management.
capex_capacity: 7 GW TOPCon cell line at Naidupeta commissioned; trial runs under way; commercial production expected later in November 2026. ALMM enrolment inspection by NISE expected in the third week of November.
Ingot-wafer project on 169 acres at Naidupeta, with land, water, and power approvals in place; wafer vendor deposit made and agreements under Chinese export-control registration.
Inventory build-up is largely raw material, linked to Seetharampur and Naidupeta ramp-up plus shipping congestion; management expects normalisation by March 2027 quarter.
Chinese draft export control on high-end equipment: cell line machinery already imported; ingot-wafer equipment sourcing dependent on clarity after 15 November.
demand_pricing: DCR module realisations: retail about INR23-24/W; KUSUM C and C&I about INR21.5; IPP about INR20 for next year; blended DCR average about INR21.5-22/W.
Non-DCR module pricing has fallen from INR14-15/W a year ago to about INR12.5/W; Premier realises INR12.75-13/W; competitors accept sub-INR12.
Cell prices: Mono PERC USD0.12-0.125/W, TOPCon USD0.14-0.145/W.
Management says a SECI bid at about INR17-18/W was an introductory price, not a market benchmark; an INR18 DCR quote reported in the market is also not seen as a benchmark.
Mix: retail about 35-40% of the order book; no QoQ mix disclosure.
Demand: management views demand at about 50-60 GW against supply, which should match or exceed supply for 12-18 months; pure-play module makers face difficulty.
Input costs: recent increases in aluminium, copper and polymer film hit module assembly profitability; silver has eased; wafer prices from China fluctuating.

Cell order book fell QoQ because no new merchant cell orders were booked; cells are increasingly used captively as module capacity (5.6 GW) was commissioned. Management says there were no order cancellations.

qa_highlights.question: Why did the cell order book fall more than cell revenue recognised in the quarter?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said no new merchant cell orders were booked in the quarter; cells are increasingly used captively as the new 5.6 GW module line came on stream. No order cancellations.

qa_highlights.question: Is the Rs 2,400 crore FY27 capex still on track and what is the spend profile?
qa_highlights.answer: Most cell and module expansion capex is complete; remaining spend covers Naidupeta, battery, aluminium and open-access captive projects. Capex about INR700 crore per quarter for the next two quarters, totalling about INR2,400 crore for FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Is the battery (BESS) plan enough to meet the 40% localisation rule without more capex?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said cell-to-pack and pack-to-container lines plus Indian EMS and localised components should meet 40% easily, with no additional capex needed. LFP cells are still to be contracted from China.

qa_highlights.question: Are the margins and pricing on the order book at current levels, and what is the risk from low-priced DCR orders?
qa_highlights.answer: Orders were booked at current prices, and management hopes to hold margins subject to cost volatility. It views the SECI at about INR17-18 and the INR18 quote as introductory and not benchmarks.

qa_highlights.question: Is the transformer margin normal level?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the normalised transformer margin is about 15%; the prior quarter's 22% was boosted by steel and copper price increases and hedged inventory.

qa_highlights.question: Is there any block sale or QIP risk?
qa_highlights.answer: Management denied a GEF block or promoter sale and said the QIP was only an enabling resolution; no QIP is planned, with internal cash flow funding the capex.

risks_watch: China's draft export controls on advanced equipment: final outcome expected in 3-4 weeks; ingot-wafer equipment timelines (Phase 1 December 2027) depend on it.
Non-DCR pricing pressure and rising aluminium, copper and film costs; margin guidance is subject to cost volatility.
Working capital: raw material inventory build-up; management targets normalisation by the March 2027 quarter.
Naidupeta ALMM enrolment inspection (expected third week of November) and the 70% CUF target by March 2027.
BESS cell sourcing is unconfirmed: no firm LFP supply tie-up with Chinese suppliers.
US factory: JV partner in place, site decision in 12-18 months; no capex size given.
Transformer ramp-up: type testing and customer acceptance for large units take 8-12 months.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: 7 GW Naidupeta TOPCon cell line is commissioned with commercial production due late November 2026, CUF ramping to 25-30% in December and ~70% by end-March 2027; 4 GVA transformer capacity is also being commissioned.

rows.why: Naidupeta CUF ramp from 25-30% (Dec) to ~70% (Mar 2027) and a INR16,260 crore order book (~10 GW to execute over 12-14 months) support a significant step-up in volumes.

rows.why: Capex is being moderated to ~INR700 crore per quarter, ~INR2,400 crore for FY27, and most cell and module expansion capex is complete; the next major project (ingot-wafer, ~10 GW by June 2028) is already approved and in progress, though its equipment is dependent on China export-control clarity.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management expects a significant step-up in financial performance as Naidupeta and Seetharampur ramp, but gave no explicit revenue or margin number to beat.

rows.why: Risks include China's draft export controls on high-end equipment (outcome in 3-4 weeks), non-DCR price pressure, input cost inflation, and an unconfirmed LFP cell supply for BESS; transformer margin normalising to ~15% from 22% prior quarter.

rows.why: BESS operationalisation is expected in Q2 2027 via cell-to-pack and pack-to-container lines with RCT, though LFP cell supply is not yet tied up; transformer type testing is complete for all ranges except EHV.

rows.label: Raw material inventory normalisation
rows.why: Working capital rose on raw material build for Seetharampur and Naidupeta ramp plus shipping congestion; management targets normalisation by the March 2027 quarter.

rows.label: Order book execution and new order wins

rows.label: US cell factory with JV partner
rows.why: JV partner is in place and site finalisation is targeted in 12-18 months; no capex size was given.

tone.note: Management was confident on demand, the Naidupeta ramp and policy tailwinds, but cautious on China export controls, BESS LFP cell sourcing and non-DCR margins; analysts probed cell order book decline, margin sustainability on low-priced DCR orders, and transformer margin normalisation.

544239|2026-03.headline: ECOS Q4 FY26 revenue up 16.65% to INR2,067.6 million, EBITDA down to INR241.5 million; FY27 guided to 18-20% growth at 11-13% margin.
544239|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue from operations grew 16.65% YoY to INR2,067.60 million, while EBITDA declined to INR241.53 million from INR264.67 million in Q4 FY25, reflecting continued investment in people, technology and leadership. For FY26, revenue rose 23.58% to INR8,081.58 million and EBITDA was INR939.29 million, with margins hit by higher manpower cost, tech spend, ETS price competition and a one-time doubtful-debt provision of about INR80 million. Management said the Middle East crisis dented CCR growth in March, and guided FY27 revenue growth of 18-20% and EBITDA margin of 11-13%, with cost growth expected to be lower than revenue growth. Analysts pressed on margin compression, falling revenue per trip and competitive pricing in ETS; management attributed the trend partly to shorter trips and airport transfers.

financial_highlights.change: vs INR264.67 million in Q4 FY25 (decline)
vs 4.04 million in FY25, approx. +29% YoY

segments.name: ETS (employee transportation services)
segments.commentary: 58% of FY26 revenue and 57% in Q4 FY26. Stable demand from IT/ITES and a strong surge from GCC clients, but competitive pricing pressure was most visible here.

segments.name: CCR (chauffeur-driven car rental)
segments.commentary: 42% of FY26 revenue and 43% in Q4 FY26. Growth slowed in March after the Middle East crisis, though management says it bounced back; management described CCR as a brand-led business with a premium.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth aspiration of 18% to 20%; management expects about 60-65% of growth from new client acquisition and the rest from existing clients.
FY27 EBITDA margin expected at 11% to 13%, with management saying this holds for the next couple of years too.
Employee cost growth budgeted at about 13% to 16% in the latest AOP; other expenses to rise about 8% to 9%.
Fuel price increases above roughly 5% are generally passed through to clients, with lags of a few days to a few weeks.
No dividend declared; the board will hold a separate meeting to consider dividend or other ways to enhance shareholder value.
capex_capacity: FY26 vendor partner network of about 20,000 vehicles, versus about 14,000 in FY25; the model remains asset-light.
Over 14% of CCR corporate bookings came through CabDrive Pro, API or the customer app in Q4 FY26.
Direct web booking portal launched in Q4 FY26 for pre-scheduled rides, aimed at premium individuals and SMEs rather than mass B2C.
New core backend platform launched to improve process efficiency.

EV investment remains cautious; capex would rise materially only if EVs become financially sustainable and charging infrastructure and residual values support them. Analyst noted about INR120 million capex over four years (about INR30 million a year).
demand_pricing: Active client base above 1,750; 223 new clients added in FY26 (64 in Q4) versus 188 in FY25.
55% of FY26 revenue from clients associated with ECOS for more than five years. Churn among top 200 clients is about 2-3%, per management.
Demand from GCCs and manufacturing facilities is a notable driver of ETS enterprise wins; CCR growth is diversified across sectors.
Competitive price pressure is mainly in ETS, led by new entrants; management says prices should rise once operations prove unsustainable.

Average revenue per trip fell from about INR1,600 in FY25 to about INR1,550 in FY26, versus about INR1,750-1,780 in FY24. Management cited pricing pressure plus shorter ETS trips and more CCR airport transfers.
No demand impact seen yet from the government's work-from-home appeal.

qa_highlights.question: How is the West Asia crisis affecting demand, and what is FY27 growth guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: CCR growth slowed in March after the Middle East crisis, with a bounce back expected if the disruption is short. Management aspires to 18-20% growth in FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Can fuel price hikes be passed on, and what is the margin impact?
qa_highlights.answer: Most contracts have pass-through clauses triggered above roughly 5%, with lags of days to weeks. Management says the 6-7% increase has been fully passed on.

qa_highlights.question: What is the status of the INR8 crore receivable provision?
qa_highlights.answer: Legal proceedings for recovery are ongoing and management is hopeful. Recovery may come in FY27 or later.

qa_highlights.question: What are the expected growth rates for employee and other expenses?
qa_highlights.answer: Employee cost is budgeted to grow about 13-16% and other expenses about 8-9%, both below the revenue growth target. Management expects operating leverage.

qa_highlights.question: Why is revenue per trip declining, and is pricing pressure easing?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited ETS pricing pressure and shorter trips plus airport transfers. Pressure appears to have stabilised in the last quarter, while the company is also winning larger enterprise contracts.

qa_highlights.question: Will EBITDA margins recover to the earlier 14-16% range?
qa_highlights.answer: Management guided 11-13% for FY27 and the next couple of years. It expects CCR brand premium to offset ETS price competition over time.

risks_watch: Margin compression: EBITDA margin in FY26 was about 11.6%, down from roughly 15% at IPO, and Q4 EBITDA fell YoY despite 16.65% revenue growth.
Falling revenue per trip (about INR1,550 in FY26) indicates pricing pressure in ETS from new entrants.
Pending legal recovery of the roughly INR80 million doubtful debt; timing is uncertain.
Middle East and fuel-price volatility affecting CCR demand and the lag in fuel pass-through.
Cost growth versus revenue growth in FY27: the company needs to deliver operating leverage against its 13-16% employee cost budget.
Dividend decision pending a separate board meeting.
544239|2026-03.management_tone: Confident on long-term demand and client wins, but cautious on near-term margins and EV capex. Management was candid that pricing pressure in ETS and the March CCR slowdown weighed on the quarter, and it avoided quantifying the timing of margin recovery beyond guidance.
key_quotes: So, we have to focus on both and we have to see how we are able to draw a balance between the growing the revenue and also expanding the margins.
So, that was a one-time and we have already that is under legal proceedings for recovery of that money and we are very hopeful of the recovery.
I cannot sacrifice revenue growth for expanding the margin in any one year because then I'm compromising my business for the future.

rows.why: Trips rose about 29% to 5.23 million in FY26 from 4.04 million, 223 new clients were added (64 in Q4), and management targets 18-20% revenue growth with 60-65% from new clients, though the March CCR slowdown and falling revenue per trip temper this.

rows.why: Asset-light model with about 20,000 vendor vehicles (vs about 14,000 in FY25) and EV capex kept cautious at roughly INR30 million a year; no utilisation figure or board capex plan was disclosed.

rows.why: Legal recovery proceedings are ongoing and management is hopeful, but the roughly INR80 million provision may only be recovered in FY27 or later, so timing is uncertain.

tone.note: Management was confident on client wins, GCC-driven ETS demand and the CCR brand premium, and cautious on near-term margins, the March CCR slowdown and EV capex. Analysts pressed on margin compression (FY26 about 11.6% vs roughly 15% at IPO), falling revenue per trip and ETS pricing competition.

544239|2026-06.headline: ECOS Q1 FY27 revenue rose 16.7% to INR2,113.7 mn, but EBITDA margin fell to 10.3% and FY27 margin guidance was cut to ~10%.
544239|2026-06.overview: Revenue grew 16.7% YoY to INR2,113.72 million and trips rose 27% YoY to about 1.48 million, with 61 new clients added. EBITDA was flat YoY at INR218.47 million, and margin fell to 10.3% from 12.0% a year ago and 11.7% in Q4 FY26. Management attributed the drop to higher operating costs, a higher ETS mix and more intense pricing pressure, especially in ETS. The FY27 EBITDA margin guidance was lowered to around 10% from the earlier 11-13% range, while revenue growth guidance of 15-18% was retained.

544240|2026-09.headline: Raymond Lifestyle Q2 FY27 total income rose 14% YoY to INR2,125 crore, a record, with EBITDA up 4% to INR270 crore and margin down to 12.7%.
544240|2026-09.overview: Q2 FY27 set a record quarterly total income of INR2,125 crore (up 14% YoY), with revenue from operations at INR2,075 crore (up 13%). Consolidated EBITDA rose 4% YoY to INR270 crore, but margin fell about 120 bps to 12.7% on freight, wool and cotton costs and higher brand spend ahead of the festive season. The company ended with a net cash surplus of INR69 crore versus a net debt of INR246 crore a year earlier, and working capital days fell to 82 from 105. Management reiterated FY27 guidance of double-digit revenue growth, mid-to-high double-digit EBITDA growth, INR300 crore-plus net cash and double-digit PBT growth, with H2 expected to carry the year.

segments.name: Branded Textile
segments.commentary: Q2 revenue INR971 crore (+7% YoY); H1 INR1,650 crore (+3%). Segment EBITDA INR188 crore at 19.3% margin, helped by mix shift to pure wool and poly-wool blends; up 42% QoQ.

segments.name: Branded Apparel
segments.commentary: Q2 revenue INR559 crore (+20% YoY), highest ever quarterly; H1 INR908 crore (+14%). Segment EBITDA INR49 crore (+20%), margin stable at 8.8%, with casual brands ColorPlus and Parx leading.

segments.name: Emerging Businesses
segments.commentary: Q2 revenue INR100 crore (+15% YoY), first time above INR100 crore; H1 INR179 crore. EBITDA negative INR23 crore in Q2; H1 losses reported as roughly doubled on analyst question.

guidance_outlook: FY27 guidance reiterated: double-digit top-line growth, mid-to-high double-digit EBITDA growth, INR300 crore-plus net cash/FCFF, and PBT at least double-digit higher (about INR220-225 crore).
Management expects H2 revenue growth above 10%, taking full-year growth above 10%, with H2 EBITDA margin likely above 12.7%.

Branded Apparel margin guided to double-digit plus in a couple of years; Ethnix breakeven in 18-24 months; Home breakeven-plus by end FY27; Innerwear breakeven at year-end, real breakeven next year.
capex_capacity: Garmenting: Hindupur (Andhra Pradesh) fifth plant expanded from 3 lines to 10 lines; over INR70 crore of capex going to Hindupur. Three lines are live; fourth line expected live Nov-Dec 2026, one line roughly every 3 months, all 10 lines in about 18-21 months.
Garmenting peak capacity about 10 million units after expansion; existing plants run at 90%+ utilisation; Ethiopia plant running at full capacity.
Capex also covers mill machinery upgrades, worker safety, ESG upgrades, COCO stores and SAP S/4HANA (textile and B2C go-live from 1 November 2026).

demand_pricing: Festive timing: Diwali on 8-9 November 2026 vs 22-23 October 2025, so primary loading partly shifted into Q3; management says Q2 loading was about half of last year's full loading.
Like-to-like store growth in double digits; Dussehra minus 45 days LFL +14%; Diwali minus 30 days offtake up about 20-23% YoY.
Casual brands (ColorPlus, Parx) grew at high double digits in Q2.
Garmenting order book: factories full till end January/mid-February 2027, booking end-February; Europe H1 up 30% YoY, Q2 up 50%; UK improving.

qa_highlights.question: Is Branded Apparel's strong growth driven by channel stocking from the festive shift or by secondary sales?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Diwali timing moved about 20-25 days; Q2 had only partial primary loading, yet Branded Apparel grew 20%, backed by secondary offtake and like-to-like store growth in double digits.

qa_highlights.question: How will Branded Apparel margins move, and what is the medium-term target?
qa_highlights.answer: Margin of 8.8% held despite higher marketing and raw material costs; management expects improvement from fresh pricing and scale, guiding to double-digit-plus margin in a couple of years.

qa_highlights.question: How will H2 deliver the FY27 guidance given H1 revenue up about 10% and EBITDA up mid-single digit?
qa_highlights.answer: H2 is seasonally larger (about 57-58% of revenue); with Diwali in November, management expects H2 revenue growth above 10% and H2 EBITDA margin above 12.7%, with cost-saving initiatives and full price pass-through in Q3-Q4.

qa_highlights.question: What is the cash flow trajectory and why is H1 operating cash flow weak?
qa_highlights.answer: H1 is seasonally weak; net cash was INR69 crore vs minus INR246 crore a year ago. Management expects year-end cash of INR300 crore-plus vs INR179 crore last year.

qa_highlights.question: Why did other expenses rise 21% and what is brand spend?
qa_highlights.answer: Brand spend rose to INR116 crore from INR98 crore (+18%), 7.2% of B2C sales vs 6.8%; salaries rose about INR20 crore. Higher brand spend is budgeted to continue.

qa_highlights.question: Why did High Value Cotton Shirting margin compress, and when does it recover?
qa_highlights.answer: Cotton and flax costs stayed high, and B2B orders were booked earlier at lower prices; flax prices are stabilising and newer orders carry better prices, so H2 margin is expected to be better, with EBITDA margin double-digit-plus by year end.

qa_highlights.question: What is the working capital discrepancy between balance sheet and cash flow?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO explained that unutilised GST credits and other current assets/liabilities explain the gap; the days metric fell to 82 from 105, and management expects below 70 days at year end.

risks_watch: Raw material inflation (crude at USD105-110/bbl, wool at multi-year highs, cotton and flax elevated) with partial pass-through in B2B lines.
Rupee near 94-95/USD; US tariff uncertainty; UK/EU FTA signing expected December 2026 and not yet implemented, so EU shipments depend on it.
Domestic demand risk from inflation, repo rate hike of 25 bps to 5.50%, weak monsoon, and election outcome in a large foreign country on 3 November.
Emerging Businesses losses (Q2 EBITDA negative INR23 crore); Ethnix breakeven 18-24 months away; Innerwear sleepwear run-off.
Working capital and H1 cash flow seasonality; store additions skewed to H2; Hindupur ramp-up efficiency lags line commissioning.

544244|2026-03.headline: Gala Precision FY26 revenue rose 32% to INR314 crores, but EBITDA margin fell to 16.51% on a ~1% (INR3.23 crore) forex loss.
544244|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue was about INR95 crores (up 26% YoY), with EBITDA of about INR17 crores (up 31%, margin 17.57%) and net profit of about INR12 crores (up 22%, PAT margin 12.9%). For FY26, revenue reached INR314 crores (up 32%), EBITDA INR52 crores (up 27%, margin 16.51%), and profit after exceptional items INR36 crores (up 32%). Management attributed the annual margin dip mainly to a forex loss, and said raw material costs are passed through to customers with a lag. The Chennai fastener plant reached a Phase 1 run-rate of about INR5 crores per month, with Phase 2 expected to add capacity by mid-2026.

segments.name: DSS (disc spring)
segments.commentary: Largest segment at about 49% of FY26 revenue, described as a stable recurring base.

segments.name: SFS (special fastening solutions)
segments.commentary: Crossed INR100 crores, reaching INR108 crores in FY26 (+64% YoY); about 34% of revenue and fastest growing, with fasteners sales of about INR100 crores.

segments.name: CSS (coil spring)
segments.commentary: About 17% of FY26 revenue, supported by steady industrial and mobility demand.

guidance_outlook: Company growth target of 20% to 25% in overall revenue; wind segment fasteners and springs targeted at 25% to 30% in the short term.
Chennai FY27 sales expected at about INR80 crores (67% to 70% of INR120 crores capacity); capacity to reach INR10 crores per month by end of FY27.
Cash flow guidance: maintain or improve cash-flow conversion by about 10% YoY; inventory days at 103, with a target to cut about 10 days.
EBITDA margin expected to stabilise in the 17% to 19% range by FY27 end, assuming no further forex volatility.
Export share expected to stay at 35% to 40% of sales.
Offshore wind expected to contribute about 10% of fastener sales within two to three years.
EU-India FTA expected to take effect around January 2027, removing the 3.7% EU import duty, though CBAM may offset the benefit.
Wada land (5 to 10 acres) expected to be finalised around June-end or July 2026; new plant build of 15 to 18 months; FY27 capex about INR50 crores, funded by internal accruals and bank borrowings.
capex_capacity: Chennai fastener plant: installed capacity 4,600 MT; Phase 1 reached about INR5 crores per month (about INR60 crores annualised) from August 2025 ramp-up; plant utilisation about 35% in FY26.
Chennai Phase 2 capex to complete by June-July 2026, adding another INR5 crores per month (about INR60 crores annual); total Chennai capacity INR120 crores per annum by year-end.
Wada plant: no additional land; disc spring running about 80% utilisation; coil spring and fastener capacity have headroom, to be unlocked via productivity, line balancing and outsourcing.
Wada land purchase of 5 to 10 acres under negotiation for an own-land expansion; Chennai backup option is a SIPCOT long lease or an existing building to shift stud manufacturing.
Renewable and mobility capex: 1.8 MW open access solar plant ordered for captive consumption.
demand_pricing: Wind: about 60% to 65% of wind sales from India and 30% to 35% from exports; first high-tensile bolt supply to a global wind OEM in India from Chennai in Q4 FY26.
Growth mix in FY26 cited as about 10% from new customers, 10% to 12% from new parts with existing customers, and 5% to 7% organic growth.
Addressable market expanded: studs cover about US$1 billion; bolts and nuts take it to about US$2.5 billion. Global fastener market cited at about US$100 billion.
CSS competitors named as NHK Spring and Stumpp Schuele & Somappa; some imports from Europe remain a substitution opportunity.
Raw materials are 100% passed through to customers; process costs (gas, diesel) are being repriced from April 2026, with recovery expected on an annualised basis.
Hedging policy cut from 70% to 40% of estimated export collections, covering 12 months, net of imports for USD exposure.
Management says a currency depreciation gave a top-line benefit in Q4 but also created a non-cash forward-cover loss; the amount was not quantified on the call.

qa_highlights.question: What wind-energy order book and growth visibility exist for the coming year?
qa_highlights.answer: Management targets 25% to 30% growth in short-term wind fasteners and springs; wind sales are about 60% to 65% India and 30% to 35% exports.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Chennai revenue ramp and outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Phase 1 ramped from INR1 crore to INR5 crores per month from August; Phase 2 adds INR5 crores per month by June-July, with INR80 crores targeted for FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Why did EBITDA margin fall to 16.5%, and how is raw-material inflation handled?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the drop from about 17.1% mainly to a roughly 1% (INR3.23 crore) forex loss, not mix or raw materials; raw materials are fully passed through with a lag.

qa_highlights.question: Is there a land and expansion plan beyond Chennai?
qa_highlights.answer: Wada land (2 to 3 plots) is in advanced talks, likely finalised June-end or July; a 15 to 18 month build is expected, with about INR50 crores of capex in FY27.

qa_highlights.question: How much did the EU-India FTA and CBAM matter?
qa_highlights.answer: Current EU import duty of 3.7% on Gala products would fall to zero when the FTA takes effect around January 2027, but CBAM could offset the benefit.

qa_highlights.question: What is the hedging policy and export mix outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Forward cover is set at up to 40% of estimated export collections for 12 months; exports are expected to remain 35% to 40% of sales.

risks_watch: Forex volatility: a forex loss of about INR3.23 crores hit FY26 margins, and forward-cover losses can distort quarterly profit.
Chennai utilisation: FY26 was about 35%; the FY27 target of about INR80 crores depends on Phase 2 commissioning by mid-2026 and on scaling the bolt business.
Inventory: Chennai ramp-up adds inventory; working-capital days (103) and cash conversion are a watch item.
Wada land acquisition timelines could slip; Chennai backup plan depends on a SIPCOT lease or an existing building.
Pending patent suit on wedge lock washers: next hearing in June 2026; no arguments yet.
CBAM and EU trade changes could offset the expected FTA duty benefit.
Raw-material and gas cost pass-through is lagged; quarterly margin volatility is possible before price revisions take effect.
544244|2026-03.management_tone: Confident on growth and capacity plans, with specific timelines. Cautious and hedged on land acquisition and on quarterly forex and cost pass-through effects. Several answers were loosely worded, and exact figures (such as the currency benefit to revenue) were deferred.

So, we are quite close to in closing this land, but still not close, that is the fact.
So, with combination of this all, we are seeing that the current year whatever number we are targeting, we should be able to optimize our capacity utilization in Wada.
On the annualized basis, we will definitely see that whatever is been incurred is recovered.

rows.why: Wada disc spring runs at about 80% utilisation with no additional land, and management guided about INR50 crores of FY27 capex for a 5-10 acre own-land plant once land is finalised; timing depends on land negotiations.

544244|2026-06.headline: Gala Precision Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue ~INR75 crore (+20% YoY), EBITDA margin 16.51%, PAT margin 11.44%; FY27 EBITDA margin guided 17-19%.
544244|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue from operations was about INR75 crore, up 20% YoY, with EBITDA of about INR12 crore (+28% YoY, 16.51% margin) and net profit of about INR8 crore (+29% YoY, 11.44% margin). Management said order booking rose about 40% YoY and first-quarter revenue is typically 20-22% of the full year. A roughly INR3 crore dispatch slipped out of the quarter due to a customer payment delay, which management said cost about 5 percentage points of growth. Management reiterated 20-25% FY27 revenue growth and a 17-19% EBITDA margin range, and said FY27 working capital would stay at similar levels (around 180 days) pending a KPMG study. The call also covered a Chennai ramp-up, a planned Wada land purchase, and a reduction in forex hedging cover from 70% to 40% of export collections.

financial_highlights.change: vs ~INR80-85 crore same period last year

segments.name: Disc Springs (DSS)
segments.commentary: Largest segment at 54% of Q1 FY27 revenue, sales +31% YoY, growth attributed mainly to the Wada plant. Disc springs are a niche category with customer buying of INR5-10 crore each.

segments.name: SFS
segments.commentary: Contributed 29% of revenue, INR223 million. Management cited growing customer adoption and new business wins; the SFS cost spread versus European peers was described as 10-15% (up to 18%) on exports and 2-3% in India.

segments.name: CSS
segments.commentary: Contributed 17% of revenue, INR125 million, citing steady demand across industrial and mobility applications.

segments.name: Fasteners (Chennai)
segments.commentary: New Chennai plant (4,600 MT installed capacity, high-tensile bolts) is ramping; Phase 1 utilisation about 70-80% in Q1. Wind-turbine fastener contribution is about 25-26% of Q1 sales as stated, with the offshore-wind product targeted at 10% of FY27 fastener sales.

guidance_outlook: FY27 EBITDA margin guided at 17-19%; management said it is confident and that this range holds for FY28 as well.
FY27 revenue growth guided at 20-25% YoY; management said it is on track or exceeding this.
Effective tax rate expected at around 20% or less, helped by deductions and a solar open-access project due for commissioning in Q3.
Working capital expected at similar levels (around 180 days) for now; KPMG study report expected by end-August 2026, with targets to be set in Q3.
Chennai Phase 1 utilisation targeted at 80-90% in Q2 and ~70% for Phase 1-2 combined by Q4; Chennai EBITDA expected to be comparable with Wada around Q4 FY27 or Q1 FY28.
New Wada land (10-11 acre) capex of about INR40-45 crore, mostly in FY28, subject to completing the purchase (2-3 months).
capex_capacity: Chennai plant: new fastener facility with 4,600 MT installed capacity; Phase 1 utilisation ~70-80% in Q1 FY27; Phase 2 mezzanine (~10,000 sq ft) construction to finish in Q2 and more machines by Q3, required in Q4.
Chennai monthly run rate: manufacturing INR4-5 crore per month; June production ~INR4.5 crore but dispatches lower due to an item on hold.
Hot-dip galvanising (HDG) plant commissioned at Chennai, brought in-house to improve margin and delivery.
MoU signed for ~10.15 acre of land at Wada, adjacent to existing plant; ~50,000 sq ft shed planned mainly for fasteners and partly disc springs; legal due diligence underway.
Solar open-access project initiated, expected commissioning in Q3 FY27.
demand_pricing: Order booking up ~40% YoY, per management.
Pricing stable; management says it offers 10-20% savings to customers while holding margins, and passes through raw-material increases with a lag.
Fasteners cited as the main growth driver. Customer wallet sizes: fasteners INR50-500 crore vs disc springs INR5-10 crore.
New products (bolts, smart fasteners for offshore wind, wedge lock washers) are ~30-35% of order book, per management.
Company said it is taking share from European producers; some multi-year accounts grew share of business from 5-10% to 50-75%.
Forex: forward cover on export collections reduced from 70% to 40% due to euro volatility and war-related uncertainty; ~4% of 12-month exposure already covered.
Product mix: ~85% customised products; ~15% sold to fastener distributors at company level. Disc spring and Gallock 75-80% to OEMs; SFS >95% direct to OEMs.
Management said a single ~INR3 crore+ dispatch was held because of a customer payment delay; ex-this, growth would have been ~25%.
Management cited TAM of USD100 billion for fasteners, with Gala addressing ~USD2.5 billion including bolts and nuts.
Seatbelt retractor spring: customer approved Gala as source after July visit; small-batch supply to start, slow ramp due to safety-critical nature.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY27 margin bridge from 16.51% to the 17-19% guide, across forex, Chennai leverage and mix? Also, why cut forward cover from 70% to 40%?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said FY27 EBITDA margin should be 17-19% with no forex hit since exports are hedged. Jalan cited Chennai utilisation improving in Q3/Q4 and Q1 being ~20-22% of full-year revenue to absorb fixed overheads. The cut to 40% reflects euro volatility and war-related uncertainty; about 4% of 12-month exposure is covered so far.

qa_highlights.question: How will FY27 growth stack up, and what drove the Q1 growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Order booking up ~40% YoY. A ~INR3 crore+ dispatch was held for a customer payment delay; ex this, growth would have been ~25%. Management said it is confident of meeting or exceeding the 20-25% FY27 growth guide. DSS growth came from Wada and fastener growth from Chennai.

qa_highlights.question: What is the working capital outlook, and when will KPMG study benefits show up?
qa_highlights.answer: Working capital is expected to stay at similar levels (around 180 days). The KPMG study started in July, with the report expected by end-August or in Q2; targets and actions to be set in Q3, so no firm improvement guidance yet.

qa_highlights.question: Why don't customers switch to Gala despite a 15-18% cost advantage over European peers, and how long does onboarding take?
qa_highlights.answer: Onboarding takes 12-24 months (plant approval, audit, samples, then share-of-business ramp). Some multi-year accounts grew share from 5-10% to 50-75%. Some customers with cost advantage still do not switch immediately. No customer lost on quality or delivery in 25 years.

qa_highlights.question: Seatbelt retractor spring status, land capex timing, and effective tax rate sustainability?
qa_highlights.answer: Customer approved Gala as source after a July visit; small-batch supply starts with a slow ramp given safety-critical use. Wada land (~10 acre MoU, 2-3 months to close) needs ~INR40-45 crore capex, mostly in FY28. ETR guided at ~20% or less, helped by 100% deductions for R&D (Sec 35(1)(i)), ESOP perquisite deduction, higher tax depreciation and a solar open-access project commissioning in Q3.

qa_highlights.question: Chennai utilisation, run rate, and HDG plant impact?
qa_highlights.answer: Phase 1 utilisation was ~70-80% in Q1 and is targeted at 80-90% in Q2, with Phase 1-2 combined ~70% by Q4. Chennai manufacturing runs at INR4-5 crore a month; June output was ~INR4.5 crore but dispatches were lower due to a held item. In-house HDG improved margin and delivery and unlocked some customers.

risks_watch: Customer payment delays: a ~INR3 crore+ dispatch slipped out of Q1, costing ~5 percentage points of growth; watch Q2 receivables and working capital days versus ~180 days.
Chennai ramp execution: Phase 1 utilisation must reach 80-90% in Q2 and Phase 2 machines are needed by Q4; Chennai EBITDA parity with Wada is guided only for Q4 FY27 or Q1 FY28.
Forex: export hedge cut from 70% to 40% with only ~4% of 12-month exposure covered; euro volatility and war-related risk could affect realisations.

Bank MCLR hikes by leading public sector banks and an early 15-20 bps move by one or two banks were cited; a clearer picture expected around 24-25 October.
Management said prime pricing competition from PSU and private banks is an ongoing feature; if acquisition pricing lags, prime attrition may rise and the company will lean on non-prime growth.

Insurance commission regulation draft: management estimated 10-11% of PBT comes from cross-sell income; about 4-5% can be offset, leaving 6-7% of PBT at risk. Sambhav fees and prime efficiencies may offset part of this, mainly on a longer-term basis.

qa_highlights.question: Why did developer finance decline QoQ, and what is the strategy for the DF book?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said higher repayments from project cash flows plus slower disbursements drove the decline, not a conscious strategy. DF sanctions rose sharply in H1, and the target is 15-17% of the portfolio, with recovery expected in Q3-Q4.

qa_highlights.question: Will the repo hikes compress margins and how much pass-through is possible on the prime side?
qa_highlights.answer: About 80-82% of repo hikes flow through to cost of funds and to portfolio pricing, so the main margin risk is on acquisition pricing. If prime acquisition pricing lags, attrition and BT-out rise and the company shifts toward non-prime.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the fall in fee income?
qa_highlights.answer: Fee income rose on higher insurance income (attachment rates higher with Sambhav growth) and higher foreclosure income in the quarter, not a decline. Fee-related expenses are marginal and range-bound.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 20 bps cost of funds decline a one-off, and what is the exit COF?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is a starting point, not a one-off, though part came from one-time maturity of high-priced borrowings. Three 25 bps hikes would take COF up about 61 bps, from roughly 7% in September to about 7.6% by March.

qa_highlights.question: Why did home loan originations decline QoQ, and what is the YoY growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said quarterly movements are seasonal and the company tracks AUM rather than disbursals. Home loan disbursal growth was 24% YoY, close to the company's 25% disbursement growth.

qa_highlights.question: Will guidance be revised given NIM expansion this quarter?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said no revision for now. NIM compression of about 25 bps is still expected, and AUM growth could slow to 22-23% if acquisition pricing lags, given the rise in BT-out rates.

risks_watch: Acquisition pricing pass-through by banks after the repo hike, due around 24-25 October; a lag could increase prime attrition and cut AUM growth from 25% toward 22-23%.
Insurance commission regulation: a 6-7% PBT impact is possible if the draft guidelines stand, which would push opex to NTI flat next year.
Developer finance book: a QoQ decline and 13% YoY growth; watch whether disbursements recover in Q3-Q4 as management expects.
Rising salary costs (19% YoY in Q2) as Sambhav and senior hires build out; management expects elevated costs for 1.5-2 years.
Home loan GNPA rose to 36 bps from 34 bps; watch for further upward movement, and whether the single LRD slippage stays isolated.

544253|2026-03.headline: Kross Q4 FY26 revenue rose 22% YoY to INR 225.4 crore, with EBITDA margin at 14.9%; management guides 14-15% margins and FY27 growth near 22%.

Q4 revenue rose 22% YoY to INR 225.4 crore, EBITDA rose 25% to INR 33.6 crore and PAT rose 31% to INR 22.4 crore. Management says the Middle East conflict caused LPG shortages and commodity and consumable cost increases in Q4, with steel price hikes of INR 3-5/kg expected from April and a retrospective OEM pass-through lagging by about one quarter. The company has raised prices about 5% in trailer axles and suspensions and says it has fully deployed IPO proceeds.

Chhattisgarh market recovered after a long gap, contributing to trailer order growth; share gains with larger customers cited.
Q2 tractor volumes linked to TAFE planned production of 13,000-14,000 tractors in October; below-average rainfall noted by analyst.

544254|2026-03.headline: Tolins Tyres FY26 consolidated revenue rose about 12% to INR327.12 crore, but EBITDA fell to INR47.8 crore and PAT to INR35.69 crore.
544254|2026-03.overview: FY26 consolidated revenue from operations grew about 12% YoY to INR327.12 crore, while EBITDA (excluding other income) declined to INR47.8 crore from INR57.91 crore, with margin at 14.6%. PAT fell to INR35.69 crore from INR38.67 crore, and basic EPS was INR9.03. Q4 FY26 revenue rose about 12% to INR77.99 crore, but Q4 EBITDA fell to INR11.22 crore (14.4% margin) from INR13.57 crore, with PAT of INR8.94 crore. Management attributed the pressure to a GST rate mismatch on retreading materials, higher inventory, longer receivable cycles and West Asia disruption, and gave only a soft FY27 outlook of maintaining FY26 performance.

Industry association has sought a 5% GST rate on retreads, which the government is reportedly considering.

segments.commentary: Tyre production rose to 5,35,870 units in FY26 from 3,93,253 in FY25, about 36% growth, while top-line growth lagged. Utilisation in the Indian tyre segment was about 45%. A new heavy-duty tractor rear tyre has received an encouraging dealer response.

segments.commentary: Plant capacity is 1,200 metric tons, with utilisation below 50%; management said margins are better than India, but GCC demand fell from the last quarter of FY26. Utilisation is expected to drop to 30-40% in the near term before recovering to 40-50%. Receivables are rising in the UAE.

segments.name: Exports, precured tyres and US business
segments.commentary: Management said US business started last year and repeat orders are slowly coming in, with a Europe push under way. Logistics are impacted by the Middle East war. No quantified export revenue was given.

EBITDA margin: management said 10% to 13% is an acceptable range, with a further 2-3% from waste and scrap reduction and operational efficiency.

Management expects capex to be limited this year because existing capacity is sufficient to meet demand, and says the government is likely to correct the GST imbalance.

Management said competition is intense with tyre majors in retreading materials, but it believes its 40-year expertise gives it an edge.

qa_highlights.question: Why was top-line growth only about 12% against the 20% growth previously guided, and how do gross current assets of INR309 crore compare with revenue of INR327 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the 20% was an optimistic projection and that actual growth was about 12%. It pointed to 36% growth in tyre volumes, with the gap explained by selling prices.

qa_highlights.question: When will operating cash flow turn positive, and what is the sales and marketing strategy?
qa_highlights.answer: The CFO said credit periods were extended by about one month due to GST and geopolitical uncertainty, with the aim of reducing them over a few quarters. Management said branding spend is small and that it relies on a strong marketing manager team.

qa_highlights.question: What is the status and margin of the Ras Al Khaimah UAE plant?
qa_highlights.answer: Capacity is 1,200 MT with utilisation below 50%. The CFO said UAE margins are better than India's, and utilisation could fall to 30-40% in the next three months before recovering to 40-50%.

qa_highlights.question: Why did margins decline in Q4 and FY26, and when will GST be corrected?
qa_highlights.answer: The CFO attributed the decline to margin pressure in retreads from the GST imbalance and weaker dealer off-take. The industry body has asked for a 5% retread GST rate, and the government is considering it.

qa_highlights.question: What are the three biggest growth drivers beyond FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management pointed to higher tyre production volumes, precured tyres (Europe and the US, where repeat orders are starting), and Terra Rubber integration for in-house raw material offtake.

qa_highlights.question: Why did tyre volumes decline QoQ, and why did working capital rise from about INR230 crore to near INR300 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: Q4 volumes fell because of March uncertainty. Working capital is driven by 3-4 months of dealer credit, about 4-5 months of inventory across more than 1,200 SKUs and seasonal rubber prices, and government retentions. IPO proceeds were partly used to fund inventory.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY27 top-line guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it expects at least to maintain FY26 performance and will review after Q2 FY27, preferring to commit less and perform better.

544256|2026-03.headline: P N Gadgil FY26 consolidated revenue crossed INR10,000 crore to INR10,739 crore (+40% YoY); Q4 gross margin fell to 9.7% on a 40% bullion mix.
544256|2026-03.overview: FY26 revenue rose 40% YoY to INR10,739 crore, with full-year gross margin up 280 bps to 12% and EBITDA margin up 180 bps to 6.6%. Q4 revenue grew 123% YoY to INR3,544 crore, but gross margin fell to 9.7% (about 230 bps down YoY) as gold bars and coins rose to 40% of sales, plus one-time discounts and franchise mix. Management attributes the Q4 margin dip to mix and one-offs, and it guided FY27 revenue of INR13,500 crore, EBITDA margin 7-7.5% and PAT margin 4%, with a review next quarter given the import duty hike.

qa_highlights.answer: Management says the advance authorisation targets exporters, so it does not apply. The duty is passed to consumers, with no margin impact; it may shift demand from bars and coins toward exchanging old gold for jewellery.

qa_highlights.question: Hedging levels for FY26 and the FY27 plan?
qa_highlights.answer: Hedging was 57% in Q4 FY25, 63% in Q3 FY26 and 67% in Q4 FY26, averaging about 60% for FY26. The target is 75-80% in FY27, held back by MCX margin and premium costs of 15-20% that tied up cash.

qa_highlights.question: Why was FY27 revenue guidance raised from INR12,000 crore to INR13,500 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: FY26 beat the INR9,500 crore guidance by about INR1,000 crore. Management cites non-Maharashtra demand (about 10% of business) and strong same-store growth, which pushed the range up to INR13,500 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Why are the margin drivers one-off rather than structural, given likely repeat discounts and franchise growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Management says the discounts were one-time events worth about 0.5% of Q4 sales. Bars and coins (40% of Q4 sales) drove most of the dip, and it expects that mix to normalise to about 25%.

qa_highlights.question: Gross margin split between bars and coins and jewellery?
qa_highlights.answer: Bars and coins earn 0.5-1% gross margin; plain gold jewellery earns 12.5-13%. Franchise gross margin is about 2-3%, nearly net margin since the franchisee bears all costs.

qa_highlights.question: Inventory turnover decline?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributes the 3.8x FY26 turnover to about 8 COCO stores opened in Q4 that have not matured. It says turnover has been broadly flat, declining slightly over two to three years.

qa_highlights.question: FY27 store additions and non-Maharashtra plans?

qa_highlights.answer: Bars and coins were about 32% of FY26 sales. The promoter must reach 75% by September 2027, three years after the September 2024 listing.
