tone.note: Management was confident on FY26 results and FY27 guidance of INR13,500 crore and 7-7.5% EBITDA margin, but defensive on Q4 gross margin of 9.7%, attributing it to bars and coins mix and one-offs; it was less specific on FY27 volume after the duty hike, the QIP and hedging costs.

544256|2026-06.headline: PNG Jewellers Q1 FY27 revenue rose 41% YoY to INR2,413 crore, with EBITDA up 57% to INR192.4 crore and PAT up 52% to INR105.3 crore.
544256|2026-06.overview: Revenue from operations grew 41% YoY to INR2,413 crore, driven by retail (up 56%, with 46% SSSG), franchise (up 8%) and e-commerce (up 20%). EBITDA margin expanded 80 bps to 8.0% and PAT margin rose 40 bps to 4.4%, with gross margin flat at 13.2% reported. Management kept FY27 guidance (around 25 store additions to 103 stores, about 7% EBITDA margin, about INR400 crore other expenses) and flagged that Q1 other expenses were low due to cuts in marketing and no store launches. Hedging gains and lower other income were discussed in detail, and the promoter stake and franchise economics drew scrutiny.

financial_highlights.change: Reported gross margin flat YoY; adjusted ex-hedging up ~40-50 bps per CFO
vs ~INR12 crore in Q4 FY26 (analyst cited INR31 crore, CFO disputed); lower FD balances on mortgage

segments.name: Retail
segments.commentary: Grew 56% with 46% SSSG; now about 78% of total revenue, with jewellery about 78-79% of retail and bars/coins about 20-21%. Newer North and Central India stores run 15-18% studded ratios.

segments.name: Franchise
segments.commentary: Grew 8% YoY; management attributed the slowdown to B2B billing timing and stock replenishment, with franchise openings expected to pick up in Q2-Q3 (about 10 legacy and 5 litestyle planned).

segments.name: E-commerce
segments.commentary: Grew 20% YoY; company is deliberately shifting mix towards jewellery and away from bars/coins, so management expects better margins but slower total sales growth.

segments.name: Litestyle by PNG
segments.commentary: Studded ratio 32.9% in Q1; current litestyle gross margin of about 18-20%, with management targeting about 50% studded ratio in two years and 30-35% margin later.

guidance_outlook: Open around 25 stores in FY27, taking network to about 103 by March 2027 (63 COCO, balance FOCO); a few launches in Q2, bulk in Q3-Q4.
Network targets: about 140 stores by March 2028 and about 177 by March 2029 (about 113 legacy and 64 litestyle; about 75 COCO and 40 FOCO by March 2029).
EBITDA margin guidance of about 7% for full year FY27; other expenses about 3% of sales or roughly INR400 crore for FY27.
PAT margin underlying (ex-hedging gains) targeted at 4.1-4.25% in FY27 per CFO, versus 4.2% per CEO; 4.5-4.7% by FY29.
Hedging coverage to reach about 80% around Q3 FY27 (Q2 around 80% per CEO), and fully hedged in FY28; currently 70%+.
Gold metal loan of INR1,500-1,550 crore to be reduced by INR500-600 crore by FY29, non-GML borrowing about INR1,200 crore; targeted debt-free in four to five years.
Gross margin guidance for retail mix of 13-14% (CFO: 12.5-13.5% at 10-11% studded ratio), including hedging gains shown separately.
capex_capacity: Store count 78 at end-Q1 FY27 (57 COCO, 21 FOCO).
FY27 plan: 25 new stores, bulk in Q3 and Q4, franchise-led; deepening Maharashtra and expanding UP, Bihar, Central India and NCR.
UP stores running 18%+ studded versus 15% projection; 8-10 UP franchise openings planned in FY27; Ayodhya store opening soon.
Capital allocation focused on store expansion, franchise network, digital and operational excellence, funded from internal accruals.
Management plans a QIP at a suitable time to reduce promoter holding (above 75%); board enabling resolution already in place.
demand_pricing: Management said demand held up through April-June despite record gold prices, supported by weddings and Akshaya Tritiya; Adhik Maas was muted due to high silver prices.
Weddings postponed by Adhik Maas expected to benefit Q2 and a large part of Q3.
Customers shifting towards lightweight jewellery, studded products and old gold exchange, favouring organised players.
Hedging gains: Q3 FY26 about INR45 crore, Q4 FY26 about INR20 crore, Q2 FY26 about INR5.5-6 crore; gains shrinking as hedging coverage rises.
Marketing kept within 1.5% of sales; 250-300 hoardings cut versus last year. FY26 other expenses included about INR40-50 crore for UP launch and one-time campaigns that are not expected to recur.
Inventory turns stabilised at about 3.5-4x after refinery and B2B sales wound down (previously about 7x).

qa_highlights.question: Why is gross margin flat YoY despite mix shift toward retail, and what is the ideal retail margin at a 10-11% studded ratio?
qa_highlights.answer: Reported gross margin is flat because hedging gains are shown separately; ex-hedging adjusted gross margin is up about 40-50 bps YoY. Management targets 12.5-13.5% retail margin at a 10-11% studded ratio, and 13-14% overall retail gross margin including hedging gains.

qa_highlights.question: Why did other expenses grow only about 5% despite store expansion?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited conservative spending amid demand uncertainty, lower scheme-redemption discounts, marketing kept within 1.5% of sales with 250-300 hoardings cut, and no store launches in Q1. Spending will rise in Q3-Q4 with expansion, but EBITDA guidance is still expected to be met.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY27 other expense guidance and why was other income so different between Q4 and Q1?
qa_highlights.answer: Other expenses are guided at about 3% of sales, roughly INR400 crore for FY27. Other income was about INR10 crore in Q1 versus about INR12 crore in Q4 per the CFO, who said lower fixed deposits placed on mortgage drove the decline; cash and hedging margin money also hold some balances.

qa_highlights.question: What is the store expansion and COCO/FOCO mix plan through FY29?
qa_highlights.answer: Plan adds 25 stores in FY27 to reach 103 (63 COCO, balance FOCO), then 37 each in FY28 and FY29 to reach 140 and 177. By March 2029, about 75 COCO and 40 FOCO, with 113 legacy and 64 litestyle stores.

qa_highlights.question: What is the margin trajectory and hedging plan?
qa_highlights.answer: PAT margin underlying ex-hedging is targeted at 4.1-4.25% in FY27 per the CFO, versus about 4.2% per the CEO; 4.5-4.7% by FY29. Hedging is about 70%+ now, targeted at about 80% around Q3 FY27 and fully hedged in FY28. Hedging gains were about INR45 crore in Q3 FY26, INR20 crore in Q4 FY26 and INR5.5-6 crore in Q2 FY26.

qa_highlights.question: How is Litestyle progressing on studded mix, gross margin and store count?
qa_highlights.answer: Studded ratio is about 32.9-34% now, targeted at about 50% in a couple of years. Current litestyle gross margin is about 18-20%, versus 30-35% for the format once studded mix rises. Litestyle store target is 65-70 by March 2029 and about 100 over the longer term.

qa_highlights.question: Why are franchise revenue growth (8%) and e-commerce growth lower than company-operated stores?
qa_highlights.answer: Franchise sales are booked as B2B, so initial stocking and replenishment timing affect quarterly numbers; management expects franchise openings to pick up in Q2-Q3 (about 10 legacy and 5 litestyle). E-commerce is deliberately shifting mix away from bars and coins toward jewellery, so margins should improve but total sales growth may slow.

risks_watch: Reported gross margin flat YoY; expansion of hedging gains is shrinking as hedging coverage rises toward 80% by Q3 FY27 and full coverage in FY28, so reported margin depends on underlying retail mix.
Other expenses are guided to rise in Q3-Q4 with store openings; Q1 spend (about 5% growth) was unusually low, so H2 cost run-rate against about INR400 crore guidance needs monitoring.
Franchise revenue growth of 8% versus company-operated retail growth of 56%; visibility into franchise B2C sell-through is still being built and management has only recently gained system access.
Promoter holding above 75% with a QIP planned at a suitable time; timing and size are not specified and the stock overhang remains.
Gold metal loan of INR1,500-1,550 crore to fall by INR500-600 crore by FY29; execution of the debt-reduction path and the litestyle studded-mix shift (from about 34% toward 50%) are key checkpoints.

Other income fell to about INR10 crore from about INR12 crore in Q4 per the CFO, after the analyst cited INR31 crore; the figure was disputed on the call and should be reconciled against the filed numbers.
key_quotes: Their confidence has enabled us to deliver our highest ever first quarter, beginning FY27 on a strong note.
Despite elevated gold prices, our performa nce remains in line with our previously communicated guidance.
So franchise apple-to-apple on a quarter-to-quarter, these differences which will come, but having said that, we understand because franchise is our focus now, will be becoming big.
Eventually, we plan to take it to 80% studded inventory at a store le vel and 20% gold inventory and that would also enable us to reach a 50% to 60% studded ratio in that category.
544256|2026-06.management_tone: Confident on demand, store expansion and the long-term plan, with precise targets given across FY27-FY29. Cautious and somewhat evasive on the reasons for flat gross margin and the other income gap, leaning on adjusted (ex-hedging) figures and deferring some answers to later quarters.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: EBITDA margin rose 80 bps to 8.0% in Q1 and ex-hedging gross margin is up 40-50 bps, with FY27 EBITDA guided at about 7% and PAT margin targeted at 4.1-4.25% ex-hedging for FY27 and 4.5-4.7% by FY29, but hedging gains (Q3 FY26 about INR45 crore, Q4 FY26 about INR20 crore) are shrinking as coverage rises toward 80%.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.when: bulk in Q3-Q4 FY27, a few in Q2 FY27
rows.why: Store count of 78 at end-Q1 FY27 with about 25 openings guided for FY27 to reach 103 (63 COCO, balance FOCO), a 32% addition to the network, and a roadmap to 140 by March 2028 and 177 by March 2029.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Retail revenue grew 56% with 46% SSSG and store adds are coming in H2, though franchise grew only 8% and e-commerce 20%, and management is deliberately trading total e-commerce sales for margin.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Capex is not discussed beyond store expansion funded from internal accruals, and no utilisation figure is given, so a new capex announcement is not signalled.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management held FY27 guidance (25 stores, ~7% EBITDA margin, ~INR400 crore other expenses) and gave no revenue growth number, with Q1 other expenses only up about 5% and H2 spend due to rise.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Other expenses are guided to about INR400 crore for FY27 and are back-end loaded with store openings, and gains from hedging shrink as coverage moves from 70%+ to about 80%, so the reported margin path depends on the retail mix.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Litestyle studded ratio is 32.9% against a 50% target in two years, and Ayodhya store opening is soon, though no specific new product launch was named.

rows.label: Gold metal loan reduction and debt path
rows.why: Gold metal loan of INR1,500-1,550 crore to fall by INR500-600 crore and borrowings to go below INR1,000 crore by FY29, with non-GML borrowing about INR1,200 crore and debt-free in 4-5 years.

rows.label: QIP to reduce promoter holding above 75%
rows.when: at a suitable time, not specified
rows.why: Board enabling resolution is in place, but timing and size are unspecified and promoter holding is above 75%.

rows.label: Festive and wedding-led demand recovery in Q2-Q3
rows.why: Weddings postponed by Adhik Maas expected to benefit Q2 and much of Q3, and Akshaya Tritiya bars and coins sales rose 80.3% to INR251.4 crore.

tone.note: Management was confident on demand, store expansion and the FY29 targets, but cautious and somewhat evasive on flat reported gross margin and the other income gap (INR10 crore vs analyst's INR31 crore), leaning on ex-hedging figures; analysts pushed on hedging gains, franchise economics and promoter

544256|2026-09.headline: Q2 FY27 revenue rose 22% YoY to INR2,666 crore and EBITDA 57% to INR224.6 crore, with margin up 186 bps to 8.4%.
544256|2026-09.overview: P N Gadgil reported Q2 FY27 revenue of about INR2,660-2,666 crore (up 22% YoY), EBITDA of INR224.6 crore (8.4% margin) and PAT of INR121.1 crore (4.5% margin), with profit growing roughly twice as fast as revenue. Retail grew 31% with SSSG of 25.5%, while e-commerce fell 84% after the company cut low-margin coin sales. Management said about INR200 crore of Navaratri sales shifted from Q2 into Q3 this year, and the company completed the Silvostyle acquisition on 1 October. Gross margin was down 50 bps QoQ, which management attributed to franchisee share rising to 17% from 12%.

financial_highlights.change: +32% YoY; margin +89 bps YoY, -50 bps QoQ

financial_highlights.metric: Adjusted EBITDA (excl. INR5 crore unhedged inventory gain)

financial_highlights.value: Revenue INR5,079 crore; PAT INR226.5 crore

segments.name: Retail
segments.commentary: Retail revenue INR2,061 crore, 77% of total (72% a year ago); stud ratio 11.9% vs 9% a year ago and 10.96% in Q1. Gold bars and coins fell to 15.8% of retail revenue from about 22%.

segments.name: Franchisee
segments.commentary: Franchisee revenue grew 35% YoY; franchisee share of revenue rose to 17% from 12%.

segments.name: E-commerce
segments.commentary: E-com revenue fell 84% YoY as low-margin coin sales were deliberately reduced in favour of jewellery.

segments.name: Diamond and gold jewellery
segments.commentary: Diamond jewellery value +21% and volume +11%; gold jewellery value +47% and volume +4%. Gold bar and coin value -24%, volume -48%.

segments.name: Northern and Central India
segments.commentary: Share of retail revenue from these regions rose to 2.7% from 0.7%; seven company-owned stores there show a stud ratio of 17.4%.

guidance_outlook: Open about 23 new stores in FY27 (8-10 in Q3, rest in Q4), taking the total to about 103 stores by year-end; 80 stores at quarter end (79 India, 1 US).
FY27 company revenue target of INR13,000 crore-plus; PAT margin guidance of 4.0-4.2%.
Three-year aspiration of about INR17,000 crore revenue by FY29 (25% CAGR FY27-29); another estimate of about INR21,000 crore by FY29 was given in the Q&A.
Stud ratio to rise to 17-18% at company level and newer geographies to reach 30-35% of sales by FY30 (Maharashtra currently about 91%).
Debt to fall 20-25% by FY29-FY30; the 170-odd store target by FY29 to be funded from internal accruals.
Hedge coverage raised to about 80%.
From FY28, store openings to split 50-50 between COCO and FOCO (franchise-owned); about 30-35 stores planned for the next year.
capex_capacity: Ayodhya store operational; Prayagraj store scheduled to open 4 November 2026.

UP stores (about 4 COCO stores in Lucknow, Kanpur, Gorakhpur, Banaras, plus Patna and Indore) averaging 11-12 months old, with stock turn about 1.1x and revenue run-rate about INR60 crore per store versus INR50-55 crore plan; target 8-10 UP stores by end FY27.
Mature-store targets for new regions: 2.5-3x stock turn, rising to 3.5-4x after year 4; revenue about INR200 crore per mature store; stud ratio 22-25%.
Inventory for new-region stores is about 10% of Maharashtra gold volume because they are stud-led.
Typical Maharashtra store carries gold inventory of about INR50-55 crore, roughly 30-32 kg.
Silvostyle acquired 100% on 1 October; it already runs 18 stores and about 68 shop-in-shops.
demand_pricing: Q2 is seasonally subdued (Chaturmas), but management said demand stayed healthy; customers shifted to lightweight, studded and old gold exchange.
Footfalls above 1.78 lakh, conversion 88.6%, average transaction value INR1.22 lakh.
Management said Navaratri was good, Diwali bookings are strong and prices are soft, which should lift volumes.
Gold-bar-to-jewellery conversion improved to 68% from 53% in Q1.
Made-to-order share is 22-25% in UP versus 30-32% in Maharashtra.
Management said without gold price increases mature-store SSSG is in the single digits (7-8%).

qa_highlights.question: Was there a festive shift affecting gross margin, and by how much?
qa_highlights.answer: Navaratri moved from Q2 last year into Q3 this year; about INR200 crore of revenue from the 10 days shifted. The 50 bps QoQ gross margin dip was attributed to franchisee mix rising to 17% from 12%.

qa_highlights.question: How will capital be allocated across franchise, COCO and new brands?
qa_highlights.answer: FY27 is FOCO-led in Q3-Q4; from FY28 the split is 50-50 COCO/FOCO for both legacy and YOOU. Internal accruals are expected to fund COCO expansion, and debt is to fall 20-25% by 2030.

qa_highlights.question: How mature stores in UP are performing (turns, stud ratio, margin)?
qa_highlights.answer: Stock turn is about 1.1x (plan was 1x), revenue about INR60 crore per store (plan INR50-55 crore), stud ratio above 17% (plan 15%), gross margin about 35%.

qa_highlights.question: What is the path for YOOU inventory turn and why did legacy turn fall to 3.7x?
qa_highlights.answer: YOOU is about 70% diamond and 30% gold, with a target of 1.8-2x turns at maturity against 0.8x now. Management said legacy turns of 3.7-4x are well above the 2-2.5x industry norm and are sustainable as new stores mature.

qa_highlights.question: How will the QIP proceeds and borrowing be deployed?
qa_highlights.answer: Part of the INR700 crore QIP went into festive working capital; the rest is in FDs (about INR1,191 crore, up INR637 crore QoQ). Gross borrowings rose about INR385 crore since March on GML loans, but net borrowings fell INR167 crore after collateral and FDs.

qa_highlights.question: Outlook for employee cost and other expenses in H2?
qa_highlights.answer: Employee cost fell about INR6 crore QoQ on lower variable pay. Other expenses were INR86 crore in Q2 versus INR85 crore in Q1, and management expects similar moderation in H2.

risks_watch: Gross margin pressure as franchisee mix rises (franchisee share 17% vs 12%) and as the FOCO model scales.
Store rollout concentration: 8-10 openings in Q3 and the balance in Q4, a steep back-loaded schedule.
Festive sales shift into Q3 makes Q2 vs Q3 comparisons noisy.
Gross borrowings and finance costs rising (about INR385 crore increase since March from GML loans); deleveraging targets depend on accruals.
YOOU inventory turn at 0.8x against a 1.8-2x target; the Silvostyle integration is new.
Dependence on stable gold prices; a gold price rise is expected to lower volumes.
Call quality was poor during the Q&A; some questions (for example Vikrant Kashyap's on non-Maharashtra contribution) went unanswered.
544256|2026-09.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on growth, UP expansion, the store ramp and festive demand. More guarded on the specifics of the FY29 targets, which management called aspirational. Management also avoided some detail on the make-up of margins.
key_quotes: This reflects the strength of underlying operations and demonstrates that our margin expansion has been driven by operational improvements rather than gold price movements.
So what we're trying to say from all this is that our internal accruals should be more than enough to fund the COCO expansion, and we'll not be required to raise any further debt.
We had done a 3-year plan, which is more of an aspirational plan, but it will be difficult to right now pin a number to it.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: EBITDA margin rose 186 bps YoY to 8.4% and stud ratio is 11.9% vs 9%, but gross margin fell 50 bps QoQ as franchisee share rose to 17% from 12%, and FY27 PAT margin guidance is 4.0-4.2% (Q2 at 4.5%).

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: About 23 new stores in FY27 (8-10 in Q3, rest in Q4) taking total to ~103 from 80 at quarter end; Prayagraj opens 4 Nov 2026 and Silvostyle's 18 stores are already acquired.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Retail revenue grew 31% with SSSG 25.5%, Diwali bookings are strong and prices are soft, but management said SSSG without gold price increases is only 7-8%.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Utilisation and capex were not disclosed, but store rollout is funded from internal accruals and FY28 plan of 30-35 stores is set, so a further capex disclosure is possible rather than a firm announcement.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Q2 revenue grew 22% and PAT 53%, Diwali bookings are strong and UP stores run at about INR60 crore per store versus a INR50-55 crore plan, but about INR200 crore of Navaratri sales shifted into Q3 and the gain is partly timing.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Store rollout is steeply back-loaded (8-10 in Q3, rest in Q4), gross borrowings rose about INR385 crore since March, and the FY27 INR13,000 crore-plus target needs H2 revenue of about INR8,000 crore against H1's INR5,079 crore.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: From FY28 store openings split 50-50 between COCO and FOCO for both legacy and YOOU, and YOOU is only about 0.8x turn against a 1.8-2x target, so new-format rollout is planned but not dated.

rows.label: Northern and Central India expansion
rows.why: Share of retail revenue from these regions rose to 2.7% from 0.7%, and seven stores there show a 17.4% stud ratio; the UP stores run at about INR60 crore per store, and the target is 8-10 UP stores by end FY27.

rows.label: Debt down 20-25% by FY29-FY30
rows.why: Management targets a 20-25% borrowing cut funded from accruals, but gross borrowings rose about INR385 crore since March and the 170-store target by FY29 competes for the same cash.

rows.label: Hedge coverage raised to about 80%
rows.why: Management is raising hedge cover to about 80% to make earnings more resilient to gold price swings, a direct action already in place.

tone.note: Management was confident on store ramp, UP expansion, festive demand and FY27 revenue of INR13,000 crore-plus, but called the FY29 targets aspirational and was thin on margin make-up; analysts pushed on gross margin and unanswered questions on non-Maharashtra contribution.

544258|2026-03.headline: Q4 FY26 revenue rose 4% QoQ to INR496 crore, but EBITDA margin slipped to 5.0% as Middle East crisis cut EXIM volumes 11% QoQ.
544258|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue from operations grew about 4% QoQ to INR496 crore, the fourth straight quarter of sequential growth. EBITDA fell from INR27 crore to INR25 crore, with margin down from 5.6% to 5.0%, and PAT dropped from INR10.8 crore to INR8.3 crore. Total containers handled were 57,754, up 4.3% YoY but down 7% QoQ, with EXIM down 10.96% QoQ and domestic almost flat. For FY26, containers rose 6.14% to 2,26,578, and management attributed the shortfall from double-digit growth to the March disruption from the Strait of Hormuz closure.

financial_highlights.change: +4% QoQ from INR478 crore in Q3
down from INR27 crore in Q3
down from INR10.8 crore in Q3; margin 1.7% vs 2.3%

financial_highlights.value: over INR70 crore (management cited INR74 crore in Q&A)

segments.name: EXIM
segments.commentary: Q4 volume 34,404 containers, down 10.96% QoQ and 3.17% YoY; FY26 volume 1,40,225, up about 5% YoY. Management says the company held up better than the industry, which saw about a 40% fall in March. Growth is shifting to East Coast ports.

segments.name: Domestic
segments.commentary: Q4 volume 23,350 containers, up 17.79% YoY and down less than 1% QoQ, helped by pivots to chemicals, FMCG, aggregates and salt. FY26 volume 86,353, up 8.16% YoY.

segments.name: Devaliya MMCT (Morbi)
segments.commentary: 32-acre multimodal terminal now fully operational. Tiles throughput fell sharply in March due to propane and natural gas shortages affecting about 700 units; volumes are rising month-on-month in industrial chemicals.

guidance_outlook: Management gives no formal numerical guidance. It expects EBITDA margin to recover from about 4.6-4.7% toward roughly 7%, which it says was the FY25 level.
Management expects sequential improvement in both top line and bottom line from Q1 FY27, and says it is comfortable with the trend in May.
Management targets debtor days below 120 in FY27.
FY27 capex planned at INR100 crore, of which INR92 crore is said to be funded from remaining IPO proceeds; spend is tied to customer orders and will be calibrated to EXIM normalisation.
Management expects operating cash flow to improve as realisations and EXIM volumes recover.
capex_capacity: FY26 capex was over INR70 crore (about INR74 crore per Q&A), spent on specialised containers, reach stackers, commercial vehicles and handling equipment.
The company procured 161 specialised containers in FY26; a further order of similar size is under production and is expected to enter operations from the end of May 2026 over the next 1-1.5 quarters.
Own specialised container fleet is over 1,000 units.
Devaliya MMCT (32 acres, Morbi) is fully operational; fixed rail services run from Devaliya to CMLK, Bangalore, Chennai, Calcutta and Guwahati at lower frequency.
FY27 capex of INR100 crore covers specialised containers, commercial vehicles, reach stackers, forklifts and large cranes.
demand_pricing: Management says the order book is strong, with pedigreed customers for the rest of the year, and that the East Coast EXIM pipeline is robust.
Domestic demand for specialised containers is strong, with similar orders in the pipeline for FY27.

Industry-wide, about 40-45k Indian containers were stranded at March end; freight rates, war-risk surcharges and insurance costs rose sharply, with war-risk surcharges nearly doubling ocean freight in some cases.
Capacity on US and Europe routes is about 30-35% of normal; Cape of Good Hope diversions add about 3,500 nautical miles and 10-15 days.
Realisations were hit by geopolitical factors and are expected to improve as EXIM volumes recover.

Receivables have risen, with the company citing growth in retail MMCT customers (up 25-30% YoY) who pay only when the next consignment ships. Management said the company had INR600+ crore in receivables, a figure raised by an analyst and not disputed.

qa_highlights.question: Why did debt rise from INR172 crore to INR217 crore despite IPO net proceeds of about INR363 crore, of which about INR163 crore went to debt repayment?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the rise reflects working capital needs as the new Devaliya MMCT became operational.

qa_highlights.question: Can you give a revenue split between rail, road and water?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to split revenue, saying it operates as a consolidated multimodal logistics provider and that splitting would distort the picture.

qa_highlights.question: Why are receivables rising and when will cash flow turn positive, given negative operating cash flow in FY25 and FY26 and a planned INR100 crore capex?
qa_highlights.answer: Management targets debtor days below 120 this year, says INR100 crore of IPO funds is still unspent, and expects realisations and cash flow to improve as EXIM recovers. It said the EXIM trade should improve within the quarter.

qa_highlights.question: What further margin pressure is coming from April pricing, and when will margins recover?
qa_highlights.answer: Management did not give numerical guidance, but said margins should improve sequentially, with EBITDA margin targeted back toward 7%.

qa_highlights.question: Where will the INR100 crore capex go and what are the domestic growth drivers?
qa_highlights.answer: Capex covers specialised containers, commercial vehicles and heavy equipment. Domestic growth is expected to come from the Morbi MMLP, tiles volumes once propane supply returns, and Western seaboard clients.

qa_highlights.question: What are the drivers of the ROE/ROCE decline and the outlook for the next two years?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects ROE and ROCE to return to strong double-digit levels as margins recover from 4.6-4.7%, citing a debt position it considers under control.

risks_watch: Strait of Hormuz remains effectively closed (traffic about 5% of pre-war levels); the timing of EXIM normalisation is uncertain.
Tiles and steel demand in Morbi depends on propane and gas supply; about 700 units are affected.
Rising receivables and negative operating cash flow in FY25 and FY26, with debt up to INR217 crore.
Container detention, demurrage and empty-wagon running (15-20% vs a 5% norm) could keep costs high.
Watch whether debtor days fall below 120 and whether the Q1 FY27 EBITDA margin improves from 5.0%.
Watch the pace of FY27 capex against the INR100 crore plan and its funding.

544258|2026-09.headline: Western Carriers Q2 FY27 revenue from operations rose to Rs 449 crore from Rs 440 crore, with total TEUs up over 10% YoY.

Container volume in the quarter was 59,343 TEUs, of which 28,933 were domestic and 30,410 were EXIM, about 1,082 more than the prior quarter's 58,261. The company started operations at the GCD Yard general goods terminal at Kolkata Port in early September, with phase one fully operational and incremental volumes expected from Q3. On margins, an analyst noted the decline from high single digits to around 4-5%, and management attributed it to operational excellence efforts amid unpredictable conditions; the call did not quantify margins. 544260|2026-03.headline: Northern Arc posted record Q4FY26 PAT of INR133 crore (up 251% YoY) and FY26 PAT of INR406 crore, with AUM at INR16,594 crore (up 22% YoY).
544260|2026-03.overview: Northern Arc reported its highest-ever quarterly profit of INR133 crore in Q4FY26, taking FY26 PAT to INR406 crore (up 33% YoY). AUM grew 22% YoY and 10% QoQ to INR16,594 crore, with direct-to-customer (D2C) at 59% of AUM. Credit cost fell to 2.2% in Q4 (from 3.5% in Q3) and 2.8% for FY26, helped by the RBI's FLDG-related ECL clarification, which management said contributed a one-off benefit. Management guided FY27 AUM growth of 22-25% and ROA above 3%, with ROE in the mid-to-late teens over 8-10 quarters.

544261|2026-03.headline: Arkade posted record Q4 FY26 pre-sales of Rs 303 crore (+40% YoY), but FY26 PAT fell to Rs 5 crore after a Rs 182 crore Filmistan tenancy-rights write-off.
544261|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue rose 48% YoY to Rs 199 crore with EBITDA of Rs 38 crore (19.4% margin), and Q4 pre-sales hit a record Rs 303 crore. FY26 revenue grew 19.2% to Rs 828 crore with EBITDA of Rs 189 crore (23.2% margin), but PAT was only Rs 5 crore after a one-time exceptional item of about Rs 182 crore linked to the Filmistan tenancy rights. Management flagged the Filmistan project (GDV Rs 3,500 crore) and a Kandivali cluster redevelopment MoU (GDV Rs 1,100 crore) as the next growth drivers. On the call, management said May pre-sales were slower due to war, fuel price and global macro pressures.

544261|2026-06.headline: Arkade Q1 FY27 revenue INR 147 crore, PAT INR 19 crore (13% margin); pre-sales up 9% YoY to INR 155 crore.
544261|2026-06.overview: Revenue from operations was INR 147 crore with gross margin stable at 29.1%, while EBITDA margin fell to 18.9% (INR 28 crore) and PAT was INR 19 crore. Management attributed the YoY margin decline to lower other income (no repeat of IPO-proceeds treasury gains) and higher employee costs, with headcount rising from 213 to 277. Collections were INR 164 crore and net debt was INR 5 crore (0.01x net debt-to-equity). Management reiterated a FY27 launch plan of about INR 3,000 crore GDV and a 12,800 crore development pipeline.

financial_highlights.change: Below prior-year levels; management cited ~26-27% historically

segments.commentary: Pre-sales INR 155 crore (+9% YoY); development pipeline ~INR 12,800 crore GDV across ~4.2 million sq ft saleable carpet area. Redevelopment is a core focus.

segments.commentary: Banking assistance platform that earns commission revenue on loans, including on non-Arkade projects; management described it as profitable.

segments.commentary: Currently serves only recently completed Arkade projects; no third-party revenue disclosed.

qa_highlights.question: What pre-sales can be expected from the FY27 launches and ongoing inventory, given only about 500 crore of new-launch pre-sales is targeted?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said about INR 500 crore from new launches and about INR 500 crore from ongoing inventory (about INR 700 crore unsold as of June 30). It said FY27 pre-sales of about INR 1,000 crore is expected, and FY28 will be better with Filmistan and two other launches.

qa_highlights.question: What EBITDA margin should be modelled, given the drop from the historical 26-27% to below 20%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said gross margin is stable at about 29% and the drop is due to lower other income and higher employee costs. It expects EBITDA margin of about 25-26% over the year.

qa_highlights.question: What cash flow is expected from the portfolio?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it expects about 18-19% of PAT to convert into cash flow, and EBITDA at about 25-26%.

qa_highlights.question: Why is Anand Nagar, a top-three GDV project, not launching before FY29?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there is no delay. Approvals are constrained by a wireless station in Dahisar that limits building height; the station is to shift to Madh Marve, expected in FY27, with approvals in FY28 and launch in FY29.

qa_highlights.question: What does accelerated growth mean?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said FY27 launches of INR 3,000 crore would be roughly double the previous highest of about INR 1,500 crore in a financial year, and FY28 is planned at INR 5,000 crore-plus.

qa_highlights.question: What do Finroof and Assist360 contribute?
qa_highlights.answer: Finroof earns commission on home loans, including on non-Arkade projects, and is profitable. Assist360 currently serves only recently completed Arkade projects, and no third-party revenue was disclosed.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company need incremental debt or equity?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said outright projects are already paid for and net debt is almost nil. It may use construction finance at lower interest rates if required.

qa_highlights.question: What is the target IRR on new projects?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the target is about 20% or more, in line with historical growth.

544261|2026-09.headline: Arkade Q2 FY27 revenue fell to Rs. 145 crore with 24% EBITDA margin; pre-sales moderated to Rs. 151 crore amid no new launches.
544261|2026-09.overview: Q2 FY27 revenue from operations was Rs. 145 crore, with operating EBITDA of Rs. 35 crore (24% margin) and PAT of Rs. 25 crore (17.14% PAT margin). Management attributed the year-on-year revenue decline to a high base from four projects that started revenue recognition in the prior-year quarter after crossing 25% construction. Collections grew 22% YoY to Rs. 183 crore, but pre-sales were moderate at Rs. 151 crore, with H1 pre-sales of Rs. 306 crore. The company added four Western Mumbai redevelopment projects (about 11 acres, Rs. 5,000 crore GDV) and targets two launches worth Rs. 2,850 crore in Q3 FY27.

qa_highlights.question: What sales will the Q3 launches generate and how will they be executed?
qa_highlights.answer: Sales are planned against construction milestones over a 4-5 year project timeline, spread evenly across years; channel inquiries are good, with numbers to be released on launch.

qa_highlights.question: Reasons behind the reported delay at Arkade Rare?
qa_highlights.answer: Management disputed the delay, saying the RERA handover date was pre-poned from 28 December to 27 December.

qa_highlights.answer: Management said it has added manpower and onboarded architect, MEP, landscape consultants and execution contractors experienced in large projects.

qa_highlights.answer: Management pointed to the Bhandup MOU, a couple of other opportunities within 12 months, and said focus remains MMR; Navi Mumbai and South/North Mumbai proposals are being evaluated.

544262|2026-03.headline: Manba Finance Q4 FY26: PAT up 39% YoY to INR 11 crore; FY26 AUM INR 1,713 crore, up 29% YoY, with NIM at 13.63%.
544262|2026-03.overview: Management reported Q4 FY26 net interest income of INR 50 crore (up 34% YoY) and PAT of INR 11 crore (up 39% YoY). For FY26, NII rose 24% to INR 162 crore and PAT rose 20% to INR 45 crore, with ROE at 11.65% and ROA at 2.63%. Asset quality improved slightly QoQ, with gross Stage-3 at 3.33% and net at 2.46%, and the company raised its provision coverage. Management guided to 25-30% AUM growth, with new products (MSME LAP, used car, 3-Wheeler) and geographies (Karnataka, UP, MP) being added.

544263|2026-03.headline: KRN Heat Exchanger FY26 standalone total income rose 57.36% to Rs.689.95 crore; Q4 standalone net profit up 22.69% to Rs.16.87 crore.
544263|2026-03.overview: FY26 standalone total income grew 57.36% YoY to Rs.689.95 crore, with EBITDA up 19.41% to Rs.84.79 crore and net profit up 42.11% to Rs.71.31 crore. Consolidated FY26 total income was Rs.609.81 crore (+38.06%), EBITDA Rs.112.48 crore (+59.52%) and net profit Rs.76.47 crore (+44.62%). Q4 consolidated EBITDA rose 77.56% to Rs.33.55 crore, while Q4 standalone total income rose 55.06% to Rs.204.93 crore. Management said the new Neemrana HVAC facility is still ramping up, with working capital building in inventory and receivables, and a board-approved enabling fund raise of up to Rs.500 crore whose objective is not yet finalised.

financial_highlights.value: Around 3x YoY (per analyst question, not disputed)

segments.name: Heat exchangers (fin and tube, KRN Heat Exchanger)
segments.commentary: Management said the old facility was fully utilised in FY26; fin and tube still accounts for about 95% of revenue, with other products about 5%. Fin and tube growth expected above 80-90%, mainly from data centres.

segments.name: HVAC / new facility (KRN HVAC Products)
segments.commentary: Utilisation of the new facility was about 15% in FY26 for HVAC. Management targets 50% in FY27 and 80% in FY28 across about eight new products and new geometries.

segments.name: Data centre
segments.commentary: Data centre was about 16% of revenue in FY26 per one answer and about 18.7-19% in Q4 per another answer; management expects this to rise quarter on quarter. Top-10 customers include three data centre customers.

segments.name: Bus AC
segments.commentary: Bus AC revenue was about Rs.10 crore in FY26; management targets at least 15% market share in FY27 and has a Rs.150 crore revenue target shown in the presentation, with two to three OEMs onboarded.

segments.name: Exports
segments.commentary: Export was about Rs.100 crore in FY26 and management aims for roughly double in FY27; export order book is about Rs.120 crore including data centre orders. Geographies cited: UAE, US/North America and Europe.

segments.name: Railways / refrigeration
segments.commentary: Bar and plate heat exchanger approved by Indian Railways for field trial; company says it was L1 in three recent tenders. Full HVAC system for railways needs about 6-8 months of approvals, so limited FY27 contribution expected.

guidance_outlook: New facility utilisation targets: about 50% in FY27 and about 80% in FY28; old facility to stay fully utilised.
Management expects next eight quarters to be the highest ever, with Q4 described as an average quarter and quarter-on-quarter improvement expected.
Export to roughly double in FY27 versus about Rs.100 crore in FY26.

Margins expected to improve slightly, helped by a 5% PLI benefit in FY26, a likely RIFS state incentive of about 1.56% of top line for 10 years on the new facility, export mix and solar power savings, offset by higher depreciation and overheads.
Inventory expected to come under control within about three quarters; minimum six months to normalise per management.
Analyst cited a Rs.2,250-2,850 crore revenue target; management did not confirm the target or its timing.
capex_capacity: New Neemrana facility inaugurated 11 March 2026; production commissioning began May 2025 and the plant was shifted to fully in the week before the call.

Current facility is fully commissioned; about eight new products added, including WOT condenser, roll-bond evaporator, frost-free evaporator, skin condenser, bar and plate, dry air cooler, ammonia evaporator and bus AC, plus new fin geometries.
Further capex on existing facility is about Rs.30-40 crore over the next two years, mainly for line balancing for data centre geometry, per management's rough estimate.
Micro-channel (MCHX) product expected by end 2026 or early 2027; plate-and-plate heat exchanger (CDU) under study for next year.
Solar plant installed and operational.
demand_pricing: Raw material pass-through: management said copper LME, aluminium LME and USD-INR changes are passed to customers on a quarterly basis, with freight and logistics also passed through; it said close to 100% pass-through is possible.
UAE dispatches were disrupted in March 2026 due to the geopolitical situation; dispatches restarted in May 2026. Freight costs rose and are being passed on.
North America and Europe dispatches unaffected per management; Europe is early-stage and North America is larger than Europe for data centre exports.
Company says it competes with European and North American suppliers, not Chinese players, given customised, low-volume products.
Data centre demand: some Indian customers issue one-month firm orders on a rolling basis; one long-lead customer booked six to seven months.
Vertiv vendor approval received after QA audit; billing expected to start in coming weeks or months; Schneider Electric is the biggest domestic data centre customer.

qa_highlights.question: Are new products for liquid-cooled AI data centres in development?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said liquid cooling is early in India; fin and tube remains the core product for chillers and dry coolers, with micro-channel due by end 2026 or early 2027 and plate heat exchanger for CDUs under study.

qa_highlights.question: Can the company pass raw material costs to customers?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes, management said copper, aluminium and USD-INR movements are passed through quarter on quarter and close to 100% can be passed on under current contracts; there is a one-quarter lag.

qa_highlights.question: Why is inventory up about 3x and receivables up?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited about Rs.15-20 crore of UAE material held after March dispatch was blocked, about Rs.8 crore of export dispatched in March but not billed, minimum stock for new products, BIS-related pre-buying of inner groove tube, and new customer onboarding. Normalisation expected in about six months, with inventory days around two and a half months currently.

qa_highlights.question: Why raise equity when internal cash flow may suffice?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the IPO proceeds were exceeded by investment in the current facility and working capital will be short; the board approved an enabling resolution up to Rs.500 crore, with objectives not yet concluded. Bank funding is also an option.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Q4 revenue share from products other than fin and tube?
qa_highlights.answer: Management did not have the figure on the call; it said non-fin-and-tube business is about 5% of revenue overall.

qa_highlights.question: Is the bus AC Rs.150 crore target backed by orders?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said two to three OEMs have been onboarded and regular supply has started, with about 15% market share targeted; no specific Rs.150 crore order book was quantified.

risks_watch: Working capital and receivables build-up; inventory normalisation timeline (about six months) and the Rs.500 crore equity raise, whose use is unconfirmed.
BIS certification issue on inner groove tube (deadline around 20-28 May 2026) could drive imports and inventory build-up.
Copper and aluminium price volatility in recent weeks, which management said is beyond expectation; pass-through has a one-quarter lag.
Geopolitical disruption to UAE dispatches and freight costs.
Ramp-up pace of the new facility versus 50%/80% utilisation targets; Q4 incremental revenue from the new facility was about Rs.15-16 crore per an analyst's estimate.
Concentration of data centre revenue (about 16-19%) and dependence on a few large customers such as Schneider Electric.
Depreciation and overhead rising ahead of revenue.
544263|2026-03.management_tone: Confident on growth, data centre demand and utilisation targets, but evasive on the Rs.500 crore fund raise, the Rs.120 crore UAE order, the Q4 non-fin-and-tube share and the specific data centre order book. Several answers were vague or deferred to later updates.

So, now we have eight new businesses, so that is also we have to build the inventory.
Of course, slight improvement will be there, but honestly in the last two, three weeks in this copper and aluminum silver price is beyond the expectation because they sharply increase.

544264|2026-03.headline: Diffusion Engineers Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue rose 38.08% YoY to INR1,415.74 million, with FY27 revenue growth guided above 20%.
544264|2026-03.overview: Consolidated Q4 FY26 revenue was INR1,415.74 million (+38.08% YoY) and EBITDA excluding other income was INR206.89 million (+39.96%), at a 14.61% margin. Consolidated FY26 revenue was INR4,066.28 million (+21.28%) with PAT of INR504.1 million (+39.87%). Standalone growth was weaker: Q4 revenue +12.18% and Q4 PAT down 3.05%, which management attributed to capacity constraints in wear plates, wear parts and heavy engineering running at about 85-90% utilisation. Order book stood at about INR200 crores as of 30 April 2026, up from about INR100 crores a year earlier. New Unit 4 capacity is being commissioned from Q1 FY27 onward.

segments.name: Welding consumables (products)
segments.commentary: Management cited roughly 30% of revenue; under 3% (said 2-3%) of the business is conventional, with the rest special hard-facing and repair electrodes. Wires line at 85-90% utilisation; new wire line expected July 2026.

segments.name: Wear plates, wear parts and heavy engineering
segments.commentary: Cited at roughly 30% of revenue combined with heavy engineering; running at 85-90% utilisation, and expected to grow faster than consumables. Roller-press rolls, steel mill rollers and VRM rollers are cited as growth areas; first VRM order won.

segments.name: Services
segments.commentary: Roughly 10% of revenue per management. Covers on-site breakdown repair, hot kiln alignment and bulk deposition, with about 50-60 welding technicians deployed. UAE subsidiary set up for service and overlay work is now operational and expected to contribute from FY27.

segments.name: Railways (developmental)
segments.commentary: L1 in multiple contracts and some letters of intent received for Vande Bharat ecosystem components; execution 6-9 months, with substantial revenue expected from next year at likely lower initial margins.

segments.name: Defence (Tejorup Sunmay Systems)
segments.commentary: Investment made in February 2026 for VSHORADS work; still in prototype stage with a DRDO sanction order for 200 launchers and 1,200 rockets. No revenue expected in FY26 or in FY27 in any significant amount.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth expected to be more than 20%, supported by capacity additions, order inflows and higher-margin engineered products.
FY27 EBITDA margin expected to rise by about 80-100 basis points, aided by operating leverage and cost consolidation; gross margin may come under pressure from raw material volatility.
Medium-term aspiration of INR650 crore-plus revenue at 15-16% EBITDA margin, expected to be reached in under 3 years (2-3 years on annual run-rate basis).

Capex of about INR100 crores from IPO proceeds (INR70 crores for wear part/plate/heavy engineering, INR30 crores for electrode and slitting facility) is expected to support INR800-900 crores revenue; no additional capex planned for INR650 crores.
Debtor days targeted at 80-85 for FY27 and inventory days at 60-65; FY26 debtor days were 98 and inventory days 66.
International revenue share expected to rise to about 15%, with international sales growing above 20%.
capex_capacity: New 10 tons-per-day electrode plant commissioned around November-December 2025, along with an in-house strip-slitting line for flux-cored wires.
Wear plate capacity expanded by about 25% and now commissioned.

Unit 4 (about 170,000-180,000 sq ft) for wear plates, wear parts and heavy engineering: partial utilisation from May 2026, most capacity live by end of Q1 FY27 (quarter ending June 2026), with the facility expected to be fully commissioned by end of Q1 2027 per management.
Current utilisation: wires about 85-90%; wear plates and heavy engineering about 85-90%. Management expects utilisation to fall to roughly 50-60% once new shop floors are live.
New wire line expected to be delivered in July 2026.
demand_pricing: Order book about INR200 crores as of 30 April 2026, up from about INR100 crores on 31 March 2025; management expects 80-90% to execute in FY27, with staggered power-project deliveries extending beyond.
Over 80% of revenue from repeat customers; end-market demand from cement, steel, power, mining and engineering described as steady, with no project holds despite the West Asia crisis.

Raw material volatility (tungsten, nickel, cobalt, molybdenum, chromium) is affecting margins; price variation clauses cover under 10% of the order book, with the rest fixed-price contracts. Management books raw materials on order and gives short offer validity on volatile items.
Price increases are ongoing, linked to input costs; management says customers are aware of raw material conditions.

Exports reach more than 35 countries including Southeast Asia, Middle East and Africa; Turkey operations are maturing, a new West Africa partner has been identified, and Singapore sales rose significantly in FY26.
Competitors named: Ador Fontech (merged into Ador Welding) and EWAC Alloys (now part of ESAB) in welding consumables and wear plates; ThyssenKrupp, ISGEC and Walchandnagar in heavy engineering.

qa_highlights.question: Why is standalone growth flat relative to consolidated, and will it normalise in FY27-28?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said standalone plants were already at about 85% utilisation, capping execution in wear plates, wear parts and heavy engineering; new capacity from Q1 FY27 should lift standalone growth to match consolidated.

qa_highlights.question: What is the EBITDA margin volatility (13% to 14.8%) driven by?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed it mainly to raw material price lags on fixed-price contracts; gross margin may fall, but fixed and operating costs have been consolidated, so net margins improved with scale.

qa_highlights.question: How is the debtor-day gap versus Ador Fontech explained?
qa_highlights.answer: Debtors are at 98 days for FY26 due to large heavy-engineering shipments in March (about INR140 crores of Q4 sales, including roughly INR20 crores of rollers). Target is 80-85 days for FY27; welding consumables are cash-and-carry; heavy engineering is typically 60 days contractually but extends to 75-90 days in practice.

qa_highlights.question: Will the INR650 crore revenue target be reached faster, with growth accelerating above 20%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects growth to rise as new facilities come online and expects INR650 crores in 2-3 years on run-rate basis; no additional capex is needed for that level, and INR100 crores of capex could support INR800-900 crores.

qa_highlights.question: When will railway and defence businesses contribute meaningful revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: Railway developmental orders take 6-9 months to execute, with substantial revenue from next year after approved-vendor listing. Tejorup defence revenue is not expected in FY26 or significantly in FY27, pending prototype approval.

qa_highlights.question: What is the revenue contribution from new products such as steel mill rollers and VRM rollers?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to quantify, citing confidentiality; said steel mill roller revenue was significant last year, a first VRM order has been won, and shredder spare parts are under development.

risks_watch: Raw material volatility (tungsten, cobalt, nickel) on fixed-price contracts; gross margin pressure in FY27 with a lag in passing through costs.
Standalone profitability: Q4 standalone PAT fell 3.05% YoY despite revenue growth, and standalone growth depends on Unit 4 commissioning on schedule by end of Q1 2027.
Receivable days at 98 in FY26 with heavy-engineering payment cycles of 75-90 days; management's 80-85 target needs to be met.
Quarterly concentration: Q4 is seasonally large, and management expects Q4 to remain the biggest quarter.
Tejorup defence and railway developmental businesses carry lower initial margins and long gestation periods.
Management's stated 20%+ FY27 growth and 80-100 bps margin expansion are to be tracked against Q1 FY27 results.

544264|2026-06.headline: Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 36.5% YoY to INR1,101.08 million, with order book up 20.4% QoQ to INR209 crores.
544264|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue grew 36.5% YoY to INR1,101.08 million, with EBITDA excluding other income up 33.76% to INR141.54 million. The order book reached INR209 crores at 30 June 2026, with more than 80% stated as executable in FY27, and a ~INR100 crore capacity expansion is coming on stream in phases at Nagpur.

segments.commentary: Order book of INR26.42 crores. Management said growth in Q1 came across consumables, wear plates/parts and heavy engineering.

segments.name: Welding Consumables
segments.commentary: Order book of INR24.22 crores, described as a strong sequential increase driven by customers consolidating yearly requirements. Management said there was no one-off windfall.

segments.name: Defence

segments.name: Exports / International

qa_highlights.question: Why did standalone margin fall from ~18% peak to ~13%, and is Q1 the bottom?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said Q1 FY26 standalone PAT included a one-time ~INR5 crore subsidiary dividend. Management expects margins to return to prior-year Q1 levels and rise 100-200 bps over the next 1-1.5 years.

544264|2026-09.headline: Diffusion Engineers Q4 FY25 revenue rose 38.55% YoY to INR1,024.48 million; FY25 revenue INR3,351.96 million, up 20.51%.
544264|2026-09.overview: Q4 FY25 was the company's first earnings call after its October 2024 listing. Revenue grew 38.55% YoY to INR1,024.48 million, with EBITDA (ex other income) up 82.55% to INR147.01 million and margin up 346 bps to 14.35%. FY25 revenue rose 20.51% to INR3,351.96 million, EBITDA ex other income rose 21.12% to INR470.76 million, and PAT rose 17% to INR360.40 million. Management is roughly doubling capacity with a INR100 crore capex programme, with the new capacity targeted by end FY26 and utilisation currently around 85%.

segments.commentary: One of three equal-weight baskets; management says growth in FY25 was strong, alongside heavy engineering. Serves close to 1,000 customers. Replacement cycle is 18-24 months.

segments.name: Welding and anti-wear consumables
segments.commentary: One of three equal-weight baskets, said to carry higher margins than wear plates and heavy engineering, but grew more slowly in FY25. Flux core wire is ~7% of turnover and cold repair compounds ~3%.

segments.name: Services and rental
segments.commentary: Industrial services (on-site breakdown repair, kiln alignment) are ~1-2% of revenue. A new wear-part rental model has two ongoing contracts, already fully paid, with NBFC lease tie-ups planned.

Management aims to grow faster than the market and to improve margins; no forward revenue numbers given.
ROCE is about 15% at present, with an aspiration to match or beat pre-IPO levels.
Working capital to stay around 90-100 days given 6-9 month heavy equipment cycles and 90-100 day payment terms.
Planned 1.1 MW captive rooftop solar on the Nimji unit, funded from IPO objects.

Unit 4 has started flux-coated wire and wear plate production.
demand_pricing: Revenue growth attributed to timely execution of high-value orders and demand from cement, steel, power and engineering, with growth across all sectors.

Around 23-25% of revenue goes through OEMs; the rest is direct to end clients, with a small channel-partner share.
Exports were 12-13% of FY25 revenue, down from 13-14% in FY24, though absolute exports are rising. Export margins are higher due to less competition.

Customers are moving to ready-to-fit and complete solutions rather than buying consumables themselves.

544274|2026-09.headline: Hyundai India Q2 FY27 revenue hit a record ₹20,696 Mn (+18.5% YoY), but EBITDA margin fell to 9.5% from 13.9% on commodity headwinds.
544274|2026-09.overview: Domestic volumes rose 18.8% YoY to 165,772 units and total sales hit a record 219,072 units, with exports up 3.7% YoY and 38% QoQ. Revenue reached a record ₹206,961 Mn, but raw material inflation of roughly 400 bps YoY and 250 bps QoQ compressed EBITDA to ₹19,745 Mn and PAT to ₹11,962 Mn (5.7% margin vs 8.9%). Management guided to 8-10% domestic growth and high-double-digit export growth in H2, and a sequential margin recovery toward an 11% full-year EBITDA margin. Bayon launched two days before the call and a dedicated mass-market EV is slated for early CY27.

segments.name: Exports
segments.commentary: Volume up 3.7% YoY and 38% QoQ, 24% of total volume. Q2 mix: Middle East and Africa 52% (Middle East 34%, Africa 18%), Latin America 26%, Mexico 20%.

Export interest from about 50 countries for Bayon (about 34 in Latin America, 14-15 in Middle East).

qa_highlights.answer: H2 high-double-digit export growth is supported by demand, new products (Venue volumes to at least double, Exter at least 50% growth), new markets like Mexico, and alternate Middle East routes and ports with logistics partners.

qa_highlights.question: Demand outlook for H2 and rural trends?
qa_highlights.answer: Demand described as very strong; dealers asking for more cars. Rural remains strong and expected to outpace urban; no major El Nino impact seen so far.

qa_highlights.question: Creta volume outlook and export contribution from Bayon?
qa_highlights.answer: Creta expected at about 170,000 this year. About 50 countries have shown interest in Bayon exports; more clarity expected by the next quarter.

qa_highlights.question: How will H2 EBITDA margin reach the guided level?
qa_highlights.answer: Drivers: Tamil Nadu incentive (over 1% in Q3 and Q4), higher-margin exports, possible raw material softening after US mid-term elections, September and January price hikes, Chennai utilisation recovery, and third-shift fixed-cost leverage.

544277|2026-03.headline: Waaree FY26 revenue rose ~84% to INR26,537 crore and operating EBITDA 117% to INR5,909 crore, but Q4 margin fell to ~18.6% on commodity, freight and mix pressures.
544277|2026-03.overview: FY26 was a record year: revenue from operations of INR26,537 crore (+84% YoY), operating EBITDA of INR5,909 crore (22.27% margin vs 18.84%) and PAT of INR3,884 crore (+101%). Q4 revenue was INR8,480 crore (+111% YoY) and operating EBITDA INR1,576 crore, with margin down sharply from the prior quarter as silver and copper costs, freight spikes, lower overseas mix and in-house DCR cell shortfall weighed. Management guided FY27 operating EBITDA to INR7,000-7,700 crore and framed the Waaree 2.0 capex (~$3.5 billion) as the driver, with most cell and module capex completing in FY27 and benefits from H2 FY27 onward. Operating cash conversion fell to about 27% as export shipments were stuck on logistics delays and inventory built up.

segments.name: Module manufacturing
segments.commentary: FY26 production 12.6 GW (+77%), sales about 12 GW; Q4 production 4.2 GW (+104% YoY) and Q4 sales 4.1 GW. Capacity ~26 GW, described as the largest non-Chinese module maker.

segments.name: Cell manufacturing
segments.commentary: Operational cell capacity 5.4 GW (largest in India); Q4 cell production 0.7 GW. A 10 GW cell facility is due in H2 FY27, taking cell capacity to ~15.4 GW.

segments.name: Revenue mix (FY26)
segments.commentary: Utility/IPP/C&I 34.7%, overseas 33%, retail 20.8%, EPC 11.6%. Retail revenue INR5,515 crore (+84%). Q4 overseas share fell to ~21% from ~32% in Q3.

segments.name: US manufacturing
segments.commentary: 1.6 GW plant ramped; 2.6 GW more to go live within six months, taking US capacity to 4.2 GW. IRA benefit ~$0.07/Wp, ~$40 million in FY26, to rise with new capacity.

segments.name: Order book
segments.commentary: ~INR53,000 crore excluding retail (~20% of revenue), up from ~INR47,000 crore a year ago but down ~INR7,000 crore QoQ per analyst. ~65-70% is overseas, to be delivered over 3-4 years. More than INR8,400 crore delivered already.

guidance_outlook: FY27 operating EBITDA guided at INR7,000-7,700 crore (about 20-25% growth on FY26 INR5,909 crore).
Management says the margin benefit from in-house DCR cells starts in H2 FY27 when the 10 GW cell line goes live; H1 is a transition.
Long-range planning assumption: 19-20% EBITDA margin sustained for a decade.
Cell utilisation assumed 80-85% for FY28 on 15.4 GW capacity; 28 GW modules, 4 GW inverters, 20,000 MVA transformers and 1 GW electrolyser to run at full throttle in FY28.
Capex of ~$3.5 billion (INR30,000 crore) over the next two years; core module and cell capex complete in FY27, ingot wafer and part of battery in FY28; full Waaree 2.0 benefits seen in FY29.
Cell line transition from M10R to G12R expected to lift output and realisation by 10-12% within about a quarter; module output back to ~330 MW a month within two months.
Investor Day to be held; enabling board resolution for fundraise of up to ~INR10,000 crore approved, with shareholder approval to follow.
capex_capacity: Battery (BESS): 20 GWh planned, phase 1 of 3.5 GWh in FY27 (Gujarat), phase 2 of 16.5 GWh in FY28; capex ~INR10,000 crore.
Ingot wafer: 10 GW at Nagpur, capex ~INR6,200 crore (up from INR5,100 crore earlier with 6 GW to 10 GW); completion FY28.
PV glass: 2,500 TPD approved at ~INR3,900 crore capex, production expected within 24 months; supports ~16-17 GW of modules.
Inverters: 4 GW at Sarodhi, Gujarat (~INR180 crore); 3 GW commissioned, remaining 1 GW in FY27.
Transformers: current ~4,000 MVA; adding 16,000 MVA to reach 20,000 MVA at Alwar (~INR192 crore) in FY27.
Hydrogen: 1 GW electrolyser at Dungri, Gujarat (~INR676 crore capex); electrolyser PLI INR444 crore and hydrogen PLI ~INR510 crore.
Acquired ~55% of Associated Power Structures Ltd (APSL) for ~INR1,225 crore for T&D entry; Oman polysilicon stake acquired for non-Chinese supply.
Module lines: 3 lines converted to G12R (ramping), 3 lines remain Mono PERC, 5 lines still on M10R TOPCon, to convert over about one quarter.
demand_pricing: Domestic DCR module pricing INR21-22/Wp; non-DCR utility INR15-16/Wp, with retail carrying a premium; commodity increases are being passed through to new orders.
Silver and copper cost increases, freight spikes and a lower overseas share weighed on Q4 margin; management said customers are now accepting the higher commodity-linked prices.
ALMM-II (domestic cell mandate) takes effect June 2026; C&I and mid-market decisions were deferred pending clarity, which slowed local offtake.
India installed 44.6 GW of solar in FY26; module consumption was about 50-55 GW. Management sees DCR-compliant cell capacity at ~30 GW for ALMM-II.
US FEOC rules from April 2026 require non-Chinese cells and components, which management says is driving new US orders.
BESS pricing around $110-120/MWh cited for India and US; BESS margin guided at 18-20% before policy support.

qa_highlights.question: Why did operating EBITDA margin fall sharply QoQ, and what are the DCR and non-DCR realisations?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited silver and copper cost spikes, freight cost surge, a lower overseas mix and DCR cell shortfall. DCR modules INR21-22/Wp; utility non-DCR INR15-16/Wp, with a retail premium.

qa_highlights.question: Why was the export mix low in Q4 and what is the order book composition?
qa_highlights.answer: Export shipments were stuck on Middle East logistics delays, so inventory rose. About 65-70% of the INR53,000 crore order book is overseas, delivered over 3-4 years; retail (~20% of revenue) is excluded.

qa_highlights.question: How will the FY27 EBITDA guidance of INR7,000-7,700 crore be achieved, and what drives margin?
qa_highlights.answer: H1 is a transition from 5.4 GW to 15.4 GW of cells; the 10 GW cell line in H2 lifts in-house DCR supply. Pre-startup costs for new projects are included in guidance.

qa_highlights.question: Why did the ingot-wafer capex rise and its timeline move to FY28?
qa_highlights.answer: Capacity was raised from 6 GW to 10 GW and sites moved from Odisha to Gujarat and Nagpur, causing the delay. The new figure covers the full 10 GW.

qa_highlights.question: What is the cash conversion cycle and working capital outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Inventory built up because overseas shipments were delayed. Customer advances stayed steady but production nearly doubled, diluting working capital days. Management expects cash conversion of 70-100% at normalised inventory.

qa_highlights.question: What are the BESS unit economics and FY29 revenue contribution?
qa_highlights.answer: BESS margin guided at 18-20% without policy support. Management declined to give FY29 revenue guidance, pointing to the 20 GWh capacity and $110-120/MWh pricing.

risks_watch: Margin recovery depends on the 10 GW cell line commissioning in H2 FY27 and on the G12R ramp; Q4 showed sharp margin compression.
Working capital and cash conversion (~27%) need to normalise as stuck export inventory ships.
ALMM-II timing uncertainty is deferring C&I and mid-market orders; order book fell ~INR7,000 crore QoQ.
Commodity (silver, copper) and freight volatility; pricing pass-through to new orders is unproven.
Execution risk on ~$3.5 billion capex across BESS, glass, ingot-wafer and US plants, plus fundraise of up to INR10,000 crore.
Overcapacity concerns in the module sector; management argues demand and supply balance once ALMM-II/III take effect.

Several answers on BESS economics, the fundraise, Indosolar and ALMM-II timing were deferred or left unquantified.

financial_highlights.change: Above prior guidance of INR5,500-6,000 crore
+70% YoY; margin fell sharply QoQ (analyst cited ~590 bps decline)
vs INR644 crore in Q4 FY25
Down from over 100% in prior period per analyst; management says 70-100% normalised

The safest assumption there will be is your 19 %-20% margin consistent for a decade long at least.
So, we really don't foresee any scenario anytime next 5, 10 years of time will be the supply is going to be much higher than demand.
So, if you keep the inventory at normalized levels, the same number will go back to the normalized level of 70% to 100% conversion of cash from current 27%.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: FY27 operating EBITDA guided at INR7,000-7,700 crore (20-25% growth on INR5,909 crore) with margin benefit from the 10 GW cell line in H2 FY27, though Q4 margin fell to ~18.6% and H1 FY27 is flagged as a transition.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: FY26 module production rose 77% to 12.6 GW and Q4 production hit 4.2 GW (+104% YoY), with cell utilisation assumed at 80-85% for FY28 on 15.4 GW, though Q4 cell output was only 0.7 GW and C&I orders are deferred by ALMM-II timing.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.when: already under way; ingot wafer FY28, BESS phase 2 FY28

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: FY26 EBITDA of INR6,617 crore beat the INR5,500-6,000 crore guide, but FY27 guidance of INR7,000-7,700 crore is new and management flagged H1 FY27 as a transition with Q4 margin compression.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade

rows.label: Cell line transition M10R to G12R lifts output and realisation 10-12%
rows.why: Three module lines are already converted to G12R and five lines still on M10R TOPCon are due to convert over about one quarter, with management citing a 10-12% lift in output and realisation.

rows.label: Cash conversion normalises to 70-100%
rows.why: Operating cash conversion fell to about 27% as export shipments were held up by Middle East logistics delays, and management expects 70-100% at normalised inventory, but this is unquantified on timing.

rows.label: US FEOC rules driving new US orders

tone.note: Management was confident on the Waaree 2.0 story, FY26 results and FY27 EBITDA guidance, but defensive on the Q4 margin drop, ~27% cash conversion and the QoQ order-book decline; analysts pushed on margins, working capital and deferred BESS and ALMM-II answers.

544277|2026-06.headline: Waaree Q1 FY27 revenue rose 79.2% YoY to INR7,932 crore and order book hit a record INR61,500 crore, though operating EBITDA margin was 18.2%.
544277|2026-06.overview: Revenue from operations grew 79.2% YoY to about INR7,932 crore, with operating EBITDA up 44.4% to about INR1,440 crore at an 18.2% margin and PAT of INR892 crore (11% margin, up 15.4%). Management attributed margin pressure to higher global raw material costs, softer US exports from delayed clearances, and inventory built ahead of second-half-weighted dispatches. Order book rose to INR61,500 crore after INR16,000 crore of net inflows against about INR7,300 crore executed. Management reaffirmed FY27 operating EBITDA guidance of INR7,000-7,700 crore, pinning the margin recovery on rising captive cell integration and US local manufacturing.

segments.name: Revenue mix
segments.commentary: Utility IPP and C&I 39.7%, retail 30.2%, overseas 21.2%, EPC and O&M 8.9% of Q1 FY27 revenue. Utility/IPP/C&I share was 52.1% in FY25.

segments.name: Retail (B2C)
segments.commentary: Revenue of INR2,289 crore, up 130% YoY; management guides INR9,000-10,000 crore for FY27.

segments.name: Overseas / US
segments.commentary: US domestic revenue INR1,322 crore and direct exports INR287 crore. US plant produced about 230 MW in Q1, earning roughly USD12-13 million of IRA incentives.

segments.name: Cell manufacturing (India)
segments.commentary: 5.4 GW capacity at 62% utilisation; about 800 MW of DCR cell made in Q1. Integrated cell lines show 35-40% margin per management.

segments.name: Modules (India and US)
segments.commentary: India module capacity 24.2 GW at about 50% annualised utilisation; US module capacity 1.6 GW at about 59%. Management expects US utilisation of 75-80% in coming quarters.

segments.name: BESS / storage
segments.commentary: Automated BESS container capacity of 5.15 GWh started, versus 3.5 GWh originally planned. A 1,520 MWh BESS EPC order was won.

segments.name: Transmission and transformers
segments.commentary: Waaree Transpower began commercial production of a 17.6 MVA inverter-duty transformer. WRTL acquired about 55% of Associated Power Structures for about INR1,225 crore.

guidance_outlook: FY27 operating EBITDA guidance of INR7,000-7,700 crore reaffirmed.
FY28 ballpark of about INR7,000 crore EBITDA mentioned by Varun Goenka; FY28 expected to see about 16-18 GW module and about 10 GW cell production.
Cell-to-module integration ratio to rise from about 20% to about 65% within 2-3 quarters.
Cell production to rise from about 800 MW in Q1 to about 1.2 GW in Q2 and about 1.5 GW in Q3.
Module utilisation to reach 70-75% in Q3 and Q4; management expects 80-85% over 2-3 quarters as integration rises.
US IRA incentive receipts expected quarterly from Q3-Q4 FY27 via refund or sale of credits; US production of 400-500 MW per quarter from Q3.
Management aspires to a near INR1 lakh crore revenue vision in less than 4-5 years.
capex_capacity: Announced capex programme about INR31,500 crore; about INR9,450 crore deployed as of 30 June. Phasing is about 30% in FY27, 40% in FY28 and 30% in FY29.

FY27 additions: 2.6 GW US modules, 10 GW Indian cell (Gujarat, ALMM-II applied, equipment on site, commercial start expected from about Q3), 100 KTPA T&D EPC, 20 GVA transformers, 4 GW inverters, 1 GW electrolysers.
FY28: 10 GW ingot and wafer at Nagpur, construction started. FY29: 2,500 TPD solar glass (about INR3,900 crore, greenfield approved) and 16.5 GWh BESS plant.
Indian cell capacity to reach 15.4 GW against 24.2 GW module capacity by FY27-end; US BESS cell 3.5 GWh to commission within FY27, with 95% site construction done.
Potential QIP of about INR10,000 crore approved by Board and shareholders; timing depends on market conditions.
demand_pricing: Order book INR61,500 crore as of 28 July 2026 (25.2 GW), up from about INR53,000 crore at FY26-end; geographic mix India about 40%, US about 36%, exports about 24%.
Realisations per watt: exports USD0.25-0.26; DCR USD0.20-0.25; non-DCR USD0.13-0.14. Order book realisations seen at USD0.24-0.25 for near quarters; long-range DCR orders at USD0.21-0.22.
Non-DCR offtake delayed by developers in Q1; ALMM-II effective 1 June with about a 5-6 month window, leading to expected offtake from Q2.
Top 5 customers 27.1% of sales (from 33% in FY26); top 10 at 37.1% (from 47%).
Imported cell about USD0.04-0.045/W versus Indian manufacturing cost of USD0.07-0.08/W; DCR market price about USD0.12-0.13/W.
US market had about six months of installation lull due to tariff uncertainty; management reports recent order and enquiry pickup, including data-centre demand.

qa_highlights.question: What is the expansion timeline for 10 GW cell and wafer and battery capacity over FY28-FY29?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects about 28 GW modules, 15.4 GW cells, 4 GW inverters and 20 GVA transformers by FY27-end; FY28 to see about 16-18 GW modules and about 10 GW cell output. The 10 GW Indian cell facility adds from Q3.

qa_highlights.question: Why did module gross margin fall, and what are the recovery levers?
qa_highlights.answer: Lower IRA realisation in Q1 because US dispatches came from OEM manufacturing; delayed non-DCR offtake; softer exports. Levers are DCR cell output, US local scaling, exports from August, and non-DCR offtake over the six-month window.

qa_highlights.question: How are US export and US local manufacturing margins structured?
qa_highlights.answer: Exports from India earn about USD0.04-0.05/W EBITDA. US local manufacturing nets about USD0.055-0.06/W after expenses, with IRA incentive of USD0.07/W. Management guides total US local realisation and EBITDA at USD0.07-0.08/W, helped by a USD0.01-0.02/W cut in US conversion cost.

qa_highlights.question: Is there a lower-cost import option for cells compared with domestic manufacturing?
qa_highlights.answer: Imported cell is about USD0.04-0.045/W against Indian manufacturing cost of USD0.07-0.08/W and DCR market price of USD0.12-0.13/W.

qa_highlights.question: What is the BESS volume and earnings outlook for FY27-FY28?
qa_highlights.answer: The 5.15 GWh container line is live and order book is building. The 3.5 GWh BESS cell line is due to start commercially in FY27. FEOC-compliant cell realisations are about 25-30% above Chinese pricing, with non-FEOC at USD75-80/kWh versus Chinese USD50-55/kWh.

qa_highlights.question: What is the QIP plan and funding need?
qa_highlights.answer: Board and shareholders approved about INR10,000 crore of fundraising including equity. Management says FY27 EBITDA is broadly sufficient to fund the capex and it will wait for the right market window. Balance capex is about INR22,000 crore over three years.

risks_watch: Gross margin pressure from raw material inflation and a lower IRA realisation mix in Q1; watch whether 18.2% operating EBITDA margin recovers toward the FY27 guidance band.
Second-half weighted order book and inventory build; utilisation of India modules around 50% annualised in Q1 versus a 70-75% target for Q3-Q4.
Timing of the 10 GW Indian cell commissioning (targeted by December) and ALMM-II extension window; the non-DCR offtake ramp is unconfirmed.
US export clearance delays and the start of US local line output from August; US IRA incentive monetisation timing.
Capex execution across INR31,500 crore programme and the glass capex decision, with an update promised in about one quarter.
Pending QIP and funding plan; BESS Make-in-India incentive is not yet announced.

Management repeatedly tied recovery to specific dated levers and reaffirmed guidance. Responses on glass capex, BESS incentives and QIP timing were less specific.
key_quotes: Our order book stands at approximately INR61,500 crores, the highest in our history, up from INR50,000 crores just a quarter ago, with about INR16,000 crores in new orders won in this quarter alone.
Our cell-to-module integration ratio is going to rise from roughly around 20% currently to around 65% in next two to three quarters, close to a threefold increase.
It is on this trend that we affirm and reaffirm our 2027 operating EBITDA guidance, what we have stated in our last call.

net cash balance sheet as of 30 June
