544277|2026-09.headline: Waaree Q2 FY27 revenue rose 23.9% YoY to Rs 7,517.7 crore, with operating EBITDA of Rs 1,335.2 crore (17.8% margin); FY27 EBITDA guidance of Rs 7,000-7,700 crore reaffirmed.
544277|2026-09.overview: Q2 FY27 revenue was Rs 7,517.7 crore (up 23.9% YoY) with operating EBITDA of Rs 1,335.2 crore and PAT of Rs 753.6 crore. H1 revenue rose 47.3% to Rs 15,449.5 crore, but H1 PAT was flat at Rs 1,645.5 crore versus Rs 1,651.1 crore a year earlier. Management said the US export order book was rationalised after Section 232 minimum import prices, cutting export share of the order book from about 24% to 7.8%, while retail and US-manufactured volumes grew. Management reaffirmed FY27 operating EBITDA guidance and expects H2 to deliver 55-60% of it, driven by cell and US capacity ramp-ups.

financial_highlights.change: Q1 margin was 18.2% per analyst; Q1 included US duty refund

financial_highlights.value: about Rs 3,464 crore, 46.1% of Q2 revenue

financial_highlights.change: vs Rs 2,875 crore a year ago

financial_highlights.value: about Rs 59,200 crore; module order book 25.6 GW
financial_highlights.change: geography: 48.4% domestic India, 43.8% domestic US, 7.8% exports

segments.name: Retail / cash-and-carry (India)
segments.commentary: Q2 retail revenue about Rs 3,464 crore (46.1% of Q2 revenue), up 252% YoY; 775+ exclusive retail centres and about 3,000 distribution points. FY27 retail revenue guided at Rs 10,000-11,000 crore; over 92% of retail revenue is modules.

segments.name: Utility, IPP, C&I
segments.commentary: Contributed about 22.9% of Q2 revenue.

segments.name: Overseas
segments.commentary: 18.5% of Q2 revenue (Rs 1,389 crore vs Rs 2,875 crore a year ago). Within it, US domestic revenue rose to Rs 1,300 crore from Rs 732 crore; exports from India fell to Rs 89 crore from Rs 2,143 crore.

segments.name: EPC, O&M, T&D, others
segments.commentary: Combined 12.6% of Q2 revenue. T&D acquisition sits under the listed subsidiary, which runs a blended EBITDA margin of about 14-15%.

segments.name: US manufacturing
segments.commentary: Domestic US manufacturing revenue up 113% YoY in H1 FY27; US module output reached 0.3 GW in the period at 71% annualised utilisation. Q2 US supply about 400 MW, of which about 300 MW self-manufactured.

guidance_outlook: FY27 operating EBITDA guidance reaffirmed at Rs 7,000-7,700 crore; H1 was about Rs 2,775 crore, so H2 needs about 55-60% of the guided total per management.
Q3 and Q4 volumes expected to be heavy, with 5 GW of Indian cell capacity going live in Q3 and another 5 GW in Q4.
US 1.6 GW module line to become operational in Q3 FY27; a second 1.6 GW line in the next quarter, taking Waaree Solar Americas to 4.8 GW.
Retail revenue guided at Rs 10,000-11,000 crore for FY27.
Newer businesses (BESS, transformers, inverters, T&D, EPC, electrolysers) expected to rise from 15-20% of revenue to 30-35% over 2-3 years; long-range solar 50-60% of revenue.
Management's ambition is Rs 90,000-1 lakh crore revenue over 4-5 years (about 20 GW module output at 75% utilisation plus non-solar businesses); no timeline firmly committed.
capex_capacity: Capex programme about Rs 30,000 crore: 35% deployed, 28% under execution, 37% in planning. Management says cash balance covers under-construction projects without new borrowing.
Installed module capacity 25.8 GW, including 1.6 GW in the US; India cell capacity 5.4 GW rising to 15.4 GW with the 10 GW Unn expansion (cell-to-module ratio from about 22% to about 65%).

Ingot-wafer: 10 GW facility at Nagpur, commercial production targeted September 2027; capex about Rs 5,500 crore per management (analyst cited Rs 6,200-6,500 crore). Ingot-wafer civil works about 70% complete.

BESS: 5.1 GWh container and 5.1 GWh pack Phase 1 (container commissioned in Q2; pack expected in Q3; 3.5 GWh cell pilot from Q4 FY27). Phase 2 (16.5 GWh cell, 15 GWh container) is in planning; funding tied to policy clarity and overseas orders.

Inverter capacity 4 GW (production started); transformer capacity 20,000 MVA with incremental capacity by March 2027; electrolyser capacity also coming. Combined committed capital about Rs 1,200 crore.
Solar glass: about Rs 3,900 crore budget, about Rs 360 crore spent (land, filling, EOP); location near Navsari, Gujarat; go-live targeted FY29; technology partner talks ongoing.
Renewable power infrastructure: about Rs 3,250 crore committed; about 10 GW of grid connectivity, about 2 GW of PPAs (including 700 MW SECI FDRE), 25,000-30,000 acres of land under procurement.
demand_pricing: US pricing reset under Section 232: minimum import price of 38 cents/W plus 15% duty (about 44 cents landed) versus 27-28 cents landed today; realisation on US-made modules expected to rise from 26-27 cents toward 30-35 cents.

US-manufactured margin estimated at 8-9 cents/W at 70%+ utilisation (incl. about 7 cents/W incentive) versus about 3-4 cents/W EBITDA on exports from India; IRA incentives booked against dispatches and some sold.

India DCR module spot prices: utility 19-21 cents/W, retail 22-24 cents/W; forward FY28 prices 17.5-18.5 cents (utility) and 20-21 cents (retail). Non-DCR utility about 12-12.5 cents, retail 13.5-14 cents.
Management expects broad price correction in FY28 as capacity ramps across the industry; large integrated players expected to retain scale benefits.
Domestic module CUF fell to about 45% in Q2 as ALMM List-II extension shifted supply chains; management expects higher non-DCR volumes in Q3.
Indian demand (AC): residential plus C&I rooftop about 15 GW annualised; utility about 25 GW annualised; total about 55-60 GW DC per year per management.

qa_highlights.question: Retail channel economics: distributor margins, profitability, and how the distribution model is managed without visible opex increase.
qa_highlights.answer: Retail network is 775+ exclusive retail centres with about 3,000 distribution points and about 5,000 people; H1 retail revenue about Rs 5,700 crore, FY27 guided Rs 10,000-11,000 crore. Management cited operating leverage and partner growth (some partners from Rs 1-2 crore to Rs 50-75 crore a year), without giving channel margin figures.

qa_highlights.question: Will there be further US order cancellations after the 2-2.5 GW deemed cancellations in the quarter?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said about 3 GW-plus of export orders were stopped being reported, cutting export share of the order book from about 24% to 7.8%; US order book is rising. Post Section 232, US realisation is expected to rise from 26-27 cents to 30-35 cents per watt. Renegotiation into MIP-compliant contracts is ongoing for orders already dispatched but not yet recognised.

qa_highlights.question: Why did domestic module CUF fall below 50% (about 45%) in Q2?
qa_highlights.answer: ALMM List-II extension of about 6 months shifted supply chains and replanning took time, so non-DCR supply was delayed. Management expects non-DCR supply to rise and Q3 volumes to be higher.

qa_highlights.question: Why did EBITDA margin fall sequentially from 18.2% to 17.8%?
qa_highlights.answer: Q1 included a US duty refund; the refund rose from Rs 349 crore in Q1 to Rs 360.4 crore in Q2 (about Rs 11 crore booked in Q2). Like-for-like, margin improved with cell utilisation up from about 800 MW to over 1.1 GW per quarter and US module utilisation up from 60% to 70%+. Q3 and Q4 are expected to be heavy with 5 GW cell capacity each quarter plus US 1.6 GW lines; H2 expected at 55-60% of FY27 EBITDA guidance.

qa_highlights.question: US margin: how do exports from India compare with US-manufactured modules, and are IRA benefits included in reported numbers?
qa_highlights.answer: Export from India yields about 3-4 cents/W EBITDA; US manufacturing gives about 2-3 cents operating margin at 70%+ utilisation plus about 7 cents/W incentive, so 8-9 cents/W total. Management said this is more than double export margins. IRA incentives are booked against dispatches and some are sold, so reported numbers include them.

qa_highlights.question: Domestic pricing: DCR and non-DCR prices and expected correction in FY28.
qa_highlights.answer: DCR spot: utility 19-21 cents/W, retail 22-24 cents/W; FY28 forward utility 17.5-18.5 cents and retail 20-21 cents. Non-DCR utility about 12-12.5 cents, retail 13.5-14 cents. Broad price correction expected in FY28, with scale players retaining benefits.

qa_highlights.question: Why are subsidiary (listed entity) EBITDA margins low relative to revenue of about Rs 22 billion?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the listed subsidiary runs about 17-18% EBITDA standalone, but after acquiring a T&D entity (T&D margins about 10-11%) the blended margin is about 14-15%. T&D is lumpy, so the subsidiary is chasing larger order books.

qa_highlights.question: BESS, inverter and transformer revenue contribution in FY28 and margins.
qa_highlights.answer: Newer businesses expected to rise from 15-20% of revenue to 30-35% over 2-3 years; solar pure-play to 50-60% long range. Inverter and transformer EBITDA expected 18-22%; electrolyser 13-15%. Ballpark revenue from inverter, transformer and electrolyser about Rs 7,000-8,000 crore on about Rs 1,200 crore committed capital.

qa_highlights.question: Rs 1 lakh crore revenue ambition: how achievable and what split?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited about 20-22 GW module output from the 29 GW solar PV base, realising about Rs 40,000-45,000 crore of solar revenue; with non-solar business and 75% utilisation, Rs 90,000-1 lakh crore within 4-5 years, with roughly equal module and non-module contribution. No firm timeline.

risks_watch: Further US order cancellations or renegotiations: about 2-2.5 GW deemed cancellations this quarter; export order share now 7.8%, and orders dispatched but not yet recognised are being renegotiated to MIP-compliant terms.

Execution of H2 ramp: H2 must deliver 55-60% of the Rs 7,000-7,700 crore FY27 EBITDA guidance; 5 GW India cell in Q3 and another 5 GW in Q4, plus US 1.6 GW lines in Q3 and Q4, must come online on time.

Q2 EBITDA dependence on US duty refund: refund was Rs 349 crore in Q1 and Rs 360.4 crore in Q2; reported margins include IRA incentives that management says are booked against dispatches and partly sold.
Pricing correction in FY28 as industry capacity rises (cell capacity close to 40 GW, heading to about 60 GW); DCR forward prices are 17.5-18.5 cents vs spot 19-21 cents.
Ingot-wafer plant at Nagpur (10 GW, commercial production targeted September 2027, capex about Rs 5,500 crore vs analyst's Rs 6,200-6,500 crore cited earlier); civil works about 70% complete.

Capex funding and balance sheet: Rs 30,000 crore programme (35% deployed, 28% under execution, 37% planning); large capital advances and rise in other current liabilities; BESS phase 2 funding tied to policy clarity and overseas orders.
Domestic CUF at about 45% in Q2 due to ALMM List-II extension; management expects higher non-DCR volumes in Q3.
key_quotes: We affirm our operating EBITDA guidance of Rs. 7,000 to Rs. 7,700 crores in FY '27.

So, partially yes, because the existing cell capacity is at around 81% in Q2, and considering the ramp-up which has already happened, I think we are at around 90% plus already running in the existing capacity.
So, H2 overall shall be around 55 % to 60% of the overall EBITDA guidance is what we are looking at.
We remain a net debt-free company with net cash of around Rs. 3,224 crores and a net debt-to-equity ratio of minus 0.2x.

544280|2026-03.headline: Afcons posted its first-ever quarterly loss (Q4 net loss INR 89 crore) and FY26 PAT fell to INR 251 crore; no FY27 revenue or margin guidance given.
544280|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue fell 18% YoY to INR 2,777 crore and EBITDA dropped to INR 170 crore from INR 415 crore, with a net loss of INR 89 crore. Management blamed customer payment delays, overseas supply-chain disruption from the Middle East conflict, one-off provisions and marine cost overruns, and failure to cross margin-recognition thresholds on some projects. FY26 revenue was INR 12,322 crore (down 5.4%), EBITDA INR 1,439 crore (11.7% margin) and PAT INR 251 crore after a INR 76 crore Labour Code charge. Management guided FY26 order booking of INR 30,000 crore for FY27 but declined to give revenue or margin guidance until visibility improves.

segments.commentary: Management estimated about 25% of domestic projects were affected in March; UP Jal Jeevan Mission payments are being withheld until 100% completion, against a contractual stage-wise payment basis.

qa_highlights.question: Why was Q4 so far below the mid-quarter confidence expressed on the Q3 call, and what drove the miss?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said Q4 customer payments did not come as in the past 15-20 years; Afcons chose liquidity over growth, funding projects only up to limits, and overseas supply disruption in March (fuel, gas, logistics) hit execution.

qa_highlights.answer: Management did not give the Q2 ECL quantum on the call and said it is higher than the INR 86 crore cited by the analyst; it will follow up offline. Breakeven is about INR 2,400-2,500 crore quarterly revenue, and incremental revenue earns about 35% gross margin.

qa_highlights.question: Will there be further provisioning, and what is the outstanding and stuck receivable position (UP JJM, contract assets)?

Contract assets (unbilled) stand at about INR 8,200 crore, and the company aims to reduce them by year end.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: FY27 capex is held at about INR 700 crore and FY28 at about INR 650 crore, with no new capacity programme discussed and utilisation not disclosed.

tone.note: Management was confident on FY28 growth of 20-25%, HSR tunnelling and the INR 30,000 crore order inflow target, but cautious and vague on FY27 revenue, H2 quantum, collections timing and the Q2 ECL amount; analysts pushed on provisioning, receivables and the implied H2 revenue.

544282|2026-03.headline: Sagility Q4 FY26 revenue rose 29.1% YoY in INR to ₹20,243 million, with FY26 adjusted EBITDA margin at 25.3%, ahead of guidance.
544282|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue was ₹20,243 million ($222.1 million), up 29.1% YoY in INR and 22.2% in constant currency, with organic growth of 19.4% CC. Adjusted EBITDA was ₹5,036 million (24.9% margin) and adjusted PAT ₹3,069 million (15.2%). For FY26, revenue reached ₹71,929 million (up 29.1% INR, 23.6% CC; organic 15% CC) and adjusted EBITDA was 25.3%, ahead of the Q3 guidance, helped by higher-than-expected seasonal open enrolment and AEP revenue. Management guided FY27 organic growth to low double digits in CC and adjusted EBITDA margin of 24% to 25%, tracking the upper end if FX holds.

Medicare Advantage final rate increase 2.48% for CY27 (preliminary was almost flat).

qa_highlights.question: Will AI reduce future revenue, and how is the company adapting?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said AI will lower client costs and reduce some revenue, but it expects market-share gains; organic growth is still seen in double digits, with several AI use cases implemented.

qa_highlights.question: Capital allocation: will dividends rise given the debt payoff and higher cash?
qa_highlights.answer: Debt to be repaid in FY27, funds kept for M&A (payer or provider, capability or client-access deals such as BroadPath); dividend to be reviewed with no firm commitment.

qa_highlights.question: What is the base for FY27 revenue and the cumulative ACV?
qa_highlights.answer: Cumulative ACV was about $130 million, but ramp timing, volume changes, AI reductions and geographic mix all affect conversion; roughly 7% to 8% growth is seen as already factored in.

qa_highlights.question: Why is the margin guidance of 24% to 25% below FY26's 25.3%?
qa_highlights.answer: Headwinds include wage hikes funded by FX, a rising US (lower-margin) revenue mix and possible price reductions; top end of the range expected if FX holds.

qa_highlights.question: Why is guidance low double digits when organic growth was 15%? Is AI compression higher?
qa_highlights.answer: Guidance is organic. AI compression is expected at about 2% in FY27 versus 1% to 1.5% historically, and deal timing is uncertain.

qa_highlights.question: Why was Q4 attrition higher, and will other expenses moderate?
qa_highlights.answer: Attrition rose because seasonal headcount exited after open enrolment. Other expenses rose on IT and AI investment plus some asset write-offs from centre rationalisation; management expects them to stay high.

544282|2026-06.headline: Sagility Q1 FY27 revenue rose 27.6% YoY to INR 19,635m; FY27 margin guidance held at 24-25% despite a 120 bps minimum-wage hit.
544282|2026-06.overview: Revenue grew 27.6% YoY (15.2% in constant currency) to INR 19,635 million, with organic growth of 27.3% in INR and 14.9% in constant currency, helped by the CareSeed acquisition closed 11 June 2026. Sequentially, reported revenue fell because about $24.8 million of Q4 open-enrolment revenue did not recur, but steady-state organic revenue grew 5.1% QoQ in constant currency. Adjusted EBITDA rose 27.9% to INR 4,716 million at a 24.0% margin (down from 24.9% in Q4), and adjusted PAT rose 35.1% to INR 2,697 million at 13.7%. Management reiterated low double-digit FY27 organic constant-currency growth and the 24-25% margin range, with the wage impact absorbed via efficiencies and FX.

qa_highlights.question: Is M&A pipeline focused where?

544282|2026-09.headline: Sagility Q2 FY27 revenue rose 22.5% YoY in INR to INR 20,321 mn, adjusted EBITDA margin hit 26.3%, and FY27 margin guidance was raised to 25-26%.
544282|2026-09.overview: Q2 FY27 revenue was INR 20,321 mn ($212.6 mn), up 22.5% YoY in INR and 12.2% in constant currency, with organic growth of 11.9% in constant currency. Adjusted EBITDA rose 23% to INR 5,353 mn at a 26.3% margin, the highest in six quarters, helped by operating efficiencies, FX tailwinds and geo mix despite higher statutory wage costs. Management acquired Chirok Health LLC (closed October 21, 2026) to build a mid-cycle RCM capability and push provider growth, and raised FY27 adjusted EBITDA margin guidance to 25-26% from 24-25%. The company now holds a net cash position of INR 1,127 mn, and management expects open enrolment/AEP revenue to be slightly lower than last year.

qa_highlights.answer: Ramesh said about 100 bps lower than last year's roughly 6% of revenue on current visibility; CFO said it is marginally below flat YoY at this early stage.

qa_highlights.answer: Management said the goal is a much larger provider share over time but gave no explicit 2-3 year target; provider share is about 10% today. Investment is mainly the Chirok deal plus a dedicated provider go-to-market team, with no major margin impact.

qa_highlights.question: Why is provider growth lagging, and what is Chirok's growth history?
qa_highlights.answer: Provider growth has been 10-11% with some revenue taper from discrete projects at one client. Chirok revenue dipped in 2023-24 when one client's volumes fell, then recovered; management said the 35.8% margin is broadly on the same basis as Sagility's adjusted EBITDA.

qa_highlights.answer: Ramesh said there is no inherent conflict, citing about 15 years of running both businesses and claims-denial friction the company helps resolve.

qa_highlights.answer: Ramesh said the range remains 24-26%, with possible gradual upside if the company keeps some AI productivity benefits; most gains are expected to flow to clients.

544283|2026-03.headline: ACME Solar Q4 FY26 revenue rose 31% YoY to INR705 crore, FY26 revenue INR2,507 crore (+59%), with 2.3 GW of merchant BESS now running.
544283|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 total revenue was INR705 crore (+31% YoY), including INR157 crore of other income, and FY26 revenue was INR2,507 crore (+59%) on capacity addition and higher CUF. PAT was INR138 crore for the quarter (19.6% margin) and INR498 crore for FY26 (19.9%), with management citing EBITDA margins above 90%. Management said about 2.3 GW of BESS is now commissioned and earning on merchant and short-term contracts at roughly INR2.2 crore per day. Management also flagged a timeline shift: most of the 1.5 GW generation commissioning and the 10 GWh BESS target depend on CTU substations, some of which are delayed by up to about 6 months.

segments.name: Solar and wind generation (operational)
segments.commentary: Operational contracted generation capacity is 2,990 MW. Management said plant and grid availability were above 99% for the year, and FY26 portfolio CUF was about 26%. Sikar (Rajasthan) new plants ran at about 29-30% CUF for the year, and roughly 28%+ in Q4.

segments.name: BESS (merchant)
segments.commentary: About 2.3 GWh of BESS is commissioned, mostly in March, and earns about INR2.2 crore per day net (over INR60 crore per month) from tariff arbitrage. Round-trip efficiency is 88-90%. Management said the Q3 battery contribution was negligible.

guidance_outlook: Target of about 1.5 GW of generation projects commissioned in FY27, with the first FDRE commissioning at Neemuch substation in June 2026.

Battery target of about 10 GWh for the next calendar year: roughly 8.5 GWh merchant and 1.5 GWh in FDRE format. Management said the 10 GWh target is achievable on connectivity and financing; supply and geopolitics are the main uncertainties.
Around 2.5 GW of connectivity at operational substations (Fatehgarh-1, Fatehgarh-2 under STOA, Bikaner-3) is ready for BESS discharge at night.
Under-construction portfolio of 5.1 GW (total pipeline 8,071 MW) with PPA-signed capacity of 3,280 MW; PPA-signed projects expected to be commissioned by FY28.
Management expects a run-rate EBITDA jump as battery revenue starts; a 75-80% EBITDA margin is expected on merchant BESS at INR6 tariff arbitrage.
capex_capacity: Committed total capex INR12,475 crore: INR6,445 crore incurred in FY26 and INR6,030 crore in purchase orders. Battery capex was about INR1,000-1,200 crore in Q4.
Gross block rose about INR3,460 crore in FY26, of which about INR1,000-1,100 crore is battery.

Capital advances of about INR323 crore, mainly battery (10% advance against bank guarantee) and turbines (20% advance). Management said solar module capex is being deferred until the LTA is operational.
Under-construction portfolio added 301 MW of peak-power FDRE with SECI in the quarter; total under construction is 5.1 GW, requiring about 17 GWh of BESS.

Commissioning timeline: NTPC hybrid solar ready, LTA by December 2026; Pachora wind component a couple of quarters later; SJVN Fatehgarh full FDRE by FY27 end (LTA March 2027). Pavagada and Anantapur are targeted this year per CTU timelines.
demand_pricing: India peak demand hit 256 GW on 25 April 2026, against 250 GW in May 2024. Electricity consumption grew 8.9% in April 2026.

India added about 55 GW of RE in FY26 (cumulative 283 GW). Management expects peak-power and FDRE/BESS-linked bids to dominate, with 15-20 GW of bids this year (fewer than last year) and state plus central tenders of 20-30 GW.

Management said peak-power products sell fastest, followed by partial peak, then wind; plain solar sells slowest. Thermal-equivalent BESS pricing is cited at INR9-10 per unit at peak, with the annual realisation at INR7-8.
Receivable days have fallen to about 14-15 days from about 180 days in the past. Trade receivables fell 13% YoY. Central offtakers take a cash discount and pay in about 10 days.

qa_highlights.question: What battery capex was incurred and how much BESS capacity was commissioned?
qa_highlights.answer: Battery capex was about INR1,000-1,200 crore in the last quarter, and about 1.3 GWh was commissioned as of the prior quarter. Battery capacity reached 2.3 GWh by the time of the call.

qa_highlights.question: What is the run-rate EBITDA from existing capacity?
qa_highlights.answer: FY26 EBITDA including other income was about INR2,200 crore, mainly from the PPA projects. BESS revenue at INR2.2 crore per day is over INR60 crore per month.

qa_highlights.question: Is there curtailment, and how is future project allocation shaped?
qa_highlights.answer: Only about 2 projects are connected to the state grid. FY26 curtailment impact was INR5-6 crore, plus INR3 crore of STU impact in Rajasthan. Nearly all of the portfolio is on CTU, with the goal that each project has a battery.

qa_highlights.question: Why is gross block growing faster than run-rate EBITDA?
qa_highlights.answer: About INR1,000-1,100 crore of the gross block increase is battery, and the battery was commissioned late in the year, so it is not yet in run-rate EBITDA. Wind is also still ramping in phases.

qa_highlights.question: What is the risk from LOA conversion and CERC connectivity rules?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said about 6.2 GW of signed PPAs are under construction, and 3.2 GW of LOA has converted to PPA. Management does not expect LOAs to be surrendered, and it has a backup plan of using connectivity for future bids or battery-linked projects.

qa_highlights.question: How long will the BESS arbitrage last?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the duration is uncertain. It estimated the national need at about 200-300 GWh, and said the peak price should stay at INR7-8 for four to five years given gas constraints.

qa_highlights.question: Are CTU substation delays affecting commissioning?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said about 60% of substations are on time and the maximum delay is typically 6 months. Where delays are known, modules are deferred, and no penalty applies under the sync-up framework.

risks_watch: Commissioning timelines depend on CTU substations and LTA dates; management cites delays of up to about 6 months, with the 1.5 GW FY27 target at risk.
BESS merchant revenue depends on the peak-offpeak price spread; management concedes the duration is uncertain and the spread could narrow as more batteries come online.
The 10 GWh battery target depends on supply of material and geopolitical factors.
CERC draft proposal on LOA-based connectivity and PPA signing risk for about 850 MW of older PPAs still in discussion.
Q4 PLF fell about 1% YoY, which management attributed to lower irradiation and curtailment.
Management commentary on the new CFO is that Arun Chopra has replaced Rajat Kumar Singh; watch for continuity.
544283|2026-03.management_tone: Confident and detailed on BESS deployment, regulatory tailwinds and the timeline. Management was less specific on Q4 battery EBITDA, asset-level margins and the reason for the gross block to EBITDA gap, deferring to later updates.

So technically, maybe 25 to 30 gigawatt will technically mean solar of 40, 50 gigawatt.
So 6 month s delay is, I think, very much -- should be taken in a good light.

544283|2026-06.headline: ACME Solar Q1 FY27 revenue rose 63% YoY to INR954 crore and EBITDA 56% to INR831 crore, with BESS contributing INR226 crore.
544283|2026-06.overview: Management reported record revenue and EBITDA for Q1 FY27, with total revenue of INR954 crore (up 63% YoY), EBITDA of INR831 crore (up 56%) and PAT of INR235 crore (up 80%). Growth was attributed to a record CUF of 30.9%, BESS revenue and new renewable capacity. BESS commissioning reached about 3.62 GWh cumulative, and the BESS commissioning guidance was pulled forward to more than 10 GWh by FY27 from calendar 2027. Management also said it has locked in about INR1,400 crore of short-term BESS revenue for FY27 and addressed a fire at the ACME Suryodaya BESS site, attributing it to an AC cabling short circuit rather than the battery system.

segments.commentary: EBITDA margin ~88-89% in Q1; ex-BESS EBITDA margin stated at ~91%, with seasonal range of 88-91% over recent quarters. Management cited repowering of existing plants as a margin support.

segments.commentary: Revenue INR226 crore in Q1 with ~82% EBITDA margin; cumulative commissioned capacity ~3.62 GWh (about 40% of India's cumulative commissioned BESS). Management cites an annual EBITDA-to-capex yield above 20%.

guidance_outlook: BESS commissioning target raised to more than 10 GWh by FY27 (earlier: 10 GWh by calendar 2027), roughly three quarters earlier.
Around 1.5 GW of contracted renewable capacity to be commissioned in FY27, subject to substation and transmission availability.
Full-year FY27 capex upgraded to approximately INR15,000-20,000 crore.
About INR1,400 crore of BESS revenue locked for FY27 on roughly 70-80% of the ~10 GWh target; management said it could be higher if more volume is contracted.
Management indicated a 2-3 year assumption of INR1,400 crore-plus BESS revenue is reasonable; BESS EBITDA margin expected within 2-5% of Q1 level (~82%).
Management said it may increase its 2030 target beyond 10 GWh, to be updated in coming quarters.
capex_capacity: Total portfolio 8,070 MW, with about 20 GWh of battery storage; under-construction capacity 5,080 MW.
PPAs signed for 3,880 MW, including 600 MW of new FDRE and hybrid PPAs with SECI this quarter; about 1,200 MW still awaiting PPA signing.
Debt tied up for about 85% of PPA-signed portfolio; INR6,000 crore financing secured for 700 MW of under-construction FDRE projects.
Battery procurement: more than 15 GWh ordered (CATL, Hithium); around 90% of the 20 GWh battery requirement contracted, with orders placed where PPAs are signed.

BESS capex ~INR93 lakh per MW including transformer, IDC and EPC; management said it could rise 5-10% for future batches. More than $300 million hedged at roughly $89-93 per unit of USD exchange rate.
Battery operations: round-trip efficiency ~89%, depth of discharge ~93%, state of health above 99.9%, availability above 99%; operating at one cycle per day.
demand_pricing: India power demand grew 8.8% YoY in Q1 to 485 billion units; peak demand hit a record 271 GW and was near 270 GW in July.
Short-term BESS realisations cited at INR8-10/kWh (publicly available DEEP portal and HP-TAM bids), sometimes higher; contracts are typically under one year, with 6-9 months' lead time.
Open (merchant) BESS capacity is about 600 MWh; management aims for zero open capacity outside PPA by end-2026, though a 300 MW plant is still open.

SECI is consolidating bids and will only bid with firmer power-offtake commitments, reducing near-term bid volumes; management expects large FDRE, peak power, CFD and state bids to follow over 6-9 months.
Management sees the peak-power market growing toward 300-500 GWh, potentially 1 TWh in a positive case, driven by rooftop and KUSUM solar (duck-curve effect).
Competition from other BESS entrants (including Adani) is rising, but management argues merchant supply will remain limited and that the market is still new to state buyers.

qa_highlights.question: How much open or early BESS capacity will there be in FY27 and the next couple of years, and what are realisations on the INR1,400 crore short-term contracts?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is contracting well above 10 GWh and realisations are INR8-10 per unit, depending on month and volume. Only ~600 MWh is open today, with a target of zero open capacity outside PPAs by end-2026. Management plans for 10-12 GWh to remain available for short-term markets each year over the next five years.

qa_highlights.question: What is the curtailment impact and what drove EBITDA growth ex-BESS?
qa_highlights.answer: Curtailment was about 1% of revenue, only on state-based projects. EBITDA growth was attributed to CUF (30.9% vs 28.5%) and repowering of existing plants. Management is considering adding batteries to state projects to absorb surplus generation.

qa_highlights.question: Is the INR1,400 crore revenue sustainable for 2-3 years, given El Nino-driven pricing?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it sees the 10 GWh base supporting INR1,400 crore-plus for the next 2-3 years based on PPA and GNA timelines. Beyond that, it depends on market pricing and new PPAs. It said the market is still untapped by most discoms.

qa_highlights.question: What is the core (ex-BESS) EBITDA margin and the outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Ex-BESS margin was ~91% in Q1, with a seasonal range of 88-91%. Management expects FDRE projects may lift margins because their realisations are healthier than plain solar.

qa_highlights.question: How is the 6.28 INR/kWh PPA and the hybrid configuration changed?
qa_highlights.answer: The hybrid project was offered with 1 hour of battery, a change from the standard configuration. The other project at INR6.28 per unit has no change in configuration.

qa_highlights.question: What is the plan for C&I and data centres?
qa_highlights.answer: Management has started hiring for data-centre opportunities but is focused on profitability. It intends to target CTU-connected C&I customers and will not dilute mid-to-high teen return targets.

544283|2026-09.headline: ACME Solar Q2 FY27 revenue rose 67.5% YoY to INR1,007 crore; FY27 BESS commissioning guidance raised to over 12 GWh.
544283|2026-09.overview: Q2 FY27 revenue of INR1,007 crore (up 67.5% YoY) and EBITDA of INR874 crore (up 63.6%) were driven mainly by short-term peak power BESS operations and renewable additions. PAT rose 133.5% YoY to INR269 crore, a 26.7% margin. Management raised FY27 BESS commissioning guidance to more than 12 GWh from 10 GWh and lifted its 2030 target to 15 GW renewable plus 50 GWh BESS. Partial commissioning reached 1.9 GW, but full commissioning depends on GNA/substation timelines, which remain the main execution risk.

segments.name: BESS (peak power)
segments.commentary: EBITDA margin 78.3%; about 5.2 GWh commissioned, described as second largest in India; 324 million units sold under short-term contracts.

guidance_outlook: FY27 BESS commissioning guidance raised to more than 12 GWh from 10 GWh.
FY27 renewable capacity target around 1.5 GW, possibly slipping by a quarter depending on Fatehgarh-II GNA; partial commissioning could reach 2.5-3 GW.
FY28 capacity addition guided at 2.5-3 GW, with most substations expected to go live June to December 2028.
By 2030, renewable target raised to 15 GW (from 10 GW) and BESS to 50 GWh (from 25 GWh); management says contracted capacity could reach that level by end of calendar 2027.
H2 FY27 capex expected to be similar to or above the INR6,500 crore spent in H1, per management; exact figure to be shared later.
Contracted revenue: over INR1,600 crore locked for partial FY27 capacity and over INR1,500 crore for FY28; FY27 BESS about 90-95% tied up, FY28 about 50-65%.
capex_capacity: Approximately 5.2 GWh of BESS commissioned to date; 5 GWh half-yearly target achieved.
1.9 GW of contracted projects partially commissioned; 1.7 GW of modules delivered to site, of which 1.1 GW installed and 200 MWp charged.
About 19 GWh of BESS contracted with CATL, Hithium, Ganfeng, Trina and CLOU; about 7 GWh at sites and 5 GWh with LCs opened but not yet received.
BESS capex below INR1 crore per MWh (about INR90 lakh to INR1 crore), helped by installing at operational substations, saving about INR20 lakh per MWh.
Fatehgarh-II has about 700 MWp installed awaiting GNA; Neemuch, Bikaner-III and Ananthapur are the next projects.
demand_pricing: Near-term peak power bids are priced substantially above realisations seen so far, per management; Q2 and Q3 tariffs were already contracted.

544285|2026-06.headline: Swiggy guides Quick Commerce contribution margin to 0 to -100 bps for growth, with 4-week cumulative NOV growth at 10% vs 1% prior.
544285|2026-06.overview: Swiggy's Q1 FY27 call (held July 30, 2026) centred on a deliberate pivot from contribution-margin protection to growth in Quick Commerce (Instamart). Management said it reached contribution margin breakeven, closing the last quarter at -0.2%, and now guides to a 0 to -100 bps range to fund store expansion, speed, serviceability and assortment. Take-rate gains were attributed to brand monetisation, advertising and user-fee changes, with management calling them sustainable. Food delivery growth was about 18% adjusted for cancellations, with 18-20% YoY guidance maintained, and management dismissed zero-commission competition from Toing's rivals as unsustainable. Toing, the new value-led food platform, is loss-making and was a major focus, with a Capital Markets Day planned for the following week.

qa_highlights.question: Is the food delivery zero-commission model a threat?
qa_highlights.answer: Rohit Kapoor argued zero commission is not sustainable; costs must be recovered from restaurants, consumers or delivery partners. Competition is expected in affordability, not premium.

qa_highlights.question: Wage hike and last-mile cost escalation?
qa_highlights.answer: Annual salary revision sits below CM. Minimum wage hikes in some states affect picking and packing; impact described as not material. Last-mile cost rose on seasonal factors including elections and harvest migration; efficiency offset kept the YoY dip to 20 bps.

qa_highlights.answer: Rahul Bothra said Swiggy does not capitalise employee, tech token or store costs, and is not aware of payables securitisation practices by peers.

qa_highlights.answer: Growth from transacting users and frequency; more stores in existing cities as hyper-local stores hit 2,500-3,000 orders/day. Spend priorities are store expansion, speed and serviceability, and selection availability.

544286|2026-03.headline: Niva Bupa FY26 GWP grew 27.4% to INR9,433 crores and IFRS PAT rose to INR366 crores; FY29 combined ratio target ~99%.
544286|2026-03.overview: FY26 closed with 27.4% overall GWP growth to INR9,433 crores (retail +35%) and Ind AS PAT of INR366 crores versus INR203 crores, with ROE at 10.7%. Expense of management fell to 33.7% from 39.2%, and the IFRS combined ratio improved 160 bps to 101.4% despite a 1.1 pt rise in loss ratio. Retail market share rose to 10.1% for the full year and 10.4% in Q4. Management set a long-term IFRS combined ratio target of about 99% by FY29, which it says translates to a mid-to-high teens ROE. Commission regulation remains an open question pending regulator guidance.

qa_highlights.question: How would the company respond to potential commission caps or cuts?

qa_highlights.question: Why are onerous contract loss components recognised, and what is the strategy?
qa_highlights.answer: Under IFRS, loss components are created when expected loss ratio, expenses and risk adjustment exceed 100%; a 9M loss component was unwound in Q4 and similar amounts existed in the prior year.

544286|2026-06.headline: Niva Bupa Q1 FY27 PAT rose to INR137.8 crore and CISR improved 300bp to 100.2%, driven by a 3.8pp lower loss ratio.
544286|2026-06.overview: Niva Bupa reported Q1 FY27 profit after tax of INR137.8 crore and a combined insurance service ratio (CISR) of 100.2%, against 103.2% a year earlier. Growth was strong in retail health (reported 47.1%, like-to-like 35.5%) while group business was flat amid a challenging B2B pricing environment. The company moved fully to Ind AS in Q1, with parallel IFRS 17-style disclosures continuing for public reporting. Management said July loss ratio trends were in line with plan and reiterated the FY29 mid-to-high-teens ROE target.

qa_highlights.answer: No structural change; distribution and product levers continue, targeting 8-10pp above market growth in retail. Group growth held back by pricing.

qa_highlights.answer: PPN lowers claim size by 15-20% vs tertiary care, but management said it may be used to price more competitively rather than to improve the loss ratio.

qa_highlights.answer: Retail mix about 35% fresh and 65% renewal; renewal loss ratio about 75%, acceptable given expenses of under 20% on that book, with annual high-single-digit price increases.

qa_highlights.question: Why raise INR500 crore of debt and any equity shift in investments?

ICRA issuer rating is AAA and an instrument rating is coming. No change in investment strategy; AIFs (mostly performing credit, 12-15% yield) being built toward the 5% cap.

What we guided earlier was by FY '29 mid to high teens, and we go by that.

544286|2026-09.headline: Niva Bupa H1 FY27 combined ratio improved 365bps to 99.5%, with GWP up 26% to INR5,004 crores ex-1/n and PAT at INR273 crores.

544290|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue from operations was INR4,273 mn (+8.8% YoY), EBITDA INR799 mn (18.7% margin) and PAT INR543 mn (12.4% margin), with margin pressure attributed to renewable IPP mix, higher employee cost, ECL provision and depreciation. Management said FY26 revenue partly missed guidance because awarded projects stayed in design and bid evaluations were delayed, and it cut FY27 EBITDA guidance to 21-22% from 22-24% citing commodity cost pressure. Working capital stretched to 166 days (unbilled revenue days at 195) because AMRUT state-scheme funds were delayed. The renewable segment (BESS, wind EPC via Suyog Urja) is now a major part of the order book.

financial_highlights.value: INR422 crore (LT INR250 crore, ST INR175 crore)

segments.name: Water & wastewater
segments.commentary: Execution order book about INR2,733 crore plus O&M order book about INR951 crore; FY27 water/wastewater revenue expected about INR1,350 crore. Recent wins: INR348 crore BUIDCO (Bihar) project and two Swachh Bharat sanitation projects in Pune and Nashik worth INR824 crore in Q4.

segments.name: Renewable energy
segments.commentary: Execution order book about INR2,051 crore plus O&M/IPP about INR1,079 crore; renewable revenue was about INR129 crore in FY26 (INR117 crore in Q4, mostly IPP with near-zero margin). FY27 renewable revenue target about INR650 crore; BESS EPC PAT margin guided about 10%, renewables blended PAT 10-12%.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue guidance of about INR2,000 crore, with PAT of INR270-280 crore (13.5-14% PAT margin).
FY27 EBITDA margin cut to 21-22% from earlier 22-24%, with a possible further 1-2 percentage point dip from commodity and geopolitical cost pressure.
FY27 order inflow target of at least INR2,500 crore; bid pipeline submitted about INR1,200 crore plus about INR5,000 crore under evaluation.
Working capital cycle targeted to fall to about 90 days; debt-to-equity to be capped at 1:1 on consolidated basis.
Capex for FY27 expected at about INR20-30 crore; Q1 FY27 revenue said to be well above Q1 FY26 (about INR250 crore), without a number.
FY28 indicative revenue from existing order book about INR2,500-2,800 crore; management reiterated 35-40% long-term topline growth ambition.
capex_capacity: Total execution order book about INR4,800 crore, said to give visibility over FY27 and FY28 (execution period 18-24 months for renewable projects).
BESS: 4 NTPC EPC projects totalling 930 MWh worth about INR1,070 crore (UP, Assam, Karnataka, Telangana) plus acquired 150 MWh Bihar BESS project.
Lithium-ion cell procurement deferred due to price rises; BOS works (civil, transformers, HT lines) already started.
Renewable team above 250 professionals; business heads appointed for each division.
Asset monetisation possible if leverage rises; Suyog Urja (wind EPC) acquired during FY26.
demand_pricing: Most contracts carry a price variation clause, which offsets only part of the cost increase; management says guidance was lowered for this gap.
Water project cost benchmarks: STP INR1-1.5 crore per MLD; water treatment INR30-50 lakh per MLD; CETP highly variable (INR2-15 crore per MLD).
Design component is 2-5% of turnkey water project value; STPs and CETPs are the most technology-intensive.

Revenue shortfall attributed to slow evaluations and re-bidding of an MIDC CETP/ZLD project and two Bangalore projects stuck in design, plus delayed AMRUT funds in Chhattisgarh, MP, Rajasthan, Haryana and Punjab.
Renewable receivables de-risked via NTPC and A-to-AAA rated private clients for Suyog's wind EPC work.

qa_highlights.question: Why was FY26 revenue guidance (about 35% growth) missed and is execution delayed?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said ongoing projects have no delays, but the order book of about INR1,200 crore at 1 April 2025 converted to about INR1,145 crore (about 95%) with timing slipping; some projects stayed in design and a re-bid hit timelines. Renewables were about INR100 crore below the INR200 crore guidance and wastewater about INR100 crore below as well.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Q4 margins fall and what is the underlying margin?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited mix: about INR100-120 crore of zero-margin IPP revenue, employee cost up to about 6% of revenue, other expenses 3.5%, ECL provision INR10 crore and depreciation up about INR25 crore. Manufacturing cost fell about 1 percentage point; FY26 EBITDA stayed above 24%.

qa_highlights.question: What is the split of renewable revenue in FY26 and Q4?
qa_highlights.answer: Renewable revenue was about INR129 crore for FY26, with about INR12 crore up to December and INR117 crore in Q4.

qa_highlights.question: What is the working capital outlook and drivers?
qa_highlights.answer: Net working capital cycle was 166 days, with UBR days at 195 because AMRUT funds were not released; receivable days fell to 53. Management expects funds from Chhattisgarh and a path for Rajasthan, Haryana and MP, targeting about 90 days.

qa_highlights.question: Will FY27 EBITDA guidance be cut further and what drives it?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cut EBITDA guidance to 21-22% from 22-24% due to commodity and geopolitical cost pressure; a further 1-2 point dip is possible, depending on whether the situation stabilises.

qa_highlights.question: What are the BESS and renewable margins and how is the FY27 revenue split?
qa_highlights.answer: BESS EPC PAT margin is about 10%; renewable blended PAT target is 10-12%. FY27 revenue split is about INR1,350 crore water/wastewater and INR650 crore renewables, against the INR2,000 crore total; about 42% of the INR4,800 crore order book.

qa_highlights.question: What is the operating cash flow position?
qa_highlights.answer: Adjusted pre-tax OCF is roughly balanced (about INR4 lakh positive) in FY26; post-tax OCF is negative INR63 crore, mainly due to service concession receivables recognised in OCF under audit policy.

risks_watch: Delayed central and state fund release (AMRUT, Jal Jeevan) could keep UBR days near 195 and working capital above 166 days.
Lithium-ion cell cost increases and geopolitical commodity pressure could cut EBITDA by a further 1-2 percentage points.
Revenue execution slippage: FY26 missed guidance; FY27 guidance of about INR2,000 crore depends on converting only about 42% of the INR4,800 crore order book.
Renewable IPP projects carry near-zero margin; segment profitability disclosure is promised separately going forward.
Debt rising toward the stated 1:1 debt-to-equity ceiling as renewable development projects are funded.
544290|2026-03.management_tone: Confident on order book visibility and FY27 targets, but defensive on the FY26 miss and margin compression; management repeatedly described guidance as deliberately conservative and admitted the revenue guidance was not met.
key_quotes: So we are just projecting a topline of INR2,000-odd crores, which will replicate into a conversion of somewhere around 42%. So we are trying ourselves to be just too conservative this time so that there is no fallback at all.
We will delay the procurement of lithium-ion battery to a certain extent so the prices get settled down, and at that point of time, we'll go for the procurement.
So as such, I can confirm with respect to the execution, the delay was not there.
The present debt level is 0.34.

rows.why: 4 NTPC BESS EPC projects totalling 930 MWh (~INR1,070 crore) plus acquired 150 MWh Bihar BESS project are under construction, and the INR4,800 crore order book gives visibility over FY27-FY28; no timing given for the BESS capacity itself.

rows.why: FY27 revenue guided to ~INR2,000 crore vs FY26 INR1,146 crore (~17.5% growth), with renewables target ~INR650 crore vs FY26 ~INR129 crore and water/wastewater ~INR1,350 crore, though FY26 missed guidance by ~35%.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: FY27 capex guided only at INR20-30 crore, debt is INR422 crore with D/E 0.34 against a 1:1 ceiling, and lithium-ion cell procurement was deferred; utilisation is not disclosed as a capacity constraint.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: FY26 revenue missed the ~35% growth guidance (+7.5% actual) and FY27 EBITDA margin was cut to 21-22%, so there is no sign of an upward revision.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Management flagged a possible further 1-2 pt EBITDA margin dip from commodity and geopolitical cost pressure, and FY27 revenue depends on converting only ~42% of the INR4,800 crore order book, after FY26 execution slipped (order book ~INR1,200 crore converted to ~INR1,145 crore with timing slipping).

rows.label: Working capital cycle to ~90 days
rows.why: Cycle is 166 days (UBR 195 days) vs ~90-100 target, and it depends on AMRUT and state fund releases from Chhattisgarh, Rajasthan, Haryana and MP that have been delayed.

rows.label: FY27 order inflow of at least INR2,500 crore
rows.why: Bid pipeline is ~INR1,200 crore submitted plus ~INR5,000 crore under evaluation, and Q4 wins of INR824 crore show momentum, but evaluations have been slow and a MIDC CETP project was re-bid.

rows.label: Debt-to-equity capped at 1:1
rows.why: Total debt is INR422 crore at D/E 0.34, with renewable development projects funded by debt, and management says asset monetisation is possible if leverage rises.

tone.note: Management was confident on the INR4,800 crore order book, FY27 PAT of INR270-280 crore and working capital easing to ~90 days, but defensive about the FY26 revenue miss and Q4 margin compression; analysts pressed on the margin cut and execution slippage.

544290|2026-06.headline: Q1 FY27 revenue rose 49% YoY to INR359.2 crore, but EBITDA margin fell to 21.07% from 26.65%, and FY27 guidance was trimmed to 21-22%.
544290|2026-06.overview: Revenue from operations was INR359.2 crore (+49% YoY) with EBITDA of INR75.7 crore (+17.9% YoY) and PAT of INR45.2 crore (+6.5% YoY). Management attributed the margin compression to higher raw material costs, a renewables mix, and a step-up in employee cost (about 7% of revenue vs 3-3.5% earlier). Total order book is about INR6,721 crore, split INR3,694 crore water/wastewater and INR3,027 crore renewables and BESS. Management reiterated FY27 revenue guidance of INR2,000 crore and PAT of INR260-270 crore, while lowering the EBITDA margin guidance to 21-22% from 22-24%, and later described a blended 19-20% margin.

financial_highlights.change: vs 26.65% in Q1 FY26 and 18.7% in Q4 FY26

financial_highlights.metric: Wind segment revenue (Suyog Urja, per Q&A)

segments.name: Water and wastewater treatment
segments.commentary: Order book INR3,694 crore (INR2,696 crore execution, INR998 crore O&M). Q1 revenue approx INR255 crore; management guides EBITDA margin 21-22% and FY27 topline INR1,300 crore from this order book at about 50% conversion.

segments.name: Renewable energy and BESS
segments.commentary: Order book INR3,027 crore (INR1,948 crore execution, INR1,079 crore IPP and O&M). Q1 revenue approx INR104 crore; guided EBITDA margin 15-18%, with execution over 12-18 months.

segments.name: Suyog Urja (wind EPC)
segments.commentary: Q1 revenue INR80 crore; FY27 revenue expectation INR400-450 crore; wind EPC pipeline INR800 crore with a further INR500-600 crore expected; EBITDA margin 15-16%.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue guidance maintained at INR2,000 crore; PAT guidance INR260-270 crore (per analyst recap, confirmed by management).
EBITDA margin guidance lowered to 21-22% from the earlier 22-24%; later framed as blended 19-20% (water 21-22%, renewables 15-18%).
Employee cost expected to normalise to 5-5.5% of revenue and finance cost to 3-3.5% during FY27.
FY27 order inflow expected at about INR2,500 crore (about 20% strike rate); INR256 crore won so far.
Quarterly revenue split expected as roughly 20%/20%/20% for Q1-Q3 and about 40% in Q4; BESS NTPC (930 MWh) procurement to start in Q3.
Management stated a bare-minimum growth target of 25-30% a year going forward while maintaining margins.

qa_highlights.question: What caused the gross margin decline YoY, and was it raw material costs or industry competition?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited higher raw material costs, the renewables mix, and employee cost rising to about 7% of Q1 revenue from 3-3.5% earlier (team grew from about 900 at IPO to about 2,300); employee cost to normalise to 5-5.5% and finance cost to 3-3.5% in FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Execution timelines for the order book and O&M duration?
qa_highlights.answer: Water execution INR2,700 crore over 18-24 months; renewables INR2,000 crore over 12-18 months; water O&M 5-15 years (about 10 years average), renewable O&M 5-12 years for EPC and 25 years for IPP.

qa_highlights.question: Quantify raw material impact and segment EBITDA margins; any price pass-through on new orders?
qa_highlights.answer: Water 21-22%, renewables 15-18%, blended 19-20%, around 20% for the year. Raw material impact about 1-2% of topline; WPI/CPI-linked price variation covers part, with some increase absorbed in EPC pricing.

qa_highlights.question: Wind revenue contribution and renewable EPC vs O&M split?
qa_highlights.answer: Wind (Suyog Urja) contributed INR80 crore of INR359 crore Q1 revenue; renewable execution order book about INR2,000 crore and O&M/IPP about INR1,000 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Peak debt, bidding pipeline and exit FY27 order book?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q1 renewables saw no margin downside; pipeline of about INR3,000 crore under evaluation plus INR6,000-7,000 crore being bid; renewables not being pushed aggressively; wind EPC INR600-800 crore targeted. No peak debt figure given.

qa_highlights.question: Unbilled revenue and working capital status; will operating cash flow turn positive in H1?
qa_highlights.answer: Working capital described as still bloated and funds flow slow, with management expecting a healthier cash flow position when cash flow numbers come out in September. Service concession receivables take about INR85 crore out of OCF; OCF turning positive is hoped for but not guaranteed. JJM exposure about INR150-160 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Suyog Urja tranche payments and FY27 revenue and profit contribution?
qa_highlights.answer: Acquisition valued INR311 crore: INR111 crore paid, INR100 crore second tranche after FY27 (around July) subject to KPIs, third tranche after FY28. Suyog FY27 revenue expectation INR400-450 crore at 15-16% EBITDA.

qa_highlights.question: Why was Q1 revenue (about INR360 crore) below the run-rate implied by historical seasonality, and is the INR2,000 crore guidance intact?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q1 is on target as guided at about 20% of the year; a significant jump is expected from Q3 when NTPC BESS (930 MWh) procurement starts. Guidance of INR2,000 crore revenue and INR260-270 crore PAT reaffirmed.

qa_highlights.question: Can FY27 revenue reach INR2,500-3,000 crore, and what about desalination and overseas projects?
qa_highlights.answer: INR2,000 crore is the threshold guidance, with about 50% conversion of the INR2,700 crore water execution book implying INR1,300-1,350 crore. Overseas bids submitted; desalination projects being pursued; operations in 17 states; ZLD and CBG projects under way.

qa_highlights.question: Outlook beyond FY27 and margin trajectory?
qa_highlights.answer: Management described a bare-minimum growth target of 25-30% a year while maintaining healthy margins, and said it will avoid low-margin projects. Margin upside possible but guidance based on minimum levels.

capex_capacity: Suyog Urja acquisition total value INR311 crore: first tranche INR111 crore paid; second tranche INR100 crore after FY27 (around July), based on KPIs; third tranche after FY28, funded by internal accruals and some debt.
Renewables: INR75 crore invested in the renewable segment so far; management framed it against an expected renewable profit of INR60-70 crore.

Five HAM projects now in portfolio (two new Varanasi projects, INR256.9 crore total, 18-month construction plus 15-year O&M); one completed, one near completion at Mathura, Saharanpur at 3 of 8 milestones; two new HAM projects expected to start construction in October-November.
Team size grew from about 900 at IPO to about 2,300 currently, ahead of execution ramp-up.
NTPC BESS order of 930 MWh: material procurement to start in Q3 FY27, expected to drive a significant revenue jump from Q3.
Operating footprint in 17 states; first JJM commissioning expected by October, with five JJM projects commissioned one by one and O&M of 10 years to follow.
demand_pricing: Total order book approx INR6,721 crore: water and wastewater INR3,694 crore (INR2,696 crore execution, INR998 crore O&M); renewables and BESS INR3,027 crore (INR1,948 crore execution, INR1,079 crore IPP and O&M).

Q1 FY27 new wins include INR113 crore EPC and O&M from Sardar Sarovar Narmada Nigam (Gujarat), INR207.5 crore renewable contract via Suyog Urja, and INR256.9 crore in two Varanasi HAM projects (INR130 crore Lohta 60 MLD STP; INR126.8 crore DDU Nagar 45 MLD STP).
Water execution timeline 18-24 months; renewable execution 12-18 months; water O&M tail 5-15 years (average about 10 years), with O&M expected at about INR100 crore topline and 3-5% of value.

Pipeline: bids submitted and under evaluation about INR3,000 crore; further INR6,000-7,000 crore of water/wastewater projects where bids are being invited or submitted; wind EPC pipeline INR800 crore with INR500-600 crore more expected.
FY27 order inflow target about INR2,500 crore at about 20% strike rate; INR256 crore won so far.
Quarterly revenue split expected at about 20% for Q1-Q3 and about 40% in Q4; Q1 revenue about INR359 crore vs FY27 guidance INR2,000 crore.
Pricing: raw material price impact about 1-2% of topline; tenders carry WPI/CPI-linked price variation clause, but some increase must be absorbed in EPC pricing.
Segment margin guidance: water 21-22% EBITDA; renewables 15-18%; Suyog Urja EBITDA 15-16%, PAT about 12%+; blended 19-20%; PAT margin about 13.5-14% guidance.
risks_watch: Margin compression: Q1 EBITDA margin 21.07% vs 26.65% YoY; FY27 guidance cut to 21-22% (water) and blended 19-20%, with raw material cost and partial price-variation recovery uncertain.
Working capital: management said the working capital cycle remains bloated and government cash flows have slowed; OCF turning positive is not guaranteed; watch September cash flow disclosure.

Execution conversion: FY26 revenue was flat against an opening order book of about INR1,200 crore, and FY27 needs about 50% conversion of the INR2,700 crore water book; order inflow of INR2,500 crore at 20% strike rate depends on pipeline awards.
Rising employee cost (about 7% of revenue in Q1) and finance cost (about 4%) versus guided normalisation to 5-5.5% and 3-3.5%.
Suyog Urja deferred consideration: INR100 crore second tranche after FY27 subject to KPIs, plus debt funding; the acquisition-linked profit contribution depends on hitting targets.
Quarterly back-loading: about 40% of FY27 revenue expected in Q4; NTPC BESS procurement starting Q3 is critical to the target.
key_quotes: Our EBITDA margins right now are 21% at the standalone level and we are happy to confirm that our EBITDA margins have remained at the same level of 21% even at the console level where it is getting consolidated with the business of renewables.

The position still I will say is bloated. But we are hoping since the funds are already allocated, even in the last quarter we had confirmed the movement of funds should be there, but it remained slow.
INR2,000 crores is the guidance which we understand we will achieve at any cost.
In the history of the company there has never been any bad debts and we continue to maintain that levels in future as well.

Some answers were evasive on debt levels and the exact working capital figures.

544290|2026-09.headline: Enviro Infra Q2 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 60% YoY to INR363.8 crore, but EBITDA margin fell to 20.58% from 28.56%.
544290|2026-09.overview: Consolidated revenue from operations grew 60% YoY to INR363.8 crore in Q2 FY27, while consolidated EBITDA excluding other income rose 15.3% to INR74.9 crore and margin compressed to 20.58%. PAT fell to INR39.5 crore from INR49.5 crore, which management attributed to input cost inflation from the West Asia conflict, higher finance and depreciation costs, interest accrued on the Suyog Urja acquisition payment, and reversal of EPC profits on group IPP projects. Management reiterated FY27 sales guidance of INR2,000 crore and a consolidated EBITDA margin of about 19-20%, with renewable EPC execution expected to ramp in Q3 and Q4. Debt rose to INR703.9 crore and receivables to INR321.8 crore, and management now expects OCF to turn positive only from Q4.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the 800-900 bps YoY margin decline, and what is the INR178 crore 'other construction and operating expenses' line?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited West Asia-driven input cost inflation, plus accounting entries: interest on the deferred Suyog Urja payment and reversal of EPC profits on group IPP projects. It described the line as direct costs (manpower, civil labour, job works, purchases) and suggested reading it together with purchase cost; no further breakdown was given.

qa_highlights.question: What consolidated margin should be expected going forward?
qa_highlights.answer: Consolidated EBITDA margin of about 19-20%, with water at about 21% and renewables at 15-18%. Renewable profitability is expected to rise in Q3 and Q4 as BESS and wind EPC scale up.

qa_highlights.question: Is FY27 guidance intact and how will H2 revenue be delivered?
qa_highlights.answer: Sales guidance of INR2,000 crore and PAT of INR240-250 crore are maintained; H1 delivered about INR700 crore and the balance is to come in Q3 and Q4 from the existing order book.

qa_highlights.question: When will OCF turn positive and why is it negative?
qa_highlights.answer: OCF is expected positive from Q4 FY27. H1 was hit by about INR57 crore rise in service concession receivables (over 15 years) and trade payable days falling from 93 to 63 (about INR102 crore outgo).

qa_highlights.question: What is the peak debt level and when?
qa_highlights.answer: Debt-to-equity is about 0.53 now and should close FY27 at no more than 0.6. Term loans will rise moderately for HAM and IPP projects; short-term WC lines are expected to fall as cash cycles ease.

qa_highlights.question: Will the water share of the order book decline as renewables grow?
qa_highlights.answer: No; management says the water business is the core with 35 years of history. It is bidding selectively, not lowering profitability guidance, and is comfortable waiting for quality orders given the current book.

risks_watch: Margin compression: consolidated EBITDA margin 20.58% vs 28.56% a year ago; guided 19-20% for the year, with renewable margins at 15-18%.
Working capital and leverage: receivables up to INR321.8 crore from INR155.3 crore; borrowings up to INR703.9 crore; OCF negative in H1 with positive OCF targeted only from Q4.
H2 revenue ramp needed: about INR1,300 crore in Q3 and Q4 to hit INR2,000 crore; renewable EPC execution must accelerate.
Order inflow gap: INR2,250 crore of the INR2,500 crore water guidance still to be won in FY27, amid rising competition.
Input cost inflation from the West Asia conflict, with only partial pass-through.
Disclosure: management declined to break down the INR178 crore other construction and operating expense line in detail.
544290|2026-09.management_tone: Confident on execution, guidance and order book, but defensive on margins and cash flow: management attributed the margin fall to accounting entries and input costs rather than operations. Answers on the INR178 crore cost line and OCF timing were vague or repetitive.
key_quotes: We are not interested in lowering the profitability guidance.
We maintain our guidance. There is no change.
There has been an implication of some interest costs which has been taken as an expense.
We expect that Q4 onwards, we should be OCF positive.

rows.why: Consolidated EBITDA margin fell to 20.58% from 28.56% YoY and guidance is 19-20% for FY27, with renewables at 15-18% and water at about 21%; West Asia input inflation and partial pass-through weigh.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Parli 180 MW wind due by March 2027, Mathura HAM COD soon, Bangalore projects now under execution, and BESS 930 MWh NTPC order largely due by June 2026 should add execution capacity; no new plant capex was discussed.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Revenue guidance of INR2,000 crore held, requiring about INR1,300 crore in H2 versus INR723 crore in H1 (+54% YoY), backed by a INR6,778 crore order book and renewable EPC ramp in Q3-Q4.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: FY27 PAT was cut to INR240-250 crore and margins are guided down to 19-20%, while the H2 revenue ramp remains unproven.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: H2 needs about INR1,300 crore revenue (1.8x H1 pace), water order inflow is only about INR250 crore against INR2,500 crore target, and input costs are partly unpassed.

rows.label: Water order inflow gap vs INR2,500 crore target
rows.why: About INR250 crore won so far against INR2,250 crore still targeted for FY27, amid competition rising over the past 5-6 months.

rows.label: OCF turns positive from Q4 FY27
rows.why: Management guided OCF positive from Q4 after H1 was hit by about INR57 crore service concession receivable rise and payable days falling from 93 to 63 (about INR102 crore outgo); receivables rose to INR321.8 crore from INR155.3 crore.

rows.label: Debt-to-equity capped at 0.6 at FY27 close
rows.why: Debt-to-equity is about 0.53 with borrowings at INR703.9 crore vs INR422.3 crore at FY26 end; management expects it not above 0.6 despite moderate term loan rise for HAM and IPP.

tone.note: Management was confident on order book, revenue guidance and execution ramp but defensive on the 800-900 bps margin fall, attributing it to input costs and accounting entries; analysts pressed on the INR178 crore cost line and OCF timing, which got vague answers.

544291|2026-03.headline: FY26 revenue rose 52% to ₹1,628 Cr with PAT of ₹143 Cr (8.8% margin); order book stands at ₹3,326 Cr with ₹2,200 Cr of bids pending results.
544291|2026-03.overview: Rajesh Power reported FY26 revenue of ₹1,628 Cr (+52% YoY), EBITDA of ₹197 Cr (+59%, 12.1% margin) and PAT of ₹143 Cr (+48%, 8.8% margin). H2 FY26 revenue rose 30% YoY to ₹990 Cr, but H2 EBITDA margin (11.4%) and PAT margin (8.5%) were lower than full-year levels, which management attributed to billing mix. Order inflow for FY26 was ₹2,743 Cr and the unexecuted order book closed at ₹3,326 Cr, below the ~₹4,500 Cr previously flagged, which management blamed on delayed tender results. Receivables rose sharply to ~₹350 Cr, which management attributed to heavy March billing, and payables rose to about 58 days.

segments.name: Power distribution
segments.commentary: 71% of the ₹3,326 Cr order book (₹2,365 Cr). Management cites ~₹5,000 Cr addressable distribution opportunity in Gujarat, part of the robust infrastructure scheme. Competitors per bid: 4 to 6.

segments.name: Power transmission
segments.commentary: 29% of the order book (₹961 Cr). Pan-India push into Rajasthan, Maharashtra, Odisha, Jharkhand and Uttarakhand; Gujarat is 85-90% of the total order book. Competitors per bid: 3 to 4.

segments.name: BESS (battery energy storage)
segments.commentary: Signed a 65 MW / 130 MWh standalone project for GUVNL on a build-own-operate, rental basis. Targeted IRR 10-12%; billing ~₹14-15 Cr per year; execution expected by September 2027, with Q1 FY27 mentioned as a possible earlier date.

guidance_outlook: Revenue growth guidance of ~35-40% retained; management said 40% growth is planned for FY27 and roughly 40% CAGR over the next 3-4 years.
EBITDA margin guided at 11-12% and PAT margin at 8-9%, described as stabilised rather than rising.
FY26 order inflow target of ₹4,000-5,000 Cr targeted for the year ahead; closing order book target above ₹5,000 Cr for FY27.
Pending bids of ~₹2,200 Cr expected to conclude by end-May or first week of June 2026; combined bid book (~₹5,700-6,000 Cr) assumed at ~40% win rate.
Gujarat share of order book expected to move toward 80:20 (Gujarat:outside) in the near term from 85-90% today.
Working capital cycle of 30-40 days described as sustainable.
capex_capacity: BESS: capex estimated at ₹1.5-2.5 Cr per MW; project funded 70-80% by bank debt with the balance as equity (absolute equity amount not yet quantified).
BESS revenue: ₹1.89 lakh per MW, giving ~₹14-15 Cr annual billing on 65 MW.
First 400 kV GIS project for a private Gujarat client expected to commission in September-October 2026.
FY26 execution: 350+ feeders, 4,000+ ring main units, 1,200+ distribution transformers, 1,300+ km of cable laid; over 51,000 km of MVCC work under execution in Gujarat.
Projects are typically executed in 18-24 months; the company says upcoming mobilisation of a few projects is expected within the next 2 months.
demand_pricing: Addressable market claimed at ~₹14,000-15,000 Cr per year across Gujarat (GETCO ~₹4,000-4,500 Cr addressable from ~₹10,000 Cr annual capex; distribution ~₹5,000 Cr), Rajasthan, Maharashtra, Uttarakhand, Odisha, Jharkhand, and railway traction substations.
Price escalation clauses cover most items; management says raw material (aluminium, copper) increases are passed through back-to-back with no margin impact.
Cable-jointer attrition cited at 2-3%. Labour camps are placed near sites and management reports no LPG/West Asia-related labour shortage.
Insurance surety bonds now used in ~8-10% of non-Gujarat orders and expected to rise as more states include the clause in tenders.
Current L1 position: about ₹210 Cr of pre-tax value (H1 FY26 figure was ₹808 Cr).

qa_highlights.question: Why did receivables (~₹350 Cr) and inventory jump versus H1 and last year?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is a short-term effect from very high March billing, with no BESS receivables and no client payment delays; standard terms of 45-60 days stay. About ₹150 Cr had been collected from the ~₹348 Cr receivables by the call date. Debtor days are ~78 and are expected to return to ~60 as billing evens out.

qa_highlights.question: Why did the order book fall short of the ~₹4,500 Cr target for FY26?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there was no shortfall in execution; the ~₹2,200 Cr of bids submitted in Q4 are still awaiting tender results, expected by end-May or early June 2026.

qa_highlights.question: Why did H2 gross and EBITDA margins decline, and what is the normal range?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the decline to billing mix. It sees project-level EBITDA of 11-12% and PAT of 8-9% as the normal range.

qa_highlights.question: Why did employee costs fall in H2 despite higher volumes?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said corporate and project-management employee costs are not scaling with revenue. Its later figures showed employee cost rose from ₹43.9 Cr in FY25 to ₹59 Cr in FY26.

qa_highlights.question: What is the BESS economics (ownership, revenue, IRR, margin)?
qa_highlights.answer: The company will own and develop the 65 MW / 130 MWh asset, with monthly rental billing to GUVNL from around September 2027. Targeted IRR is 10-12%. Management said margins should match transmission, and that it is not bidding for more BESS projects, preferring BESS EPC.

qa_highlights.question: Is the working-capital stress visible in creditors, MSME dues and short-term borrowings?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there is no working-capital stress. Payables stretched to ~30-day credit terms from vendors, and MSME outstanding of ₹87 Cr was paid within 45 days except where agreed terms exceeded that.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 400 kV GIS project and 765 kV expansion a margin opportunity?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the 400 kV GIS project with a private Gujarat client is due for commissioning around September-October 2026. It described the margin commitment as stabilised at 11-12%, not expanding.

risks_watch: Receivables of ~₹350 Cr and debtor days of ~78 (vs ~60 target) need to normalise in the next quarter.
Conversion of the ~₹2,200 Cr pending bids by end-May or early June 2026, plus the ₹4,000-5,000 Cr FY27 inflow target.
Gujarat concentration (85-90% of order book) and early-stage non-Gujarat transmission entries.
Rising surety bond requirements may affect working capital in new states.
Associate HKRP contribution fell in H2 due to customer site-readiness delays; recovery expected over the next year.
BESS project capex and equity requirement are not yet quantified; commissioning timeline is September 2027 (possibly Q1 FY27).
Payables stretched to ~58 days; sustainability of vendor credit terms is open.

544291|2026-09.headline: H1 FY27 revenue rose 46% YoY to INR 929 crore, with EBITDA margin of 12% and PAT up 35% to INR 79 crore.
544291|2026-09.overview: Rajesh Power reported H1 FY27 revenue of INR 929 crore (up 46% YoY), EBITDA of INR 112 crore (up 33%, 12% margin) and PAT of INR 79 crore (up 35%, 8.5% margin). Management highlighted first positive operating cash flow and an unexecuted order book of about INR 3,647 crore at 30 September 2026, with INR 450 crore more inflows in October. Growth narrative shifted toward transmission (400 kV, moving to 765 kV), BESS EPC, HKRP smart-grid SCADA/DMS, and new geographies (Odisha, New Zealand). Analysts pressed hard on receivables growth versus revenue and on HKRP's contribution, and management's answers on the receivables bridge were not fully reconciled on the call.

segments.name: Distribution (Gujarat)
segments.commentary: PGVCL order of about INR 800 to 900 crore with 18 to 24 month execution; management sees Gujarat distribution tendering of INR 5,000 to 6,000 crore a year. Distribution is not being bid outside Gujarat currently.

segments.name: Transmission
segments.commentary: RVPNL 132 kV GIS substation order in Jodhpur and OPTCL EPC order of INR 212 crore (June 2026, Odisha). Company executes 400 kV substations and expects to qualify for 765 kV after commissioning its current 400 kV project in a couple of months.

segments.name: HKRP Innovations (JV / associate)
segments.commentary: Contributed lower share of profit in H1 and is H2-weighted. Three SCADA/DMS projects in UGVCL, DGVCL and PGVCL; FY27 target of about INR 150 crore revenue and 20% PAT margin on a standalone basis. No HKRP orders in the company's order book.

segments.name: BESS
segments.commentary: 65 MW / 130 MWh standalone project at Virpur, Gujarat. Company bids only on EPC, not BOT; BESS EPC pipeline about INR 200 to 300 crore. Management says BESS revenue and margin contribution will be marginal in FY27.

segments.name: New Zealand (new subsidiary)
segments.commentary: Wholly owned subsidiary Rajesh Power Services NZ Limited set up; evaluating two or three opportunities in EPC for solar integration. No investment quantum disclosed.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth guidance of about 35% to 40% maintained; management reiterated 40% and that the longer-term growth guidance (4 to 5 years) is unchanged.
EBITDA margin guidance of 11% to 12% and PAT margin of 8% to 9% maintained.

Cumulative execution: 17,000+ ring main units, 6,500+ distribution transformers, 11,400 km of LT/HT/11 kV cable, about 35,000 km of MV covered conductor (about 25,000 km under execution), 104 air-insulated substations commissioned (four in H1), 2,700+ km of EHV cable.
H1 FY27 installations: 2,700+ RMUs, 300+ distribution transformers, 905 km cable laid, 10,800 km covered conductor, 157 km EHV cable, 12,000 poles erected.
Management expects to qualify for 765 kV substation bids after commissioning the current 400 kV project in a couple of months; entry into 765 kV not expected in FY27.

demand_pricing: H1 FY27 fresh order inflows of INR 1,250 crore (analyst cited about INR 1,700 crore for April to November); October inflows about INR 450 crore.

Gujarat Wire-Free City Mission targets about 46,000 circuit km of undergrounding by 2030; Odisha government plans about INR 16,000 crore of 765/400/220 kV and underground projects.
SCADA/DMS pan-India opportunity estimated above INR 3,000 crore; states tendering include Maharashtra, Assam, Kerala, UP, Bihar and Uttarakhand.

qa_highlights.question: Is the HKRP profit share H2-heavy and what is the order book contribution from HKRP?
qa_highlights.answer: HKRP is H2-heavy with targeted margins expected by year-end. There are no HKRP orders in the order book; it is 100% parent.

qa_highlights.question: Is there a slowdown or project slippage behind the inventory jump versus H1 FY26?
qa_highlights.answer: No. Management said inventory is only INR 100 to 125 crore and nothing similar is happening.

qa_highlights.question: Are receivables plus retention up more than 100% YoY against 45% revenue growth, and is working capital improving?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited receivables of INR 324 crore versus INR 174 crore, with INR 150 to 200 crore of H1 revenue booked in September. It said the improvement comes from better collections and longer supplier credit. Management did not reconcile the YoY retention jump (INR 8 crore to INR 58 crore) to the analyst's satisfaction.

qa_highlights.question: Is the company's working-capital view consistent with the cash-flow target and H2 expectations?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects better or similar working capital in H2 and targets positive operating cash flow for full FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company disclose quarterly numbers?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said June-month execution figures were already given and it would follow a similar approach through the year; no quarterly P&L was committed.

qa_highlights.question: Is the company still on track for 40% growth and 11% to 12% EBITDA margin?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes, management maintained FY27 guidance of about 40% growth (35% to 40% per analyst) and 11% to 12% EBITDA margin, with PAT of 8% to 9%.

qa_highlights.question: What are the nature and size of transactions with HKRP Innovations, which the annual report lists as purchases of about INR 500 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: HKRP provides GIS mapping and tech support on distribution projects. Management said the higher approved limit avoids repeated AGM approvals as new projects are won.
