544292|2026-03.headline: Q4 FY26 revenue rose 47% QoQ to INR4,282 million and EBITDA reached INR919 million, while management reiterated the FY28 target of US$400 million revenue at ~40% EBITDA margin.
544292|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 showed a sharp sequential recovery after a weak Q3, driven by the start of invoicing for drug-device combinations (DDC) and the India Semaglutide launch at the end of the quarter. Full-year revenue fell 2% YoY to INR14,216 million and EBITDA fell about 35%, both hit by delayed Semaglutide approvals. Management deferred the Steriscience injectables and Brooks merger scheme, citing smaller-investor valuation concerns and a lower listed-company share price, and said it will revisit in about two years. Capacity expansion remains on track, with a new DDC line expected to be available from next quarter and three lines installed by end FY27.

segments.name: DDC (drug-device combinations) / Semaglutide
segments.commentary: Invoicing began this year; Canada approvals received for two partners, and shipments to both Canadian partners have commenced. Current line is fully committed back-to-back, and the new 500-litre-capable line is expected to be available from next quarter.

segments.name: Injectables and soft gelatin (base business)
segments.commentary: Signed 10 new licences, launched 15-plus products and added customers during the year. Soft gelatin capacity is expected to be fully utilised within the current period, and a fourth injectable line is coming in unit two.

segments.name: Biologics (nascent)
segments.commentary: Funnel expanded almost 4x YoY; a European biosimilar partner, a US biosimilar major and a second animal-health project from a top-three global player were added. Management expects a meaningful contribution in FY28 and commercial manufacturing from FY29; no revenue or EBITDA split was disclosed.

guidance_outlook: FY28 guidance reiterated: US$400 million organic revenue at around 40% EBITDA margin; FY27 guidance not given beyond expecting a strong year and a sequential improvement in revenue and EBITDA each quarter.
Medium-term target of 50%-plus ROCE.
Working capital is expected to normalise during FY27 after elevated levels this year.
Soft gelatin and injectables trending close to the US$100 million mark, with further growth expected.
Saudi Arabia Semaglutide launch described as imminent, now that freedom to operate is in place.
Scheme with Steriscience injectables and Brooks deferred; to be revisited in about two years if strategic intent holds.
capex_capacity: Part of a US$100 million capex programme; the new line installed a couple of months ago is in qualification and expected to be available from Q1 FY27 (next quarter), with commercial availability in Q2.
Two additional lines are planned this year, giving three lines by end FY27; a fourth injectable line is coming in unit two.

Existing line capped at 200-litre batch size; new lines can go to 500 litres, and up to 750-1,000 litres in the longer term. Moving from 200 to 500 litres raises output about 2.5x (about 60,000 pens/day at 200 litres).
Sterile manufacturing capacity framed as about 225 sterile days per line, roughly 675 days across three lines.
Capacity expansion fully funded through incremental domestic and international bank borrowings; the company added about 400 people at its flagship site.
demand_pricing: Management says demand exceeds supply for at least the next two years; customers have reserved capacity with upfront fees and take-or-pay contracts.

qa_highlights.question: Why did EBITDA margin decline from 33.8% to 31.8%?
qa_highlights.answer: Fixed costs for new centres rose, with pre-operative and rental costs; management did not quantify the drag.

544293|2026-06.headline: Suraksha Diagnostic Q1 FY27 total income rose 21% YoY to INR 887 million, with PAT up 40% to INR 128 million and EBITDA margin at 36%.

544294|2026-03.headline: Q4 FY26 revenue rose 62% YoY to about INR142 crores; FY26 revenue up 87% to INR485 crores, but margins fell and management guided to similar growth in FY27.
544294|2026-03.overview: Management reported its strongest quarter yet, with Q4 revenue of about INR142 crores (up 62% YoY) and profit of about INR9.5 crores. For FY26, revenue rose 87% to INR485 crores, PBT rose from INR10 crores to INR28 crores, and EBITDA rose from INR38 crores to INR66 crores. Margins were lower than previously guided, which management attributed to qualification and investment costs for new semiconductor and space customers. Management guided to similar growth in FY27 and said margins would improve, and it is pursuing a QIP sized at about 7-10% of market cap.

544296|2026-03.headline: Nisus standalone core revenue rose 110% YoY to INR 141 crore and PAT to INR 68 crore (48% margin) in FY26, with Q4 PAT of INR 11 crore.
544296|2026-03.overview: FY26 was the first full year as a listed company, and management said core standalone revenue (ex-NCCCL) of INR 141 crore beat the INR 120-140 crore guidance despite a Q4 slowdown tied to West Asia conflict. Q4 core PAT was INR 11 crore, and the consolidated group (including NCCCL, acquired August 2025) reported revenue of INR 575 crore and PAT of INR 83 crore. Management said UAE transactions worth over INR 500 crore were deferred rather than lost, and FY27 guidance is presented as a two-scenario framework rather than a point estimate. NCCCL's PAT rose to INR 16.4 crore from INR 3.5 crore, and its order book was INR 1,833 crore at March-end, plus INR 870 crore added in April-May 2026.

financial_highlights.change: ~4.7x from INR 3.5 crore; NCCCL top line up ~7%

segments.name: Fund and asset management (core)
segments.commentary: Management said fund and asset management is now about 55% of core revenue versus advisory at about 45%; fee income is largely from sponsor capital in own funds plus treasury/investment income. UAE GCC portfolio of four assets reported 30% NAV growth in latest valuation, with management saying no impairment.

segments.name: Transaction advisory (core)
segments.commentary: Advisory held firm in Q4 despite the UAE transaction slowdown and was described as the counter-cyclical offset; advisory share was 67% of revenue when the business started versus about 55% now.

segments.name: NCCCL (construction/EPC, consolidated from Aug 2025)
segments.commentary: Order book INR 1,833 crore at 31 March 2026, plus INR 870 crore added in first two months of FY27 (management cites ~INR 2,600-2,700 crore total). Repaid about 65% of acquisition debt (INR 38 crore outstanding at March 31); EBITDA margin about 9%, PAT margin about 2-3%.

segments.name: Tokenisation (UAE)
segments.commentary: Presented as a separate digital asset business in the UAE entity; awaiting token issuance licence and white paper approval, with live launch hoped for within FY27. No financial contribution quantified.

guidance_outlook: FY27 core business: management referenced an EM (equity/assets under management) target of INR 4,500-5,000 crore; the Nisus Neon fund (INR 1,800 crore, INR 500 crore green shoe) received SEBI approval and launches from Q2 FY27, with fees broadly INR 220 crore.

FY27 revenue-to-AUM ratio assumed at around 2.85% (blended), with management calling 3% a steady-state assumption versus 5.3-5.6% in FY26, which included one-off UAE advisory contracts and book investment gains.
NCCCL FY27 target of about INR 850 crore revenue; management aims for 3-4x turnover over the next year per Vice Chairman, with EBITDA margins of 9-10%.
REIC Ops fund (launched 2019) expected to wind up in 2026, with management fee booking expected more likely in Q2 FY27.
Pipeline: India about INR 700 crore (60-70% at term sheet); UAE about INR 2,000 crore being renegotiated on entry prices; management expects India deployment over the next couple of quarters.
capex_capacity: Own prop book investment grew to about INR 2,125 crore (almost 4x), per management; a separate slide cited INR 48 crore to INR 128 crore growth for a different measure, so the figures should be verified against the presentation.

Two India transactions (about INR 150 crore each) slipped by a few months due to Pune land demarcation methodology change, lender committee NOC delays, and RERA/e-Khata issues in Gujarat, Karnataka and Telangana; management expects these to close in the current quarter.
UAE deferred deals: one INR 500 crore transaction and one INR 300 crore transaction pushed to later closure.
NCCCL migrating to SAP HANA and adopting digital project management tools.
demand_pricing: Dubai: off-plan share fell from about 78% last year to much smaller levels as ready-to-move-in inventory rose to about 60-70%; investor purchases fell from about 87% (2017-18) to about 45%, with end-users at about 55%.

Dubai pricing: management cited 10-15% discounts from January levels in Dubai and 5% in Abu Dhabi, with a weighted average market discount of roughly 15-20%; management said its own assets were up around 30% in valuation.
Management said it is buying at discounts to market and that renegotiation of entry prices is underway on the INR 2,000 crore UAE pipeline.
NCCCL works on 3-4 year order book visibility; industry EBITDA norm 9-10%, PAT 3-4%.
Management said advisory fees are directly correlated with AUM and fund size, and that the blended AUM-fee mix should shift toward management fees over time.

qa_highlights.question: What regulatory or lender-approval delays pushed India transactions out, and what is the status?
qa_highlights.answer: Avadhoot Sarwate said Pune demarcation methodology changed, and consortium lender NOCs took longer (March to May); about two trades of roughly INR 150 crore each slipped by a few months and are expected this quarter. Gujarat RERA and Bengaluru e-Khata were also cited as slowing approvals.

qa_highlights.question: What are the Neon Fund size, fees and timing, and REIC Ops closure economics?
qa_highlights.answer: Aanchal Singh said SEBI approval for the Neon Fund came the previous day, with launch from Q2; INR 1,800 crore fund plus INR 500 crore green shoe, fees broadly INR 220 crore, 7.5-year tenure. REIC Ops has a 12% hurdle with no catch-up, closing this year, with fees more likely in Q2.

qa_highlights.question: What is the core run-rate fee income excluding one-time investment gains, and how does revenue compare to cost base?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the segment reporting does not split recurring fees from treasury income; fee income is described as small relative to the fund and asset management segment, which includes treasury income from sponsor capital in own funds. No quantified run-rate was given.

qa_highlights.question: Why is FY27 revenue-to-AUM assumed at 2.85% versus 5.3% in FY26?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said FY26 was inflated by high-margin UAE advisory contracts and book investment gains on yield compression; 3% is the steady-state assumption, and capital is expected to deploy mainly in H2 FY27.

qa_highlights.question: What is the status of the India (INR 700 crore) and UAE (INR 2,000 crore) pipelines?
qa_highlights.answer: Avadhoot Sarwate said 60-70% of the India pipeline is at term sheet stage, with deployment in the next couple of quarters. For UAE, management said 50-60% of the pipeline is at a complete stage, and at least INR 800 crore of transactions were deferred.

qa_highlights.question: Why did standalone employee costs rise to 32% of revenue, and what is the outlook for NCCCL margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited new hires, annual appraisals, and a change to accrual-based bonus accounting from this year. NCCCL margins target 9-10% EBITDA with 2-3% PAT, with growth coming from volume.

risks_watch: UAE real estate weakness: off-plan decline, lower investor demand, and deferrals of INR 500-800 crore deals; management did not give a timeline for stabilisation.

NCCCL execution: PAT margins of about 2-3%, dependence on order inflows, and a stated target of 3-4x revenue next year.

Stock price weakness since IPO (~50% down per an investor question); management attributed this to market perception rather than fundamentals.
Tokenisation and Neon fund launches depend on regulatory approvals (token licence and white paper; SEBI approved Neon fund).

544304|2026-06.headline: Jungle Camps Q1 FY27 revenue rose 12% YoY to ₹5.97 cr, but EBITDA fell to ₹1.69 cr (27% margin) after a ₹0.52 cr exceptional charge.
544304|2026-06.overview: Q1 FY27 revenue from operations grew 12% YoY to ₹5.97 cr, with occupancy up 2 pts to 45% and RevPAR up 9% to ₹4,763. EBITDA declined to ₹1.69 cr from ₹1.81 cr and margin compressed to 27% from 32%, partly from new-property ramp-up costs and a ₹0.52 cr exceptional charge tied to the discontinued Parsili project. PAT fell to ₹0.47 cr from ₹1.13 cr. Management outlined Devprayag and Palash Kothi (42 rooms combined) as FY27 additions, Mathura (105 rooms, IHG Holiday Inn Express) and Sheopur Fort (35–40 rooms in phase 1) for FY28, and a debt build-up to about ₹50 cr by FY28.

Mathura (IHG Holiday Inn Express, scaled to 105 rooms) targeted for FY28 opening; revenue estimate ₹18–20 cr/yr, with management comfortable even at ₹12 cr; project cost ₹49 cr with ₹32 cr HDFC debt at 8.14%; lease rental 5% of gross revenue or ₹54 lakh, whichever higher.

qa_highlights.question: What ADR growth can be expected for full-year FY27, given Q1 ADR up ~5% YoY and H2 seasonality?
qa_highlights.answer: Management confirmed October–March (H2) should deliver better ADR and revenue than April–June, but gave no formal FY27 number; it said it is 'quite hopeful' of ~5% YoY ADR growth. FY26 property ADRs cited: Pench ₹9,248, Tadoba ₹12,300, Kanha ₹9,500, Rukhad ₹11,800, Bison ₹3,500.

qa_highlights.question: Is 40% FY26 occupancy low, and can it improve?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the park is closed for about three months (July–September), so 40% is ~54% on the open period; wildlife occupancy tops out near 60%, with Tadoba at 57%. Mathura and other new properties are expected to lift the numbers, with a 12-month operating model for Mathura and Sheopur.

qa_highlights.question: Will EBITDA spike in FY27 or stay flat, and how quickly do new properties break even?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Devprayag and Palash Kothi will add top-line and bottom-line growth this year. New properties take about 4–6 months, up to 6 months, to stabilise, and management agreed break-even around six months after commissioning is a fair read.

qa_highlights.question: What are the revenue terms for Palash Kothi and Devprayag, and what ADRs are guided?
qa_highlights.answer: Palash Kothi (20 rooms, Bandhavgarh) pays Jungle Camps a 13% revenue fee and operates October to June, ADR ₹8,000–12,000. Devprayag (22 rooms, leased from UP Tourism) starts in Q2 FY27 with ADR ₹5,000–6,000, capex up to ₹1 cr, and lease rental ₹28,000 per year.

qa_highlights.question: What is the debt build-up, interest rate and repayment schedule for Mathura and Sheopur?
qa_highlights.answer: Mathura project cost is ₹49 cr with ₹32 cr HDFC debt at 8.14%; Sheopur budget ₹25 cr with ~₹17.5 cr HDFC loan and ₹10.5 cr internal. Both loans have a 2-year moratorium then 7-year repayment, combined EMI ~₹53 lakh/month (~₹6.5 cr/yr). Management said debt reaching ~₹50 cr by FY28 is correct and no working capital debt is needed.

qa_highlights.question: What revenue is expected from Mathura and Sheopur, and is debt serviceable at downside?
qa_highlights.answer: Mathura revenue estimate ₹18–20 cr/yr, with management comfortable even at ~₹12 cr. Sheopur first-year revenue at least ₹12 cr on ~35 rooms, with 8–10 weddings a year and ~15% other occupancy cited as a cushion. Mathura lease rental is 5% of gross revenue or ₹54 lakh, whichever is higher.

qa_highlights.question: How were the two land-related incidents (Parsili and a second site) handled, and what due-diligence changes followed?
qa_highlights.answer: Around ₹70–75 lakh was invested in the first site; ~₹50 lakh is being written off, with some assets moved to another property. Management said due diligence now includes forest department engagement upfront and checks of revenue, police and court records. It said there is no significant challenge at Sheopur or Mathura, but development timelines apply.

544305|2026-03.headline: Q4 FY26 EBITDA positive at INR 174 mn (5.9% margin) and PAT INR 44 mn; FY26 EBITDA still negative INR 52 mn after heavy reinvestment.
544305|2026-03.overview: MobiKwik reported back-to-back EBITDA- and PAT-positive quarters in Q3 and Q4 FY26, with Q4 total income of INR 2,960 mn (+6% YoY) and contribution margin of 46% versus 23% a year earlier. FY26 EBITDA improved to negative INR 52 mn from negative INR 794 mn, and full-year PAT narrowed to negative INR 621 mn from negative INR 1,215 mn. Management said it is deliberately reinvesting core payments and lending profits (about INR 55 crore spent in FY26) into four growth engines: offline and online merchant payments, an NBFC, and AI. Analysts pressed on the gap between UPI-led GMV growth and flat payments revenue, on the timing of breakeven for merchant businesses, and on NBFC rollout.

financial_highlights.change: underlying INR 81 mn before INR 37.6 mn one-time labour code charge
from negative INR 794 mn in FY25
from negative INR 1,215 mn in FY25

financial_highlights.value: INR 117 crore (incl. INR 4 crore one-off exceptional)

financial_highlights.metric: Remaining debt (working capital lines) at 31 Mar 2026

segments.name: Payments (wallet, UPI, recharge and bill payments)
segments.commentary: Wallet is the largest in India by GTV with about 20% share as of March 2026. Customer-initiated UPI transactions grew 170% YoY vs industry 26%. Recharge and bill payments GMV reached INR 269 bn in FY26 (2.2x). Payments revenue has been flat for 4-5 quarters as UPI mix rises and gross take rate falls.

segments.name: Lending (digital credit, LSP model)
segments.commentary: Management cited a 59% gross margin in Q4, with super-prime share of disbursements up from 10% to 32% and repeat loans up from 20% to 63.5%. Lending spread was 5.3% (analyst cited 5.4%); management sees 4.5% as more sustainable, with 4% as the sweet spot. FY26 digital credit GMV was about INR 3,200 crore.

segments.name: Merchant payments (offline and Zaakpay online)
segments.commentary: Offline targets 5x device scale-up for 10x revenue by FY28; Zaakpay targets 10x GMV by FY28. Both are guided to reach EBITDA breakeven by FY28. Merchant partners stand at 4.9 mn.

guidance_outlook: GMV growth of 30-35% expected in both payments and lending in FY27 (per management).
Digital credit GMV growth of 30-35% in FY27.
FY27 EBITDA margin guided in the same broad range as the current ~5%, with better unit margins offset by higher investment.
Merchant-business investment of roughly INR 55 crore in FY26 expected to be similar in FY27; investment to continue for at least 18 months.
Fixed costs at INR 115-120 crore per quarter; 15-20% increase expected in FY27 from depreciation and device-distribution people costs.
Payments margin guided at 12-15 bps mid-to-long term; management advised against modelling 16 bps over two years.
NBFC timeline: move LSP business into a wholly owned subsidiary in 2-3 months, set up NBFC in 3-6 months, launch co-lending disbursals in 6-9 months.
Target of 10-20% of the market leader's size in offline merchant categories in 18-24 months; Zaakpay 10x GMV in about 18-24 months.
Management expects payments revenue to follow GMV growth from the next few quarters once PPI-over-UPI MDR is implemented.
capex_capacity: Merchant device investment is capitalised and depreciated; other merchant spend (people, product) is expensed through P&L. INR 55 crore total FY26 investment excludes device capex.
Depreciation rising as merchant devices are deployed.
Part of unencumbered cash is still IPO proceeds not yet available, which trickle in as used; IPO funds also being used for merchant investment and will hit P&L.
NBFC to be funded by parent capital infusion into the wholly owned NBFC subsidiary, subject to board and shareholder approval.
demand_pricing: Payments revenue flat for 4-5 quarters despite GMV growth: UPI mix dilutes gross take rate, and some low-margin categories were added.
PPI-over-UPI MDR has not yet been implemented; management expects it to add revenue.
UPI credit and RuPay credit transactions generate MDR; plain bank UPI does not.
Net payments margin remains positive; gross take rate has moderated in existing businesses.
Lending: digital credit GMV growth was subdued QoQ as the company prioritised quality over volume.
Offline merchant focus on three categories: organised retail (mid-market and above), petrol and oil/gas, and small mom-and-pop stores. Zaakpay targets education, government and BBPS categories.

qa_highlights.question: What is being done to fix payments revenue growth, and is there long-term guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said revenue lags GMV because growth is UPI-led and PPI-over-UPI MDR has not yet come; consistent revenue growth is expected in the next few quarters.

qa_highlights.question: How much investment is needed in the merchant business over two years, and is it through P&L?
qa_highlights.answer: INR 55 crore was invested in FY26, and a similar range is expected in FY27. Everything except device capitalisation hits P&L, and IPO proceeds are being used for it.

qa_highlights.question: Why did the merchant breakeven timeline move from 3-4 quarters to FY28, and what does baseline profitability mean?
qa_highlights.answer: Fixed costs were raised deliberately to build new businesses; without the merchant investment FY26 EBITDA would have been about INR 50 crore. Management aims to stay PAT-positive while reinvesting, with FY27 EBITDA hypothetically between 1x and 2x of the reinvested base.

qa_highlights.question: Why is ex-UPI GTV growing above 30% while payments revenue is flat?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited gross take rate moderation and mix shift to lower-margin categories; the non-UPI revenue growth has been below expectations.

qa_highlights.question: What are the NBFC timelines and funding?
qa_highlights.answer: LSP business moves to a subsidiary in 2-3 months, NBFC set up in 3-6 months, and co-lending disbursals launch in 6-9 months. Parent will infuse capital after board and shareholder approval.

qa_highlights.question: Why is working capital debt still INR 261 crore when cash is INR 434 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: Part of the cash is still IPO proceeds not yet accessible; the short-term lines cover weekend and holiday settlement gaps when bank funds are delayed.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 5.3% lending margin sustainable and what is the payments margin outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management prefers 4.5% as more sustainable and 4% as the sweet spot, and guided 12-15 bps for payments mid-to-long term, though Q4 ran above that.

qa_highlights.question: What fixed-cost increase is expected next year?
qa_highlights.answer: Fixed costs are INR 115-120 crore per quarter; a 15-20% increase is expected in FY27.

risks_watch: Payments revenue has been flat for 4-5 quarters even as GMV rises; PPI-over-UPI MDR timing is uncertain.
Gross take-rate compression from UPI mix and low-margin categories.
Merchant investment of about INR 55 crore a year continues for at least 18 months, delaying group profitability; FY28 breakeven target for the merchant businesses.
FLDG capital is blocked against lending book growth and absorbs about 5% of credit cost.
Lending margin of 5.3% may normalise toward 4-4.5%; some gains came from previously matured cohorts.
Regulatory risk on payments MDR and on the NBFC licence and governance.
Working capital dependence (INR 261 crore) and finance cost reduction; IPO proceeds still being drawn down.
Merchant partner growth was only about 7% last year, with a more aggressive onboarding target not yet quantified.

544305|2026-06.headline: MobiKwik posted Q1 FY27 PAT of INR76 million, its third straight profitable quarter, with payments GMV up 50% YoY to INR587 billion.
544305|2026-06.overview: Management described Q1 FY27 as its most profitable quarter yet, with PAT of INR76 million and EBITDA of INR158 million, up INR470 million YoY. Payments gross profit rose 31% YoY to INR777 million and financial services gross profit grew 5.6x to INR433 million. Lending disbursements dipped in Q1, while payments revenue fell as card-linked categories were paused under regulatory pressure and UPI (near-zero take rate) grew. Management targets full-year PAT of about INR400 million and EBITDA of about INR750 million including other income, and is scaling a merchant acquiring business that is still loss-making.

financial_highlights.change: Swing of INR495 million vs Q1 FY26; up from INR45 million in Q4 per management
+50% YoY; 14th straight quarter of payments GMV growth

segments.name: Payments
segments.commentary: Gross profit INR777 million (+31% YoY) on revenue of about INR208 crore versus INR59 crore a year ago on similar revenue; net payments take rate 13-15 bps in recent quarters, guided at 12-14 bps long term. Zaakpay (payment gateway) GMV INR25.6 billion; revenue not disclosed.

segments.name: Financial services (lending)
segments.commentary: Gross profit INR433 million (5.6x YoY). Net financial services margin 4.1% in Q3, 5.4% in Q4 and 5.9% in Q1; management guides 4.5-5.5% long term. About 18% of gross lending revenue came from write-backs on past books (about INR16 crore).

segments.name: Merchant (Zaakpay online + offline acquiring)
segments.commentary: Merchant GMV INR125 billion, up 17% QoQ. Business is loss-making with an expected full-year burn of INR50-60 crore; breakeven targeted for FY28. Management expects 10x ramp over two years.

guidance_outlook: Full-year FY27 PAT target of about INR40 crore (INR400 million) and EBITDA of about INR75 crore (INR750 million) including other income; management said it is 'fairly confident'.
Lending disbursements to rise from about INR700 crore per quarter to INR1,000 crore per quarter; management says Q2 is already running at that rate.
Consumer payments revenue expected to grow 5-6% QoQ; merchant revenue expected to grow about 25% QoQ.
Merchant business burn for FY27 capped at INR50-60 crore; breakeven targeted in FY28.
Long-term net payments take rate guided at 12-14 bps; net financial services margin guided at 4.5-5.5%.
Paused card-linked payment categories expected to be relaunched in Q2 FY27.
Digital lending business transfer to wholly-owned subsidiary expected to close in August 2026; own NBFC launch still 'some time away'.
capex_capacity: About INR25 crore of IPO proceeds remains available for buying more merchant devices (soundboxes, EDC, QR); management does not expect more than this needed for FY27.
Merchant ramp: 10x over two years targeted; merchant counts, device counts and merchant revenue not disclosed yet.
Employee benefit expense rose from INR46 crore in Q4 to INR53 crore in Q1, mostly merchant business manpower; expected to rise 5-15% YoY, linked to breakeven.
Lending partner base: nine major NBFC partners in Q1 (10-15 total); top-three lender concentration cut from about 91% (Q2-Q3 FY26) to 87% in Q4 and 71% in Q1.
demand_pricing: Payments revenue dipped because high-take-rate card-linked categories (credit and debit) were paused, while low or zero take-rate UPI and merchant volumes grew; management attributes the pause to regulatory guardrail changes on categories such as rent and education.
Wallet transactions up 68% YoY but GMV up only 24%, as users shift to lower-ticket wallet-on-UPI payments on which no PPI MDR is earned.

UPI: MobiKwik's transactions grew 5x faster than the industry; ranked 13th in NPCI UPI stack rankings and described as second fastest-growing TPAP. No MDR on UPI; PPI-on-UPI MDR mandated by RBI but not rolled out by NPCI.

Lending: Q1 disbursements dipped; 60% of loans went to repeat customers and credit quality improved 25%. Cross-sell from about 96 million engaged non-lending users targeted at INR150-250 crore extra disbursement per quarter; AI funnel engine targeted at about INR100 crore per quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Why has quarterly revenue growth been muted over the last seven to eight quarters, and what levers will accelerate it?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said FY26 was spent re-stabilising businesses and Q1 is the baseline. Lending disbursements are to rise from about INR700 crore to INR1,000 crore per quarter via new lending partners, pre-approved offers to about 96 million engaged users, and an AI funnel engine. Card-linked categories were paused in Q4 and Q1 and are to be relaunched, while merchant revenue is to scale.

qa_highlights.question: Non-UPI GMV trend and whether take rate is falling?
qa_highlights.answer: Non-UPI GMV rose to INR317 billion from INR300 billion in Q4 (about 6%). Management said card-linked categories with higher take rates de-grew under regulatory pressure. Net payments take rate guidance remains 12-14 bps long term, at gross profit level, versus 13-15 bps in recent quarters.

qa_highlights.question: Merchant roll-out: what numbers and how should it be modelled?
qa_highlights.answer: Merchant GMV was INR125 billion, up 17% QoQ from INR107 billion. Management targets a 10x ramp over two years, expects merchant revenue to grow about 25% QoQ and consumer payments revenue 5-6% QoQ. Merchant counts, device counts and merchant revenue were withheld as too early. About INR25 crore of IPO proceeds remains for devices, and no more is expected to be needed in FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Own NBFC timing and FLDG share of lending?
qa_highlights.answer: Digital lending transfer to a wholly-owned subsidiary is expected to close in August 2026 after shareholder approval on 2 July, then CoR will be sought; own NBFC lending is 'still some time away'. As of Q1, 32% of lending was pure distribution and 68% FLDG, with a possible 40/60 mix by year-end.

qa_highlights.question: Is FY27 guidance of INR750 million EBITDA and INR400 million PAT still valid after Q1 operating EBITDA ex other income of about INR80 million?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is confident in the baseline and expects about INR400 million PAT for FY27 with some growth, plus about INR750 million EBITDA including other income. Q1 PAT of INR76 million annualises to about INR302 million, and improving by INR20-30 million per quarter would reach about INR400 million.

qa_highlights.question: Why did lending disbursements fall in Q1, and what is the top-three lender concentration?
qa_highlights.answer: Top-three lender concentration was cut from about 91% in Q2-Q3 FY26 to 87% in Q4 and 71% in Q1, with two new partners added in Q1. Management said the digital lending transfer to the subsidiary consumed focus in Q1, and it is already at the INR1,000 crore run rate in Q2.

qa_highlights.question: Why did wallet transactions grow 68% but GMV only 24%, and is PPI-on-UPI monetised?
qa_highlights.answer: Users shifted to lower-ticket wallet-on-UPI payments and card-linked pauses removed high-ticket transactions. No MDR is earned on PPI-on-UPI although RBI mandated it; NPCI has not rolled it out in about 2.5 years.

qa_highlights.question: Merchant business burn, breakeven timing and employee cost trajectory?
qa_highlights.answer: Merchant burn for FY27 is capped at INR50-60 crore (about INR15-16 crore in Q1); breakeven targeted for FY28. Employee benefit expense rose to INR53 crore from INR46 crore in Q4, and merchant-related manpower cost may grow 5-15% YoY, linked to breakeven.

risks_watch: Payments revenue dip from paused card-linked categories (credit and debit, rent, education); relaunch targeted for Q2 FY27 and not yet proven.
Lending disbursements fell in Q1; Q2 INR1,000 crore run rate depends on the digital lending transfer closing in August 2026 without disruption.
Gross take-rate compression as UPI (near-zero take rate) and merchant volumes grow; net payments take rate guided at 12-14 bps long term versus 13-15 bps recently.
Net financial services margin of 5.9% in Q1 includes write-backs (about 18% of gross lending revenue); management guides 4.5-5.5% long term.
Merchant business still loss-making (FY27 burn INR50-60 crore); merchant revenue, device and merchant counts not disclosed; breakeven FY28.
Regulatory dependence: PPI-on-UPI MDR mandated by RBI but not rolled out by NPCI; no timeline given.
Own NBFC launch still 'some time away'; CoR pending until digital lending transfer completes.
Q1 PAT of INR76 million rests on one quarter; full-year PAT of about INR400 million requires sustained sequential improvement of about INR20-30 million per quarter.
key_quotes: Q1 FY27 has been our most successful and profitable quarter yet.
We are targeting full-year PAT profitability for this financial year, and Q1 is of course the baseline.
So yes, INR75 crores EBITDA and INR40 crores PAT is the kind of numbers that we are fairly confident of achieving.
It's too early. Apart from the GMV for merchant, we are not revealing any other numbers yet.

Cautious and evasive on merchant metrics (no merchant counts, devices or revenue, calling it 'too early'), on regulatory issues around UPI MDR (expressed frustration), and on the timing of its own NBFC.

544305|2026-09.headline: MobiKwik posted record Q2 FY27 PAT of INR 11.8 crore and EBITDA of INR 22.7 crore (7.5% margin), its fourth straight profitable quarter.
544305|2026-09.overview: Total income rose 8% YoY to INR 302 crore and revenue from operations rose 9% YoY to INR 295 crore. Reported EBITDA reached INR 22.7 crore with margin of 7.5%, up 977 bps YoY and 204 bps QoQ, and PAT was INR 11.8 crore, up 55% QoQ. Contribution profit grew about 50% while GMV grew 34-35% YoY in both payments and lending, but consumer UPI GMV was soft QoQ on seasonality and a festive-season shift. Management guided to FY28 PAT of INR 100 crore if UPI MDR is implemented, versus earlier INR 75-80 crore.

financial_highlights.change: Above INR 1,000 crore guided last quarter
Merchant GMV +76% YoY, merchant revenue +150% YoY, +18% QoQ GMV, +29% QoQ revenue
Up 1 bp in quarter as stated

segments.name: Payments (consumer and merchant)
segments.commentary: GMV growth of about 34-35% YoY, but consumer UPI GMV fell QoQ in Q2 on seasonality. Consumer take rate is 16 bps plus; merchant net take rate is about 3-4 bps. Merchant share rising dilutes the consolidated take rate.

segments.name: Lending (digital distribution / FLDG)
segments.commentary: Disbursals of INR 1,083 crore in Q2 with 11 active lending partners. 79% of disbursals are under FLDG (5% DLG) and 21% under pure distribution. Processing fees run 3-4% upfront and NIM share accrues over 12-15 months.

guidance_outlook: UPI MDR, once implemented, expected to add at least INR 100 crore to payments revenue in FY28; INR 20-25 crore of that expected to reach EBITDA/PAT.
FY28 PAT target raised to about INR 100 crore if UPI MDR is implemented (earlier target INR 75-80 crore; FY27 target INR 40 crore).
Lending disbursals to keep growing with strong double-digit growth, though not at the same percentage rate.
Management expects better numbers in Q3 FY27 on festive-season spend; fixed costs as % of total income expected to decline in coming quarters.

NBFC plan: aim for about 10% of lending disbursals (about INR 600 crore out of an illustrative INR 6,000 crore) via own NBFC in co-lending 10:90, requiring about INR 60 crore equity; awaiting RBI go-ahead for CoR.
capex_capacity: NBFC: slump sale and migration of credit distribution business completed in August; all RBI conditions met, awaiting final RBI approval for Certificate of Registration before operations start.
Investment in people continuing to support merchant payments and NBFC build-out; employee cost increase described as deliberate build phase, with low base from Q2 FY26 cited.
Fixed costs at about 40% of total income.
demand_pricing: Consumer UPI competition is intense: MobiKwik ranks number 11 among TPAPs; management is shifting to higher-ticket users (transactions above INR 2,000) and deprioritising INR 150-200 ticket transactions.
Merchant side has 2-3 clear competitors per management; merchant net margin cited at 3.4 bps and merchant take rate expected to rise about 2.5 bps after UPI MDR.

UPI MDR: merchant gross take rate 40 bps on eligible transactions above INR 2,000; about 28 bps goes to ecosystem partners; management estimates 8-10 bps net realisable. Consumer side about 8 bps net.
Industry UPI value grew about 1% QoQ in Q2 versus roughly 4% in prior two quarters (NPCI data).
Lending: credit performance improving QoQ, enabling renegotiated partner contracts and better commercials with new partners, lowering lending-related costs as % of revenue.

qa_highlights.question: Why did UPI and PPI GMV decline QoQ, and how is consumer UPI growth going to improve?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited seasonally weak Q2 (industry UPI value +1% QoQ) with festive spend shifting to Q3, and a strategy shift to higher-ticket users above INR 2,000 that may depress near-term numbers; better Q3 expected.

qa_highlights.question: Lending take rate and expense ratios look low; is that due to late-quarter disbursals?
qa_highlights.answer: Soham Roy said disbursals were consistent across the three months; processing fees (3-4%) are upfront while NIM share flows over 12-15 months, so the larger denominator makes ratios look muted. Lending costs fell due to renegotiated partner contracts.

qa_highlights.question: How much FY28 benefit from UPI MDR and how much reaches the bottom line?
qa_highlights.answer: At least INR 100 crore of payments revenue uplift in FY28; roughly 20-25% (INR 20-25 crore) on the merchant side reaches EBITDA/PAT. Cost pass-through to issuing bank, TPAP and PSP is the main offset.

qa_highlights.question: Is lending partner appetite for FLDG versus distribution pushing growth?
qa_highlights.answer: 79% of disbursals are FLDG and 21% pure distribution; management is agnostic and balances both by risk-adjusted returns, staying within the RBI 5% DLG limit.

qa_highlights.question: Will payment take rates stabilise after UPI MDR?
qa_highlights.answer: Soham Roy said take rates were stable QoQ; merchant take rate will improve post-MDR and consumer take rate partially, with a 1-2 bps swing thereafter depending on merchant mix. Consolidated uplift will be smaller than the 2.5 bps peer example.

qa_highlights.question: How long will the employee-cost build phase last and when will fixed cost fall to around 30% of income?
qa_highlights.answer: Management will keep investing in people while it meets growth targets, but said fixed costs as % of total income should decline in upcoming quarters; no specific timeline or 30% target given.

qa_highlights.question: What is the NBFC playbook over 2-3 years?
qa_highlights.answer: Asset-light: target about 10% of lending disbursals via own NBFC in co-lending (10:90), needing about INR 60 crore equity for INR 600 crore of disbursal; FLDG stays at 5% guarantee.

risks_watch: UPI MDR timing is still unannounced (originally 15 October, now after Diwali); FY28 upside depends on implementation and final construct.
Competitive intensity expected to rise with MDR; peers may offer free Soundbox devices.
Consumer UPI GMV was soft QoQ; management asked for patience until Q3 numbers.
Fixed costs about 40% of total income; employee costs rising and linked to new business build-out.
RBI approval for the NBFC CoR is pending.
EPS figure in board results (INR 0.75) appeared inconsistent with PAT growth; management said a typo is possible and a correction would be published the next morning.
544305|2026-09.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on profitability and merchant growth, but cautious and somewhat defensive on the soft QoQ consumer UPI GMV, which management attributed to seasonality and a deliberate strategy shift. Management repeatedly declined to quantify MDR economics before final implementation.
key_quotes: This is the fourth consecutive profitable quarter for the company. We have also posted our highest-ever PAT and EBITDA in this quarter.
So we have made a little bit of shift and change in our strategy here. And any time you make certain changes in strategy, there is a short time period when the numbers don't look good.

So in totality, locking in the merchant with a device subscription, generating card-related MDR, wallet-related MDR, RuPay credit card MDR, and then the highly anticipated potential UPI MDR - I think these are all going to be amazing tailwinds for our sector.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: EBITDA margin hit 7.5% (+977 bps YoY, +204 bps QoQ) and fixed costs at about 40% of total income are expected to decline; UPI MDR could add INR 20-25 crore to EBITDA/PAT in FY28, but MDR timing is unannounced.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Own NBFC slump sale completed in August and all RBI conditions met, but operations start only after RBI grants the Certificate of Registration, which is still pending; lending disbursals of INR 1,083 crore in Q2 run through partners, not owned capacity.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: GMV grew 34-35% YoY in both payments and lending, merchant GMV +76% YoY with +18% QoQ, and management expects better Q3 numbers on festive spend and strong double-digit lending disbursal growth.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Management's only capital item is about INR 60 crore of equity for the NBFC, already planned; no utilisation figure is disclosed and no new plant, line or large capex is discussed.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: FY28 PAT target raised to about INR 100 crore from INR 75-80 crore, but only if UPI MDR is implemented; without MDR the earlier range stands and FY27 target is INR 40 crore.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Consumer UPI GMV fell QoQ in Q2 on seasonality and a shift to higher-ticket users, and industry UPI value grew only about 1% QoQ versus roughly 4% in the prior two quarters; MDR delay would remove the FY28 upside.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: NBFC launch (co-lending 10:90, target about 10% of disbursals or INR 600 crore of INR 6,000 crore) is pending RBI CoR; no other product launch was named.

rows.label: UPI MDR implementation
rows.why: MDR at 40 bps gross on transactions above INR 2,000 could add at least INR 100 crore of payments revenue in FY28 and INR 20-25 crore to EBITDA/PAT, but the date was originally 15 October and is still unannounced.

rows.label: RBI Certificate of Registration for NBFC
rows.why: Slump sale completed in August and all RBI conditions met, so only final CoR approval is pending before the NBFC can start operating.

rows.label: Lending partner renegotiation
rows.why: Renegotiated partner contracts have already lowered lending-related costs as a share of revenue, and credit performance is improving QoQ.

tone.note: Management was confident on profitability, merchant growth and the FY28 PAT target, but cautious and somewhat defensive on soft QoQ consumer UPI GMV and declined to quantify MDR economics before final implementation; analysts pushed on the take-rate, lending ratios and fixed-cost trajectory.

544306|2026-06.headline: Sai Life Sciences Q1 FY27 revenue rose 12% YoY to INR553 crore, with CRO up 26% and CDMO up 6%; management guides to a stronger H2.
544306|2026-06.overview: Q1 FY27 revenue was INR553 crore against INR496 crore a year earlier, up about 12% YoY. CRO (about 40% of revenue) grew about 26% YoY, while CDMO (about 60%) grew about 6%. Management said the quarter was in line with expectations and reiterated a stronger H2 as new capacity comes online, with the Discovery facility already commissioned and sold out and Bidar production block 1 due in H2/Q3. Management reaffirmed the mid-term revenue growth guidance of 15-20% and EBITDA margin of 28-30%, and FY27 capex of INR1,100-1,300 crore.

financial_highlights.change: about +12% YoY vs INR496 crore in Q1 FY26

segments.name: CRO / Discovery
segments.commentary: Revenue up about 26% YoY. About 65% of customers now use integrated discovery services, mainly biotech; a pilot with a large pharma converted to a long-term high-volume discovery chemistry partnership. Discovery capacity came on stream in Q1 and is already sold out.

segments.name: CDMO / CMC
segments.commentary: Revenue up about 6% YoY, described as lumpy. Portfolio is 33 active commercial molecules and 14 late-phase molecules. Three of the four commercial contracts expected this year were added in Q1; management said three are commercial supplies, primary supplier in about two of three (anecdotal).

guidance_outlook: Mid-term (3-5 year) revenue growth guidance of 15-20% reiterated; management said guidance should be viewed over a longer horizon, not quarterly.
EBITDA margin range of 28-30% reiterated.
H2 FY27 expected to be stronger than H1, with capacity coming on stream by end-Q2 or early Q3; management referenced a 40/60 historical H1/H2 split, with FY26 at about 48/52.
FY27 capex guidance INR1,100-1,300 crore unchanged; no FY28 capex guidance yet.
Target of about 1,150 KL capacity by FY27 reconfirmed.
Expects to convert at least two large pharma customers to integrated models in FY27.
Formulation (oral solids up to Phase 2) expected to be operational in about six months, within the current fiscal year.
capex_capacity: Discovery capacity came on stream in Q1 FY27 and is sold out, ahead of the one-to-1.5-year fill timeline management had assumed.
Bidar: two production blocks of 225 KL each (450 KL total); first block due for completion and operation in H2/Q3 FY27, on track.
First dedicated peptide development lab coming online shortly for a top-tier pharma company; GMP pilot-scale peptide facility coming online soon for clinical supply.
Commercial peptide manufacturing at a new greenfield site near Hyderabad expected to be operational in 2028; groundbreaking planned. Peptide spend to end-2028 likely below INR300 crore.
XDC Center of Excellence close to opening; ADC pilot-scale space under build.
demand_pricing: Management said Indian outsourcing demand is strengthened by geopolitical concerns and IP worries, with customers using India for diversification.

FTE (dedicated team) model: one top-tier pharma FTE relationship expanded from small scale to a sizable dedicated contract running end-to-end from discovery to commercial; another large pharma process development FTE deal expected to close by end-Q2, with work from Q3.

Pipeline sourced via three routes: biotech molecules acquired by pharma partners, molecules transferred from acquirers, and FTE-led progression. Five of six late-phase molecules added in 15 months came via large pharma FTE relationships.
Phase 3 pipeline: one customer approved in FY26, two more with regulatory milestones in FY27, one expected Q2 FY28.
Modalities: about 4-5% of revenue from new modalities, all in development and discovery, none in commercial. Peptide work is mainly early-stage discovery.
Sai works with 19 of the top 25 pharma companies. Five FDA-approved molecules in calendar 2025 involved Sai in discovery, development or commercial manufacturing.

qa_highlights.question: Has the shift to integrated CRDMO and big pharma FTE engagements accelerated this calendar year?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is still early, with relationships growing from one service at a time; FTE model started about 15 months ago and acceleration is seen mainly in scale and scope.

qa_highlights.question: Is the H2-weighted FY27 guidance due to capacity, given the historical split?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes. Management said FY26 was about 48/52 H1/H2 versus a historical 40/60, and capacity additions are behind the stronger H2 call.

qa_highlights.question: What is the capex threshold and what would cause a slowdown?
qa_highlights.answer: Internal hurdle rates are set above the company's ROCE/ROE targets. Capacity-addition capex can be slowed if demand slows; capability-building capex is harder to defer absent severe circumstances.

qa_highlights.question: Why guide 15-20% when the pipeline is large and recent quarters slowed?
qa_highlights.answer: Guidance is framed over 3-5 years given lumpiness; management said it is not constraining growth and FY26 grew close to 30%, with quarterly revenue driven by delivery timing.

qa_highlights.question: Is the AI initiative the same as the high-throughput experimentation platform?
qa_highlights.answer: No. HTE generates more data points per experiment; the AI initiative targets non-value-added chemist and operator work, with an update expected before year-end.

qa_highlights.question: What is the commercial profile of the four new commercial contracts?
qa_highlights.answer: Three of four are commercial supplies, described as decently sized by value; one is a lower-volume product. Primary supplier in about two of three, anecdotally.

risks_watch: CDMO growth of about 6% YoY and quarterly lumpiness; H2 recovery depends on Bidar block 1 and formulation start-up timelines.
Capex of INR1,100-1,300 crore is heavy; FY28 capex guidance not yet given.
Formulation entry (oral solids to Phase 2, China+1 driven) is new; management says it is not yet commercial and profitability was questioned.
Management did not disclose revenue at the individual molecule or customer level, and declined to discuss mAb strategy or fermentation capex.
Commercial peptide capacity not due until 2028.
544306|2026-06.management_tone: Confident on demand and the FTE model, with a long-term framing; cautious and evasive on quarterly guidance, customer-level revenue, and capex phasing beyond FY27. Management said the quarter was in line with expectations.
key_quotes: We remain confident in our ability to sustain our longer-term revenue growth guidance of 15% to 20%, and the EBITDA range of 28% to 30%.
Generally, we don't quantify what we're doing with each customer.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Discovery capacity commissioned in Q1 FY27 and sold out; Bidar block 1 (225 KL of 450 KL) due H2/Q3 FY27 and ~1,150 KL target reconfirmed for FY27.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Management guides H2 stronger than H1 as capacity comes online, against a FY26 H1/H2 split of 48/52 vs historical 40/60; Q1 revenue up 12% YoY (CRO +26%, CDMO +6%).

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: FY27 capex of INR1,100-1,300 crore is heavy and FY28 capex guidance not yet given; the Hyderabad peptide greenfield site (operational 2028) has a groundbreaking planned, with peptide spend to end-2028 below INR300 crore.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management reiterated 15-20% mid-term revenue growth and 28-30% EBITDA margin without raising them, and framed guidance over 3-5 years rather than quarterly; Q1 CDMO growth only 6%.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: CDMO grew only about 6% YoY and is lumpy; H2 recovery depends on Bidar block 1 and formulation start-up timelines, and formulation is not yet commercial.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Formulation (oral solids up to Phase 2) expected operational in about six months, within FY27; XDC Centre of Excellence close to opening and a dedicated peptide development lab coming online shortly.

rows.label: Integrated CRDMO conversions of large pharma
rows.why: Management expects to convert at least two large pharma customers to integrated models in FY27; one FTE deal expected to close by end-Q2 with work from Q3, and ~65% of customers now use integrated discovery services.

rows.label: Large pharma process development FTE deal
rows.when: end-Q2 FY27 close, work from Q3 FY27
rows.why: Another large pharma process development FTE deal is expected to close by end-Q2, and three of four commercial contracts were added in Q1 (three commercial supplies, primary supplier in about two of three, anecdotal).

rows.label: Phase 3 regulatory milestones
rows.when: FY27, one more in Q2 FY28
rows.why: One Phase 3 customer approved in FY26, two more with regulatory milestones in FY27, and one expected Q2 FY28, supporting future CDMO commercial volumes.

tone.note: Management was confident on the FTE model, Discovery sold out and H2 capacity ramp, but cautious on quarterly CDMO lumpiness, customer-level revenue and capex phasing beyond FY27; analysts pushed on why 15-20% guidance holds given slowing recent quarters and the 6% CDMO growth.

544306|2026-09.headline: Sai Life Sciences Q1 FY26 revenue rose 77% YoY to Rs 496 crore, with EBITDA up 305% to Rs 125 crore and margin at 25%.
544306|2026-09.overview: Revenue grew 77% YoY to Rs 496 crore, led by CDMO at Rs 314 crore (+113%) and CRO at Rs 182 crore (+38%). EBITDA rose 305% to Rs 125 crore, with margin at 25%, and PAT turned positive at Rs 60 crore versus a loss of Rs 13 crore a year earlier. Management said CDMO is lumpy, reiterated that H2 has historically been stronger than H1, and stated there were no one-off or launch-stocking items in Q1. Capex of Rs 134 crore was spent in the quarter, with about Rs 700 crore planned for the current year.

financial_highlights.change: Management cited 14% YoY improvement in EBITDA; margin expansion stated as significant
vs loss of Rs 13 crore in Q1 FY25

segments.name: CDMO
segments.commentary: Revenue Rs 314 crore, up 113% YoY, driven by certain commercial products and early-phase R&D revenue from pharma companies. Management said the business is lumpy and better judged over longer periods.

segments.name: CRO
segments.commentary: Revenue Rs 182 crore, up 38% YoY, driven by Integrated Discovery programs. Customer mix in CRO was about 38% big pharma and 62% biotech.

guidance_outlook: Management is not giving specific guidance for FY27 but expects H2 to be stronger than H1, as seen in prior years.
Medium-term: 3-5 year average growth target of 15% for the business; no separate CRO vs CDMO growth numbers given.
Long-term EBITDA margin target of 28-30% as revenue scales; Q1 margin of 25% described as a step toward it.
CRO/CDMO revenue mix broadly guided at two-thirds CDMO to one-third CRO, with quarterly deviations possible.
Steady-state CRO margin expected to be a few bps above CDMO margin, per CFO; no split disclosed.
Management said interest cost decline discussed earlier has largely occurred and is reflected in Q1.
capex_capacity: Manufacturing capacity: about 600 KL at end FY25; two new production blocks totalling about 450-550 KL. First block by Q3 FY27, second towards end FY27; manufacturing capacity to rise about 80-90%.
About 91-100 KL brought online at end of Q1 FY26.
Process R&D capacity to nearly double; new Process R&D block started, adding clinical-scale peptide and early-phase formulation capabilities.
About 30% extra Discovery space to be added by fiscal year end; new biology facility launched at Hyderabad campus.
Capex of about Rs 700 crore planned for FY27; further capex expected next year but no figure given.
demand_pricing: Management said RFP flow is healthy, including for mid-stage and late-stage assets.
An existing dedicated CRO client expanded its business by about 30%, effective about a month and a half before the call, expected to flow through from Q2.
Biotech funding is returning but mainly for later-stage CDMO assets; discovery contracts are smaller (20-30 FTE vs 100-150 FTE previously).
Top 10 customers were about 40% of revenue on a full-year basis; company does not disclose quarterly concentration.
Onboarded several new large pharma customers and deepened existing relationships; no specific strategy to favour big pharma over biotech.
Management said India has not yet caught up with China in scale or technology, but China+1 diversification is real, partly due to IP concerns in China.
Management expects R&D to remain in Asia and tariff/reshoring effects on supply geography to be short-term bumps; large pharma does not intend to make advanced intermediates in-house.

qa_highlights.question: Will H2 be stronger than H1 this year, and is there any lumpiness in Q1?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said H2 stronger is a general trend and expected to continue, but no specific FY27 guidance; no one-offs in Q1.

qa_highlights.question: Is manufacturing capacity doubling by FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Process R&D capacity doubling; manufacturing up about 80-90% (from about 600 KL base, with 450-550 KL being added).

qa_highlights.question: Phase III pipeline count and commercialisation?
qa_highlights.answer: Phase III pipeline is 10 molecules after net movement; a couple moved to commercial and a couple dropped out. Two Phase III molecules reported positive readouts; one small molecule recently approved.

qa_highlights.question: Capacity utilisation and capacity timing?
qa_highlights.answer: Utilisation about 77% last quarter; 70-75% considered fully utilised depending on project mix. First new block by Q3 FY27, second towards end FY27; external agencies used in the interim.

qa_highlights.question: Is the Rs 700 crore capex for FY27 only?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes, Rs 700 crore is for this year, covering manufacturing, Discovery, process R&D and peptide capabilities; next year will also have capex but no number given.

qa_highlights.question: Will the new capacity cause a shift in work, given US reshoring?
qa_highlights.answer: Management agreed that US capacity additions mainly involve late-stage and final formulation work; large pharma is not planning to do intermediates in-house, so impact on Indian CDMO work is not seen so far.

qa_highlights.question: Growth expectation for the CRO business?
qa_highlights.answer: No separate CRO growth number; committed to 15% average growth over 3-5 years for the business overall. CRO steady-state margin expected to be a few bps above CDMO.

risks_watch: CDMO revenue lumpiness; Q1 CDMO revenue of Rs 314 crore may not be a sustainable base.
Capacity gap until the first new block arrives by Q3 FY27, relying on internal capacity and external agencies.
Phase III pipeline fell in count with two dropouts due to clinical trial failure; further attrition could affect future CDMO revenue.
Client concentration: top 10 customers about 40% of revenue; disclosed annually only.
Geopolitical and US tariff uncertainty on pharma supply geography; management called the impact early and uncertain.
Execution of about Rs 700 crore capex and ramp-up of new blocks, with utilisation targets of 70-80%.
Management did not quantify revenue from newly commercial products, and did not disclose the scientist headcount across CDMO and CRO.
544306|2026-09.management_tone: Confident and bullish on demand and capacity, with clear caution on CDMO lumpiness and on giving forward numbers. Management avoided quantifying new-product contribution, client-level detail and CRO vs CDMO splits, and said macro/tariff effects are too early to call.
key_quotes: That's just an honest fact, I think.
We definitely have a lot more visibility than when we built in the past, because the past investments also were kind of changing our technology platforms.
I think we are not presenting a separate growth number for CRO versus the CDMO.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Q1 EBITDA margin at 25% (up from about 14% a year earlier) with a long-term 28-30% target as revenue scales; interest cost decline already reflected in Q1.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: First new production block (part of 450-550 KL, ~80-90% manufacturing capacity rise) due by Q3 FY27 and under construction; ~30% extra Discovery space by fiscal year end, with 91-100 KL already online in Q1 FY26.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Management expects H2 stronger than H1 as in prior years, a 3-5 year 15% average growth target, and a 30% expansion from an existing CRO client flowing through from Q2; utilisation at 77% with new blocks needed.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Utilisation at about 77% (70-75% treated as fully utilised) and Rs 700 crore FY27 capex already planned; further capex next year also flagged without a figure.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: No specific FY27 guidance given; management only gave a 15% 3-5 year average growth commitment, and CDMO lumpiness was flagged as a caution against extrapolating Q1's Rs 314 crore CDMO revenue.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: CDMO revenue (up 113% to Rs 314 crore) is lumpy and may not be a sustainable base; the capacity gap runs until the first block arrives in Q3 FY27, and two Phase III dropouts plus US tariff uncertainty add risk.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Phase III pipeline of 10 molecules with two positive readouts and one small molecule recently approved, but management did not quantify revenue from newly commercial products.

rows.label: CRO client expansion of about 30%
rows.why: An existing dedicated CRO client expanded its business by about 30%, effective about six weeks before the call and expected to flow through from Q2.

rows.label: Interest cost decline already in Q1
rows.why: Management said the interest cost decline has largely occurred and is reflected in Q1, supporting PAT of Rs 60 crore against a loss of Rs 13 crore a year earlier.

rows.label: Long-term margin target of 28-30%
rows.why: Management says the business can scale to 28-30% EBITDA margin as revenue grows, but gave no timeline and Q1 margin is 25%.

tone.note: Management was confident on demand, the capacity build and the 15% 3-5 year growth target, but cautious on CDMO lumpiness and gave no FY27 numbers; the Q&A pushed on capacity timing, utilisation, Phase III attrition and US reshoring effects.

544307|2026-03.headline: Vishal Mega Mart Q4 FY26 revenue rose 22.2% to INR 3,114 crore with same-store sales growth of 13.2%, while management flagged input inflation from May.
544307|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue from operations was INR 3,114 crore (+22.2% YoY), with same-store sales growth (SSSG) accelerating to 13.2% from 11% for FY26. Adjusted EBITDA margin widened to 8.8% from 8.2% and PAT rose 45.9% to INR 168 crore. Management attributed the strength to a consumption uptick after income tax and GST cuts, plus heavier promotions ahead of the spring/summer season. Management said input inflation, mainly petroleum-linked materials and fabric, began in late April and May, and it committed to keep private-brand discounts to third-party brands at least at current levels (about 40% on apparel).

segments.name: Apparel (fast fashion, biggest category)
segments.commentary: Q4 SSSG by price point: entry 11.1%, mid-price 13.6%, fashionable (top 2-3 price points) 14.7%. Management said fashion was the fastest-growing segment in Q4 and FY26.

segments.name: Private brands
segments.commentary: 74.1% of FY26 revenue; two brands above INR 1,000 crore and six more above INR 500 crore revenue.

segments.name: Quick commerce
segments.commentary: Expanded to 745 stores across 505 cities; registered users reached 1.3 crore.

segments.name: Small format stores
segments.commentary: 13 stores in total, 3 opened in Q4 FY26; management said store EBITDA and revenue per sq ft match large-format stores.

guidance_outlook: No numerical FY27 guidance given; management said it is difficult to model the West Asia situation and fuel price impact.
Private-brand discount to market leaders on apparel (about 40%) to remain at least the same, with a possible wider gap.
Store expansion will not slow; management said it aims to open more stores where practical.
Input inflation (petroleum-linked plastics, polyester, detergent inputs) is starting to flow through; full impact expected in the balance of May and June.
Fabric prices rising about 10-11%, per management's current range for suppliers.
Working capital cycle expected to stay at FY26 levels, per the CFO.
capex_capacity: Store count 795 at March 2026 after 105 openings in FY26 (25 in Q4); presence in 535 cities after adding 77 cities in FY26.
47 of the 105 FY26 openings were in South India (Kerala, Andhra Pradesh, Karnataka); 5 in Gujarat and 3 in Maharashtra.
Trading area 1.34 crore sq ft at March 2026.
Karnataka store areas reduced in many stores; sales per sq ft has risen and is now in line with the national average, per CFO.
Lease escalation about 15% every three years (about 5% a year), per CFO.
demand_pricing: Management attributed Q4 SSSG acceleration to a consumption uptick after income tax and GST rate cuts, plus extra investment in growth and promotions.
FY26 SSSG of 11% split: 7 points from new customers and transactions, 2 points from more items per customer, 2 points from higher price points.

Pricing is set by price point: no uniform price increases; opening and low price points are protected, higher fashion price points get more room, and management aims for price increases to be volume-neutral.
Suppliers facing gas and labour shortages earlier in the period; management said vendor supply is improving but labour has not fully returned.
Competition: management believes it is gaining share, citing 7 of the 11 SSSG points coming from new customers; it did not name V2 or V-Mart directly.
Management expects down-trading benefits if demand weakens, given private brands are 30-50% cheaper than third-party brands in food and grocery.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the Q4 SSSG acceleration, and was there pre-buying?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited a general consumption uptick after income tax and GST cuts, plus higher growth investment in the quarter. It did not frame it as pre-buying.

qa_highlights.question: How will private-label pricing respond to rising leader-brand prices?
qa_highlights.answer: Management committed to keep the discount to leader brands at least at 40% for apparel, and to try to widen it if possible.

qa_highlights.question: How did the company handle the cotton inflation of 2021-22?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it took a margin hit then, absorbed much of the increase, and used cost initiatives such as removing poly bags, using gunny bags, shipping shoes without outer cartons, and CAD cutting to reduce waste.

qa_highlights.question: Are price increases neutral, incremental or negative to apparel sales?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it aims for neutral, since high-fashion price points show lower elasticity, and it avoids raising opening price points.

qa_highlights.question: What is the dividend policy given strong free cash flow?
qa_highlights.answer: Management deferred to the Board and gave no dividend commitment.

qa_highlights.question: Are the new small-format and newer-state stores performing?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Kerala is above average, Gujarat and Maharashtra (6 stores each) are in line with the network, and small-format stores match large-format stores on sales per sq ft and store EBITDA.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Q4 gross margin compress, and why did working capital improve?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it cleared old spring/summer stock ahead of the April-June season and increased promotions to capture a consumption uptick. The CFO said working capital days are about the same as last year and that is the intended operating level.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for rent and operating leverage?
qa_highlights.answer: The CFO said rent rises about 5% a year under lease terms, so double-digit SSSG should keep producing operating leverage. He said Q4 rent looked low because of lease renewals in Q4 FY25.

risks_watch: Input cost inflation (petroleum derivatives, plastics, polyester, fabric at 10-11%) reaching shelf prices from May-June, and its effect on SSSG and gross margin.
Q4 gross margin compression linked to promotions; whether promotional intensity stays high into the April-June season.
Geopolitical and crude-price shocks, currency depreciation and possible weak rural demand from a poor monsoon.
Vendor labour and gas availability constraints, which the company says are easing.
Rising competition in apparel from e-commerce and value-fashion players moving into Tier 2 and Tier 3 cities.
Dividend policy remains undecided despite strong cash generation.
544307|2026-03.management_tone: Confident on the quarter and on private-brand resilience, but cautious on the outlook: management repeatedly declined to model the West Asia and fuel-price impact and said the coming months could be challenging. It was evasive on dividend policy, deferring to the Board.
key_quotes: So, it is clearly correlated with crude pricing in that sense.
We will not slow down our expansion at all because we are very excited about the long-term consumption story in this country.
So, our pricing is totally consumer -led.
The coming months and quarters could be challenging. I don't know.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Q4 adjusted EBITDA margin rose to 8.8% from 8.2%, but gross margin compressed on promotions and input inflation of 10-11% in fabric is flowing through from May, while private-brand discounts are held at about 40%; operating leverage from double-digit SSSG (rent up ~5% a year) is the offset.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Management said store expansion will not slow ('We will not slow down our expansion at all') after 105 openings in FY26 (25 in Q4) taking the network to 795 stores; no store count target or specific timeline was given.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: SSSG accelerated to 13.2% in Q4 from 11% for FY26 (7 points from new customers and transactions), and 25 store openings in Q4 add footprint, though management flagged a possible slowdown if rural demand weakens.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: No capex guidance or board-approved capex plan was discussed; store roll-out is funded through the existing lease-led model, and no utilisation figure was disclosed.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: No numerical FY27 guidance was issued, and management's tone on the outlook was cautious, so an upgrade is not signalled.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Management said the coming months could be challenging and declined to model West Asia and fuel-price impact; fabric prices are rising 10-11% and input inflation hits shelf from May-June, though no numerical FY27 guidance was given to cut.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: No new product, brand or category launch was discussed; fashion growth was described only as fastest-growing within existing categories.

rows.label: Volume-neutral price increases
rows.why: Management aims for price increases to be volume-neutral, with higher fashion price points getting more room, while fabric is rising 10-11% and opening price points are protected.

rows.why: 13 small-format stores (3 opened in Q4) match large formats on sales per sq ft and store EBITDA, with Kerala above average and Gujarat and Maharashtra (6 stores each) in line with the network.

544307|2026-06.headline: Vishal Mega Mart Q1 FY27 revenue rose 18.7% to INR 3,727 crore on 10% same-store sales growth; operating EBITDA margin 10.4%.
544307|2026-06.overview: Revenue from operations reached INR 3,727 crore, up 18.7% YoY, driven by 10% same-store sales growth. Operating EBITDA was INR 387 crore (up 19.3%, margin 10.4% vs 10.3%) and PAT was INR 259 crore (up 25.6%, margin 6.9% vs 6.6%). Gross margin improved to 28.7% from 28.4%, mainly from lower promotional spend rather than price hikes. The company added 27 stores to reach 819 across 559 cities, with management flagging elevated inflation as a demand headwind expected to ease in later quarters.

segments.name: Store network
segments.commentary: 819 stores in 559 cities at June 2026 end after 27 openings in the quarter, including 10 in South India; total trading area 13.8 million sq ft.

segments.name: Small format
segments.commentary: 3 small stores opened in the quarter (16 in total cited); currently run only in UP and Haryana, with a stated opportunity of about 3,000 small-format stores nationally.

segments.name: Private brands
segments.commentary: Contributed 75.2% of revenue; 100% of apparel, about 75% of general merchandise, about 60% by volume of FMCG, and about 50% of kitchen appliances (Tandem brand).

segments.name: Quick commerce
segments.commentary: 767 stores across 520 cities and over 1.4 crore registered consumers; contributes 2-9% of store revenue, at least 5% in most locations; average bill about INR 800; 20% of customers are new to Vishal.

guidance_outlook: Management expects inflation-driven demand impact to taper in subsequent quarters.
Small-format stores to accelerate; current guidance cited as 80 to 100 small-format store additions.
RFID rollout: Delhi NCR stores live; full network rollout expected to slightly exceed one year.
No further price increases planned beyond those already taken, assuming current conditions persist.
Gross margin sustainability depends on current cost structure; management says no significant issue if circumstances hold, but declined to forecast West Asia-linked developments.
Foreign ownership to be capped at 49.99% to keep the company Indian owned and controlled; foreign holding is close to 20% today.
capex_capacity: Store additions: 27 in Q1 FY27 (819 total); small-format openings were slow at 3 in the quarter, with some large-format stores opened alongside.
New format: first pilot store said to be very close to launch, followed by one or two more pilots before a roll-out decision.
RFID: pilot in 2 stores in Delhi NCR, now extended to all Delhi NCR stores; stock counts possible in 4-5 hours, enabling weekly counts.
Minimum wage increases in Haryana, UP, Telangana, Karnataka and others lifted employee cost per sq ft about 13% YoY.
demand_pricing: Same-store sales growth of 10%: new customer acquisition up 8%, existing customer spend up 3%.

Price increases were limited to higher price points and selected categories; opening and mid price points were not raised, and price-sensitive categories such as children's clothing and staple foods were left unchanged.
Highest-priced apparel fashion grew 13.9% same-store sales growth.
Gross margin gain came mainly from lower promotional intensity, with little contribution from price hikes.
Management says no new competitors entered apparel and expansion pace from existing players did not rise sharply this quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Why is small-format expansion slow when small towns may suit it?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said small-format stores were a test phase; they now match larger formats on revenue per sq ft and ROCE, and expansion will accelerate, with UP and Haryana as the only states so far. Large-format stores are still being opened alongside.

qa_highlights.question: Why did gross margin improve despite cost pressure?
qa_highlights.answer: Gross margin rose from 28.4% to 28.7%, mainly because promotional spend was lower YoY; prices were held to protect same-store sales, with little price-hike effect.

qa_highlights.question: What is the organisational change and the foreign ownership cap?
qa_highlights.answer: Sashi Gumma replaces Manoj, who is leaving after more than 10 years, in the same role, with no change to the org structure. The 49.99% foreign cap is to stay Indian owned and controlled; it applies because subsidiary Airplaza runs multi-brand retail.

qa_highlights.question: What is quick commerce's contribution and profile?
qa_highlights.answer: Quick commerce contributes 2-9% of store revenue, with most locations at 5% or more; average bill is about INR 800, slightly above offline, and 20% of quick commerce customers are new to Vishal.

qa_highlights.question: Is the rise in employee cost per sq ft structural?
qa_highlights.answer: Amit Gupta said the increase came from significant minimum wage hikes across several states, which is a structural change; management will try to optimise but cannot fully offset it.

qa_highlights.question: What is closing inventory and status of the new format?
qa_highlights.answer: Closing inventory was INR 1,900 crore. The new format is near its first pilot store launch, with one or two more pilots planned before a roll-out decision.

risks_watch: Elevated inflation weighing on demand; management expects easing but gave no firm timeline.
Gross margin sustainability: the gain depends on lower promotions and holding prices; West Asia developments are an open risk.
Structural rise in employee costs from minimum wage increases across several states.
Competitive pressure in apparel from value retailers; management says the competitor set is unchanged, but pace is a watch item.
Leadership change: COO Manoj departs and Sashi Gumma replaces him; further org changes not discussed.
Small-format and RFID roll-outs are gradual; timing and benefits remain to be proven at scale.

544307|2026-09.headline: Vishal Mega Mart Q2 FY27 revenue rose 14% to INR3,399 crore, but same-store sales growth slowed to 5.4% as festivals shifted into Q3.
544307|2026-09.overview: Revenue from operations grew 14% YoY to INR3,399 crore in Q2 FY27, with same-store sales growth (SSSG) of 5.4%, which management says would have been about 9% without the festival shift. Operating EBITDA rose 3.7% to INR262 crore, but margin fell to 7.7% from 8.5% on operating deleverage from low fixed-cost absorption. Adjusted PAT grew 6.4% to INR172 crore, with margin at 5.1% versus 5.4%. Store network reached 844 with 26 gross additions in the quarter, and management said it sees no demand moderation despite inflation.

financial_highlights.change: About 9% adjusted for festival shift (3-4pt impact)

financial_highlights.metric: Adjusted PAT (Q2 FY27, after ESOP charges)

financial_highlights.change: About 9.5% adjusted for festival shift (1.5-2pt impact)
